(3) UNRESOLVED PINS: no change required — tools/connectors/evidence.ts fetchPinnedWork already sets pin_unresolved:true on the fallback record when a pinned DOI does not resolve on OpenAlex (D-033), so a dead pin is a visible finding in the corpus output, not a run failure; pin_unresolved stays an output-only flag on EvidenceRecord and is deliberately NOT added to the input schema. (4) KEYED RUNS: S2_API_KEY is already set as a GitHub Actions repo secret and wired into harvest.yml / connectors.yml (harvest runs in Actions, not the app), so S2-backed runs come back keyed rather than degrading to the keyless 429 partial path (D-018). No harvest is triggered here — prep only; runs are dispatched from /ops.

decisions.title: Dossier schema widened to admit the owner-approved flag_completes_core boolean
decisions.body: Admitting the Batch 3 owner-approved dossiers surfaced one field the schema did not yet carry: DOS-ID-12 sets flag_completes_core:true to mark the dossier that completes the 12-mechanism core admission. As with D-035/D-042, the owner content is authoritative, so the schema is extended via this decision rather than the science being edited (.cursorrules #8 forbids touching owner content; #4 forbids weakening the schema for CONVENIENCE — this is fidelity to approved content through the sanctioned decision path #7, not a workaround). dossiers/dossier.schema.json is additionalProperties:false, so a field it lacks fails validation. Change: dossiers/dossier.schema.json gains an OPTIONAL flag_completes_core (boolean), not added to required — the eleven other dossiers omit it and stay valid; lib/types.ts Dossier mirrors it as optional flag_completes_core?: boolean (rule 13). This is the exact additive-optional-field pattern of D-042 (flag_lowest_admitted); the flag is data-only and, like flag_lowest_admitted, is not rendered by the /dossiers page. No HARD RULE, total-equals-sum check, dissent gate, or any other constraint changes. npm run validate and npm run build are green.

decisions.title: Core complete — all 12 L1 mechanisms admitted to incubating via dossiers; batch 3 (CG-05, SP-08, ST-09, RE-10, ID-12)
decisions.body: The third and final batch of owner-approved full L1 records is admitted, completing the core: the registry moves from 7 to 12 full records (LA-01, EN-03, VR-02, ZE-07, HA-04, FR-11, SC-06, CG-05, SP-08, ST-09, RE-10, ID-12 = 12/12) and the dossier count from 7 to 12, and the _seed folder now holds zero candidate stubs — every seed mechanism has passed the admission gate. Each of CG-05 (Curiosity gap, parent S2, grade B+, dossier total 12), SP-08 (Social proof, parent S4, grade A-, total 14), ST-09 (Status & comparison, parent S4, grade A-, total 13), RE-10 (Reciprocity, parent S4, grade B+, total 14), and ID-12 (Identity & consistency, parent S5, grade B+, total 12) replaces its _seed candidate stub (the five stubs are removed so no duplicate id enters the roster) and points dossier_ref at the dossiers/{id}.json admitted alongside it. All five records carry evidence_terms and pinned_evidence, so the D-038 corpus-reproducibility HARD RULE is satisfied, and each validates against the full mechanism.schema.json as-is — the grades (B+/A-) and relation types (all 'adjacent') were already in the vocabulary from D-035, so no mechanism-schema change was needed this batch. All five dossiers validate against dossier.schema.json with total = axis sum and rest on evidence corpora with non-empty dissent categories harvested in the Batch 3 run (D-019: CG-05 41, SP-08 59, ST-09 40, RE-10 29, ID-12 34). ID-12's dossier carries flag_completes_core:true (schema-admitted in D-045) marking it as the record that closes the core. Lifecycle status is incubating for all twelve, matching each dossier verdict; promotion to CORE remains blocked on core_condition (a recorded measured effect from the telemetry loop or public corpora), never hardcoded — the honest status is 12/12 incubating, 0 core. Cards regenerated with npm run cards (12 cards); npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Product segments are first-class evolving system data — 15 seed segments classify output products, not Ventora
decisions.body: The product-segment axis becomes first-class data the whole layer references, living in /segments/segments.yaml. This is a small constitution amendment: rule 1 (source of truth) now lists /segments/segments.yaml among the git-only data locations, following the D-011/D-023 amendment pattern; it is edited in git only, no UI write surface. The file is { version, segments[] } where each segment is { id, group, definition, status, provenance }. group is one of business-model | form | audience | usage-rhythm; status is active | retired (a retired segment is kept for history, never deleted); provenance is seed-YYYY-MM for the owner seed set, or analyzer | owner for segments added later. CRITICAL framing (rule 8): these segments classify the OUTPUT products Ventora builds (Ventora builds ANY product type), NOT Ventora itself. The 15 owner-provided seed segments carry provenance seed-2026-07 — by business model: transactional-ecommerce, subscription, freemium, marketplace, lead-gen-service, one-time-digital; by form: web-saas, mobile-app, content-media, local-offline-bridge; by audience: b2b, b2c-mass, creator-prosumer; by usage rhythm: daily-habit, occasional-high-consideration. The segment axis EVOLVES: the analyzer or the owner will add new segments later carrying provenance analyzer/owner, so the validator never hardcodes the count. Validation (tools/validate.ts, run in CI on every push): the file must parse as YAML (a yaml devDependency is added — needed now for this validation, not speculative infrastructure), every entry must match an Ajv schema whose property keys are pinned to the reader contract lib/types.ts Segment via a satisfies constraint (same drift-guard pattern as D-020), and ids must be unique. lib/types.ts gains SegmentGroup, SegmentStatus, Segment, and SegmentsFile (rule 13). Renders nowhere yet by design — this step is DATA ONLY; no app screen reads or displays segments, and the honest empty state is simply that no UI consumes them at this step.

decisions.title: Pack map is the sole hand-authored input to pack generation; packs are otherwise computed projections
decisions.body: The pack pipeline gets its one and only judgment call: /packs/pack-map.yaml, mapping each Development-Plan element type to the mechanisms whose evidence is relevant to it. This is a small constitution amendment following the D-047 pattern: rule 1 (source of truth) now lists /packs/pack-map.yaml among the git-only data locations; it is edited in git only, no UI write surface. The framing is deliberate — mapping mechanisms to product elements is the SOLE human decision here; everything downstream (the packs themselves) is a COMPUTED projection over this map plus the registry, never hand-authored. The file is { version, elements[] } where each element is { id, applies_to, funnel_stage, mechanisms, note? }. id is a unique element-type slug; applies_to is free-text product-surface slugs; funnel_stage is one of the registry applicability vocabulary (cold_acquisition | onboarding | activation | conversion | retention | reactivation); mechanisms is the list of mechanism ids whose evidence is relevant; note is an optional owner annotation. The 11 owner-provided seed elements are entry, onboarding, first-value, core-ux, retention-return, engagement-loops, social-proof-status, paywall-conversion, retention-billing, trust-friction (guardrail-forward), aha-sharing. IMPORTANT: funnel_stage records evidence RELEVANCE, not runtime applicability — an element's stage may differ from a member mechanism's applicability (e.g. entry is cold_acquisition while SP-08/FR-11 exclude that stage at generation time), so the validator deliberately does NOT cross-check element stage against mechanism excluded_stages. Validation (tools/validate.ts, run in CI on every push): the file must parse as YAML, every element must match an Ajv schema whose property keys are pinned to the reader contract lib/types.ts PackMapElement via a satisfies constraint (same drift-guard pattern as D-020/D-047), element ids must be unique, and EVERY referenced mechanism id must resolve to a registry record (checked against rosterIds — a map pointing at a phantom mechanism would silently produce a wrong pack). lib/types.ts gains FunnelStage, PackMapElement, and PackMapFile (rule 13). Renders nowhere yet by design — this step is DATA ONLY; no app screen reads or displays the pack map. npm run validate and npm run build are green.

decisions.title: Packs generated via render-packs.ts — computed projection over the pack map + registry, never hand-authored
decisions.body: Packs are now GENERATED, following the render-cards pattern (D-002): tools/render-packs.ts (npm run packs) projects /packs/pack-map.yaml (D-048) + the registry (/registry/mechanisms/*.json, /dossiers/*.json) into one YAML datasheet per element at /packs/pack-{id}.yaml. The hand-written packs/pack-paywall-conversion.yaml is the reference format and is now REPRODUCED by the generator (packs are never hand-authored; the hand version survives in git history). The datasheet structure is pinned to that reference: header (pack, applies_to, funnel_stage, version, nature, source) + LAYER 1 mechanisms + LAYER 2 interactions + LAYER 3 context_weights + hard_boundaries + signals + wiring, with the section banners preserved. Field derivation (all deterministic, registry-only, rule 8 — no invented knowledge): LAYER 1 per member — name = record name lowercased; fact = first sentence of mechanism_summary_for_context (drops instruction-voice tails); grade + source from evidence (basis + pinned_evidence DOIs); boundary = humanized evidence.caveats, plus 'contested by {citation}' ONLY when the dossier.dissent opens with a single citation-shaped clause (carries a year, one clause, <=160 chars) — prose-fronted dissents contribute no citation, so among the seed set only LA-01 yields one; active_when = precondition predicates with '== true' stripped, joined by OR; realizations = implementation ids with the '{ID}-' prefix removed; forbidden = hard_rule ids kebab-cased. LAYER 2 interactions = dedup relations where both endpoints are pack members: enables/enabled_by -> sequence-amplifying (ordered [enabler, enabled]), hybrid_with -> reinforcing, adjacent -> noted, orthogonality_note skipped; fact = relation note; grade = weaker of the two members' grades. LAYER 3 context_weights = per distinct precondition predicate, a strong entry and a negated inactive entry. hard_boundaries = union of members' hard_rules as status-facts ('{kebab-id}: forbidden — {rule}'), plus each member's boundary_test; rule text is voice-normalized (leading Do-not/Never stripped; any rule still carrying you/your/should/prefer collapses to bare 'forbidden') so the sheet stays instruction-free per its own 'no instructions' nature. signals.measured = sorted union of members' implementation metrics; tag/learning and the whole wiring block are constants from the reference. Two self-checks run before writing each file: it must re-parse as YAML, and no emitted prose outside comments may carry you/your/should/prefer. Stale pack-*.yaml files are removed on regenerate; pack-map.yaml and README.md are never touched. KNOWN DELTAS vs the hand reference (structure matches EXACTLY except one field; content is registry-derived, not the hand-condensed prose): (1) the reference put an optional 'boundary' on LAYER 2 interactions, but there is no registry field for an interaction-level boundary, so generated interactions omit it (adding one would be invented knowledge); (2) the two reference 'suppressing' interactions ([SC-06, high-pressure-framing], [all-four-saturated]) exist in no registry relation and do not appear — if wanted they must be added to the registry as relations first; (3) realizations use implementation-id stems, applies_to/version come from the pack map (so the generated paywall header shows the map's [paywall, pricing] and version 0.1.0, not the hand file's [paywall, checkout, pricing_element]/3.0.0). lib/types.ts gains PackMechanism, PackInteraction(Type), PackContextWeight, PackSignals, PackWiring, PackDatasheet (rule 13). package.json gains the 'packs' script. Renders nowhere yet by design — DATA ONLY. npm run validate and npm run build are green.

decisions.title: Sufficiency scored per pack×segment on 5 computable criteria; general-only evidence flags a segment gap
decisions.body: The analyzer layer arrives: tools/analyzer.ts (npm run analyze) computes, for every pack-map element (D-048) × every ACTIVE segment (D-047), whether the knowledge is mature — the heart of this layer. Output is /analysis/sufficiency-matrix.json, a COMPUTED projection never hand-edited (render-cards/render-packs pattern, D-002/D-049); the ONE hand-authored input is /analysis/analyzer.config.yaml, holding everything owner-tunable: grade-letter weights (A=1, B=0.6, C=0.2; the +/- modifier collapses, A- → A), per-criterion status thresholds (default green≥0.8/amber≥0.5; dissent_completeness green=1.0/amber≥0.8 so one stripped dossier in a 3–4 mechanism pack turns the cell red, not amber), the segment → typical-funnel-stage map, segment-affinity boosts, and owner replication flags. Each cell carries {pack, segment, scores{5 criteria, each 0–1}, status red|amber|green, gaps:[criteria below green], segment_evidence}. The five computable criteria: (1) dissent_completeness — share of the pack's mechanisms whose dossier dissent is non-empty (missing dossier or blank dissent = 0), deliberately UNWEIGHTED: dissent is a knowledge-hygiene bar, and a stripped dossier fails it for every segment regardless of how relevant its mechanism is to that segment; (2) grade_sufficiency — weighted mean of grade-letter weights over the pack's mechanisms; (3) interaction_coverage — share of the pack's C(n,2) mechanism pairs connected by a registry relation in either direction (the same pairing logic render-packs projects into LAYER 2; orthogonality_note is excluded — it documents separation, not interaction); (4) context_coverage — share of the segment's typical funnel stages on which the pack holds ≥1 mechanism at grade ≥ min_context_grade (B) whose applicability lists the stage and does not exclude it; (5) freshness — 1 minus the weighted share of pack mechanisms in config replication_flags (empty today, so freshness defaults green; replication concerns currently live as prose in dossier dissent / evidence caveats, and flagging one is an explicit owner judgment, never derived from prose). Cell status = worst criterion status. SEGMENT RELEVANCE: a mechanism's fit to a segment is derived from its applicability × the segment-affinity config — weight = min(1, base × boost) where base is 1 when the mechanism's funnel_stages intersect the segment's typical stages (0.5 otherwise) and boost comes from segment_affinity (e.g. daily-habit strengthens HA-04/VR-02; occasional-high-consideration strengthens SP-08/FR-11; transactional-ecommerce strengthens SC-06/LA-01). Weights only redistribute emphasis inside a cell — they never fabricate evidence. Where no segment-specific judgment touches the pack's mechanisms, the cell scores on general evidence and carries segment_evidence: general_only — THE signal that segment-specific harvesting is needed (the Maria case: works for commerce, thin for others). IMPORTANT framing (rule 8): the config's segment_stages and segment_affinity seeds are PRODUCT JUDGMENT defaults, not scientific claims — flagged owner-reviewable in the file header. The analyzer fails loudly on config problems (an active segment missing from segment_stages, unknown stage/mechanism ids, malformed thresholds) rather than guessing. Constitution note: /analysis joins the repo as an analyzer surface — analyzer.config.yaml is hand-authored git-only data; sufficiency-matrix.json is generated output (the /cards precedent). lib/types.ts gains SufficiencyCriterion, SufficiencyScores, SufficiencyStatus, SegmentEvidence, SufficiencyThreshold, GradeLetter, AnalyzerConfig, SufficiencyCell, SufficiencyMatrix (rule 13). package.json gains the analyze script. Renders nowhere yet by design — DATA ONLY. Verified: 11 packs × 15 segments = 165 cells; one cell hand-checked against the underlying records; cells without an affinity entry carry general_only; a deliberately dissent-stripped mechanism turns its cells red on dissent_completeness. npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Gap planner ranks red/amber cells into a budget-bounded queue of targeted, segment-qualified harvests
decisions.body: The prioritization layer arrives: tools/gap-planner.ts (npm run gaps) turns the red/amber cells of analysis/sufficiency-matrix.json (D-050) into a RANKED, BUDGETED queue of targeted evidence harvests at analysis/research-queue.json — the discipline of 'research the biggest gaps in the segments that matter', not 'research everything'. The queue is a COMPUTED projection, never hand-edited (the render-cards/analyzer precedent, D-002/D-050); the ONE hand-authored input is a new gap_planner block appended to /analysis/analyzer.config.yaml (kept in the single analyzer config since it too is owner-tunable product judgment, git-only, no UI write surface). The block holds: segment_weights (segment id → importance weight, default 1.0 when omitted — PRODUCT-PRIORITY judgment, not science), segment_qualifiers (segment id → generic vocabulary tokens appended to a mechanism's own evidence terms, e.g. 'b2b enterprise', 'habit daily app'), and budget { max_tasks, estimated_calls_per_task, monthly_budget_share }. RANKING: importance = segment_weight × gap_size, where gap_size = Σ over the cell's failed criteria of (green_threshold − score) read from the same thresholds the analyzer uses — a severity measure, so a deep red cell in a high-weight segment (e.g. b2b 1.5) rises above a shallow amber. Ties break red-before-amber, then general_only-before-segment_specific (D-050's segment-gap flag), then weaker-mechanism-first. SATURATION: only cells with status red|amber are queued; a green cell is saturated and never appears — verified absent in the output. EXPANSION: the matrix is pack × segment but a harvest targets a mechanism, so each cell expands via /packs/pack-map.yaml (D-048) to its pack's registry mechanisms; a task addresses one (mechanism, segment) pair, deduped across packs (highest-importance cell wins) so an identical segment-qualified harvest is queued once. Each task = { gap_cell{pack,segment,status,gaps,segment_evidence}, mechanism, segment, importance, suggested_evidence_terms, reason }. suggested_evidence_terms are the mechanism's OWN evidence_terms (registry, D-015; fallback its name), capped at the first 3 and each appended with the segment qualifier — no invented science (rule 8), and they drop straight onto the evidence connector's terms= override (npm run connector -- evidence mechanism=... terms=...), i.e. the SAME harvest machinery, segment-qualified. reason is computed from the cell's failed criteria and their scores vs thresholds, never hardcoded. BUDGET (does NOT bypass the monthly cap system): N = min(gap_planner.budget.max_tasks, floor(remaining_monthly_calls × monthly_budget_share / estimated_calls_per_task)); remaining_monthly_calls comes from lib/ops.ts computeBudgetSnapshot (the SAME month-to-date snapshot the /ops gate and progress bar read), and estimated_calls_per_task mirrors the evidence connector's max_calls_per_run (150) so one task ≈ one run. The planner never triggers a harvest and never raises a cap — each queued task is still gated per-run by evaluateRunAgainstOps at harvest time (D-025), so per-run limits and the monthly budget remain the hard ceilings. The output carries a budget block recording month, remaining calls, the share, config vs budget max_tasks, and the applied N, plus candidate_count (red/amber mechanism × segment pairs before truncation) for transparency. The planner fails loudly (like the analyzer) on a missing matrix (points to npm run analyze), a missing gap_planner block, a malformed budget, an unknown segment in weights/qualifiers, or a segment that has gaps but no qualifier — it never harvests unqualified. lib/types.ts gains GapPlannerBudgetConfig, GapPlannerConfig, ResearchGapCell, ResearchTask, ResearchQueueBudget, ResearchQueue (rule 13). package.json gains the 'gaps' script. Renders nowhere yet by design — DATA ONLY; research-queue.json is generated output on the /analysis surface, not validated by tools/validate.ts (the sufficiency-matrix precedent). Decision policy encoded and logged by the tool: gaps prioritized by segment-weight × gap-size, budget-bounded; saturated cells excluded; addressing is targeted not exhaustive. npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Weekly maturation loop: analyze -> find gaps -> targeted harvest -> re-analyze -> regenerate packs; budget-bounded, self-limiting
decisions.body: The orchestration layer arrives: .github/workflows/maturation.yml — the weekly maturation loop, on a schedule (Mon 07:00 UTC, after the scheduled evidence run) and on workflow_dispatch (with an optional max_tasks input for small-N verification runs). The loop: analyze -> find gaps -> targeted harvest -> re-analyze -> regenerate packs; budget-bounded, self-limiting. Steps: (1) npm run analyze recomputes the full sufficiency matrix (D-050) and the pre-harvest matrix is kept as the diff baseline; (2) npm run gaps recomputes the ranked, budget-bounded research queue (D-051); (3) a new ops-gate mode, plan-queue, gates the queue's top-N tasks through the EXISTING guards — paused, health-down (D-030), per-run limits and the monthly budget via evaluateRunAgainstOps (D-025) — never re-implementing them; evaluateRunAgainstOps gains an optional pendingSpend argument so the batch's already-accepted estimates are projected cumulatively on top of month-to-date spend (pendingSpend only tightens the gate, never loosens it): accepting task k accounts for tasks 1..k-1, so the loop can NEVER exhaust the budget and raise_cap is never passed. A task that no longer fits gets action 'defer' with a logged plain-language reason — it stays in the queue and surfaces again next week (deferral is a first-class plan outcome, recorded in the job summary, not a silent drop). Cadence and registry freshness deliberately do NOT gate queue tasks: the queue is gap-driven (which knowledge is thin), not change-driven (what the owner touched) — those guards keep governing the scheduled _ops-target fleet in connectors.yml. Each due task is harvested by the SAME evidence connector with the task's segment-qualified terms= override (suggested_evidence_terms, D-051), retry-once-after-backoff and the deduplicated ops-issue contract (D-022) reused verbatim; the workflow shares the exact 'connectors-s2' concurrency group so it can never call Semantic Scholar concurrently with connectors.yml/harvest.yml (D-027). (4) The analyzer gains a scoped re-score — npm run analyze -- packs=a,b re-scores ONLY the listed packs' cells and preserves every other cell verbatim from the existing matrix (pack-map order kept; fails loudly if the grid changed) — so the loop re-analyzes exactly the cells its harvests addressed. (5) render-packs gains the same packs= filter — regenerating ONLY the packs whose cells flipped to green (stale-pack removal is skipped on a scoped run, which cannot tell stale from not-rendered). (6) Changes to analysis/, corpora/ and packs/ are committed as 'maturation: week {date} — filled {N} gaps' (a dedicated maturation: commit prefix for the loop's auto-commits, extending the D-016 conventional-commit set), and the job summary carries the week's red->green cell diff (computed by comparing the baseline and re-scored matrices), the regenerated packs, the run's spend (budget snapshot delta), and the deferred-task count. Honest expectation: a harvest alone fills corpora — cell scores move only when the owner upgrades registry grades/dossiers (rule 8), so red->green flips are expected after owner review lands, and a week with zero flips is a truthful, common outcome. Nothing here touches the Ventora app surface; the loop runs entirely in Actions on the repo's file-based data.

decisions.title: Maturation cockpit visualizes knowledge sufficiency; the growing matrix is the proof the core is alive
decisions.body: The maturation layer (D-050/D-051/D-052) finally RENDERS: /maturation is the Control Center cockpit that makes the maturing knowledge visible — matrix, gaps, weekly progress, honest, read from files. Until now analysis/*.json rendered nowhere by design; this step consumes it in the app for the first time (a narrow read extension, no new write surface). The page (app/maturation/page.tsx, a server component, no client JS) shows four things, each with a file-provenance footer and a designed empty state: (1) the sufficiency matrix as a heatmap — packs (rows, pack-map.yaml order, D-048) × active segments (columns, grouped by axis from segments.yaml, D-047), cell color = computed status via lib/status.ts CELL_STATUS_META, a hollow-ring marker for segment_evidence general_only, and a CSS-only hover tooltip carrying the 5 scores, the gaps, and the segment-evidence flag; a segment active in segments.yaml but absent from the matrix renders as the neutral 'not analyzed' state (CELL_NOT_ANALYZED_META), honest, never red; (2) this week's research queue (analysis/research-queue.json) — the budget line plus each task's mechanism × pack × segment, importance, reason, and suggested terms; (3) a maturation log (analysis/maturation-log.json) — the weekly red->green cell diff, packs regenerated, and spend; (4) a coverage summary — % green overall, per pack, per segment. HONESTY RULE (.cursorrules #2): every cell, count, and log entry is READ from analysis/*.json + segments.yaml and COMPUTED at render time in lib/maturation.ts / lib/status.ts; the 'red'|'amber'|'green' and 'general_only'|'segment_specific' literals live ONLY in lib/status.ts (CELL_STATUS_META, CELL_STATUS_ORDER, CELL_NOT_ANALYZED_META, SEGMENT_EVIDENCE_META) — app/ carries no status literal, so the grep check stays clean. A 'segments are evolving' note computes the active/retired counts and provenance breakdown from segments.yaml (never hardcoded — the axis grows and the note grows with it). The Overview ROOMS nav gains a /maturation link. PERSISTENCE: the weekly loop's story used to live only in the ephemeral GitHub Actions job summary; a new tool tools/maturation-log.ts (npm run maturation-log) records it into analysis/maturation-log.json — generated output, never hand-edited (the sufficiency-matrix / research-queue precedent, D-050/D-051), computed only from the artifacts the loop already produces (cell-diff.json, budget-before/after.json, queue-plan.json); packs_regenerated mirrors the workflow's flipped_packs (packs with a cell that flipped to green) and a zero-flip week is recorded truthfully. maturation.yml (D-052) gains one step after the summary and before the commit; the existing 'git add analysis' carries the log file into the maturation: commit. lib/types.ts gains MaturationCellChange, MaturationLogEntry, MaturationLog (rule 13); the yaml package moves from devDependencies to dependencies since the app now parses segments.yaml / pack-map.yaml at runtime (not speculative — needed now by lib/maturation.ts). maturation-log.json is generated output on the /analysis surface, not validated by tools/validate.ts (the matrix/queue precedent). Verified: the heatmap matches sufficiency-matrix.json (85 red / 70 amber / 10 green across 165 cells); changing a cell's score/status in the matrix JSON moves the cell and the coverage numbers; a segment added to segments.yaml but absent from the matrix renders neutral, not red; the empty log renders its honest empty state; every displayed number traces to a file. npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Segments evolve — owner adds now, analyzer-suggestion designed for later; new segments enter the matrix red and mature via the loop
decisions.body: The product-segment axis (segments/segments.yaml, D-047) is a SEED, NOT A FIXED SET — segments grow, and the growth feeds the same maturation loop the mechanisms use. Two paths, one available now and one designed for later. PATH A (available now): the owner adds a segment with a single git edit — one entry with provenance 'owner' (the axis stays git-only, no UI write surface, .cursorrules #1). On the next analyzer run it enters the sufficiency matrix AUTOMATICALLY as an honest ALL-RED column: tools/analyzer.ts no longer fails loudly when an active segment has no analyzer.config.yaml segment_stages entry — instead that segment is a BOOTSTRAP segment and every pack × bootstrap-segment cell scores 0 on all five criteria, status red, all criteria as gaps, segment_evidence general_only. This is the honest state (.cursorrules #2): with no stage map and zero segment-specific evidence, nothing has been demonstrated FOR the segment yet, so red is the truth — never a hardcoded status, always computed from the absence of data. A malformed segment_stages entry (present but with an unknown stage) is STILL a loud error; only a fully-absent entry means bootstrap. Because a bootstrap cell has the maximal gap_size, tools/gap-planner.ts (D-051) ranks it to the TOP of the research queue; the planner derives the segment's harvest qualifier mechanically from its own id (hyphens → spaces, e.g. 'ai-agent-tools' → 'ai agent tools') so the new segment gets targeted, segment-qualified tasks before the owner hand-tunes anything — product vocabulary from the owner's own slug, never invented science (rule 8). A CONFIGURED segment (one with a segment_stages entry) that is missing a gap_planner.segment_qualifiers entry still FAILS loudly — the fallback applies only to brand-new unconfigured segments, so a real typo is never silently swallowed. The owner graduates a segment out of bootstrap by adding segment_stages (required to score on the five criteria) and optionally segment_affinity / gap_planner qualifiers+weights to analyzer.config.yaml. PATH B (designed, NOT scheduled): tools/segment-suggest.ts (npm run segment-suggest) is the discovery analog for segments — the counterpart of the mechanism seed stubs (D-046) — and is deliberately INERT: it reads nothing, writes nothing, and is in NO workflow and on NO schedule; running it prints 'designed, not scheduled — no candidates written'. Its committed header specifies the future algorithm: read the harvested corpora (corpora/evidence titles/abstracts/terms, corpora/benchmarks industry categories, corpora/wayback domains) for recurring product-context clusters, SUBTRACT everything already covered by an active segment (id, definition vocabulary, segment_qualifiers), and propose the uncovered clusters as SegmentCandidate records appended to segments/candidates.json for OWNER APPROVAL. On approval the owner hand-adds the segment to segments.yaml with provenance 'analyzer' (a tool never edits the axis, never invents science) — after which it enters the matrix all-red via Path A. segments/candidates.json { version, generated_at, candidates[] } (each { id, group, definition_draft, evidence_note, proposed_at, status: proposed|approved|rejected }) is seeded as an empty queue and validated by tools/validate.ts: schema pinned to the reader contract lib/types.ts SegmentCandidate via a satisfies constraint (same drift-guard as D-047), unique candidate ids, and no candidate id may collide with an existing segment (a candidate proposes a NEW segment). lib/types.ts gains SegmentCandidateStatus, SegmentCandidate, SegmentCandidateQueue (rule 13). package.json gains the segment-suggest script (discoverability only). The /maturation cockpit's 'Segments are evolving' panel now shows the candidate count read from candidates.json with an honest empty state ('0 candidates — segment-suggest is designed but not scheduled') — never hardcoded (lib/maturation.ts computeSegmentCandidates). Documented in docs/connectors-runbook.md (new 'Segment evolution' section: how the owner adds a segment, the all-red bootstrap, graduating to configured, and the segment-suggest design status) and segments/README.md. Verified: adding a test segment with provenance owner and no config entries makes npm run validate stay green, npm run analyze emit its pack cells all-red, and npm run gaps queue research tasks for it with the id-derived qualifier; removing it restores the committed matrix/queue; npm run segment-suggest writes nothing and is in no workflow. npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Gaps are typed by their filler — harvest vs structural; the loop must never dispatch a harvest against a structural gap
decisions.body: Every failed criterion in a sufficiency-matrix cell (analysis/sufficiency-matrix.json, D-050) is now LABELED by what can actually close it — the fix that stops the wheel spinning. tools/analyzer.ts emits a new typed_gaps array on every SufficiencyCell: one entry per failing criterion { criterion, value (the cell's score), threshold (the green bar it falls short of), fix_type, what_would_close_it }. fix_type is one of two fillers: HARVEST gaps close by fetching more/better evidence through the connector (grade_sufficiency; freshness); STRUCTURAL gaps close only by owner edits in git and NO harvest can touch them (interaction_coverage — registry relations between the pack's mechanisms; context_coverage — pack composition / a grade≥B mechanism covering the segment's funnel stages). dissent_completeness is STRUCTURAL: dossier dissent is owner-authored (rule 8), so no fetch fills it (it only surfaces as a gap in bootstrap all-red cells today). The general_only condition is ALSO surfaced as a harvest gap: when a non-green cell rests on general evidence only, typed_gaps carries a pseudo-criterion 'segment_evidence' entry (value 0, threshold 1, fix_type harvest) whose closer is segment-qualified evidence plus a segment_affinity entry — segment_evidence is not one of the five scored criteria but it IS harvest-closable, so it belongs in the typing. A cell's gaps can be MIXED type (a red cell is commonly grade_sufficiency=harvest + interaction_coverage/context_coverage=structural + segment_evidence=harvest). The reason the loop must never dispatch a harvest against a structural gap: fetching papers can never add a registry relation or recompose a pack, so a harvest aimed at a structural gap spins forever without moving the score. The existing gaps: SufficiencyCriterion[] field STAYS unchanged — tools/gap-planner.ts (gapSize, reasonFor, ResearchGapCell.gaps, D-051) and the /maturation cockpit tooltip (app/maturation/page.tsx, cell.gaps.includes) still read it; typed_gaps is the richer superset the maturation loop reads to route work. lib/types.ts gains GapFixType and TypedGap and SufficiencyCell.typed_gaps (rule 13); the constants FIX_TYPE and WHAT_WOULD_CLOSE_IT live in tools/analyzer.ts. A scoped re-score (npm run analyze -- packs=..., D-052) fails loudly if the existing matrix predates gap typing (any preserved cell missing typed_gaps), so a scoped run can never emit a partially-typed matrix; MATRIX_VERSION bumped 0.1.0 → 0.2.0. Verified: every red cell shows interaction_coverage/context_coverage as structural and grade_sufficiency/segment_evidence as harvest, and no gap is untyped; npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Loop routes by fix_type; structural gaps go to an authoring queue, not the API
decisions.body: The weekly maturation loop now ROUTES gaps by their fix_type (D-055) instead of harvesting every red/amber cell. Only HARVEST gaps generate connector tasks and consume budget; STRUCTURAL gaps are written to a new owner-facing analysis/authoring-queue.json and NEVER touch the API. The reason: fetching papers can never add a registry relation, recompose a pack, or author dossier dissent, so dispatching connectors against interaction_coverage / context_coverage / dissent_completeness gaps burns Semantic Scholar / OpenAlex budget for zero possible cell flips — the wheel spins forever. THE ROUTING RULE (tools/gap-planner.ts): a cell is HARVESTABLE iff it has ≥1 SCORED harvest gap (grade_sufficiency or freshness in cell.gaps, read via typed_gaps fix_type). The segment_evidence harvest flag alone does NOT make a cell harvestable — it is not a scored criterion, and if every scored gap is structural no segment-qualified evidence can flip the cell, so harvesting it is pure budget burn (this is exactly what drops the interaction-heavy red cells out of the harvest queue). A MIXED cell routes to BOTH queues: its harvest gaps become connector tasks, its structural gaps become an authoring task. HARVEST PATH: only harvestable cells expand to (mechanism, segment) candidates; importance = segment_weight × gap_size sized over the cell's HARVEST gaps ONLY (not all failed criteria), so a mixed cell ranks by what a harvest can actually fix; reason cites only the harvest gaps. Budget logic (computeBudgetSnapshot, effective_max_tasks) is untouched — it simply sees fewer candidates, so spend drops. Segments needing a harvest qualifier are now the segments of HARVESTABLE cells only, so a structural-only segment no longer fails loudly demanding a qualifier it will never use. STRUCTURAL PATH: every red/amber cell with ≥1 structural typed_gap becomes an AuthoringTask { pack, segment, status, importance = segment_weight × Σ structural (threshold − value), segment_evidence, structural_gaps[] }, sorted importance-desc (red before amber, stable by pack/segment), written to analysis/authoring-queue.json { version, generated_at, config_version, matrix_generated_at, cell_count, tasks } — a COMPUTED projection never hand-edited (the research-queue precedent, D-051), always written even when empty (honest empty state). To make the authoring queue ACTIONABLE, tools/analyzer.ts now enriches the two structural coverage gaps with owner-facing detail: interaction_coverage carries missing_interaction_pairs (the pack's unlinked member id pairs, locale-stable) and context_coverage carries uncovered_stages (the segment funnel stages with no grade≥min_context_grade mechanism) — so the owner sees exactly which relations to author / which stages to cover, per pack×segment, ranked by importance. WORKFLOW (.github/workflows/maturation.yml): the loop's harvest/gate steps need no change (with the planner filtered, purely-structural cells never reach queue-plan.json), and the existing 'git add analysis' carries the new file into the maturation: commit; the job summary now reports BOTH — 'N harvest task(s) dispatched, M structural task(s) queued for authoring'. tools/maturation-log.ts records structural_queued (count of authoring-queue tasks) in the weekly entry so the /maturation cockpit history has it. lib/types.ts gains AuthoringTask, AuthoringQueue, TypedGap.missing_interaction_pairs / uncovered_stages, and MaturationLogEntry.structural_queued (optional, back-compatible); authoring-queue.json is generated output on the /analysis surface, not validated by tools/validate.ts (the matrix/queue precedent). Verified: re-running the loop on the current matrix dispatches far fewer harvests for the interaction-heavy red cells and populates the authoring queue instead; the research-queue budget block claims fewer tasks (spend drops accordingly); npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Interactions are first-class authored records; interaction_coverage reads them; this is the primary structural filler
decisions.body: interaction_coverage is the biggest structural gap in the sufficiency matrix (D-050), and until now the ONLY way to fill it was a registry relation on a mechanism record — a thin, single-note projection. This introduces a first-class OWNER-AUTHORED interaction record type and store: /interactions/{MECH-A}__{MECH-B}.json = { pair (sorted by id.localeCompare, matching the filename), type (sequence-amplifying | reinforcing | suppressing | neutral), fact, grade, boundary, source }, schema at /interactions/interaction.schema.json (mechanism/dossier schema-file pattern). Content is owner-provided, never Cursor-generated (rule 8): the store ships with the schema file only, no example records. lib/types.ts gains InteractionType and InteractionRecord (rule 13). READS (three): (1) tools/analyzer.ts — interactionCoverage now counts a pair as covered if a non-orthogonality_note relation OR an authored record connects it, and authored pairs drop out of missing_interaction_pairs, so the typed structural gap and the authoring queue shrink automatically as records land (gap-planner unchanged). DECISION: ALL FOUR types count as covered, INCLUDING neutral — an authored record means the owner examined the pair, which is exactly what coverage measures; this differs from the cheap orthogonality_note RELATION, which stays excluded because it is a by-product of writing a mechanism, not a deliberate pairwise judgment. (2) tools/render-packs.ts LAYER 2 — already the pack's interaction layer; it now MERGES the store with relations: an authored record maps directly (combination = pair, type/fact/grade/boundary/source from the record, grade owner-stated not derived) and REPLACES the relation-derived entry for the same pair (richer, owner-curated); relations still fill pairs with no record. PackInteractionType gains suppressing/neutral; PackInteraction gains optional boundary/source (authored entries only). With an empty store LAYER 2 output is byte-identical to before. (3) tools/validate.ts — a new pass compiles the schema and validates every /interactions/*.json plus cross-checks: pair sorted and distinct, both ids in the registry roster, filename = {pair[0]}__{pair[1]}.json, no pair authored twice. AUTHORING VIEW: /maturation gains an 'Interaction authoring' panel (lib/maturation.ts computeInteractionAuthoring) that aggregates the authoring-queue's interaction_coverage missing_interaction_pairs into a ranked, deduped list, each pair showing a computed 'not yet authored' vs 'authored' chip (from file existence, mapped through lib/status.ts INTERACTION_AUTHORING_META — no status literal in app/), the expected filename to create in git, and the affected pack×segment cells. Read-only: knowledge is edited in git, no UI write surface. This is the PRIMARY structural filler for the matrix. VERIFY: adding one owner-provided interaction JSON raises interaction_coverage on the affected cells (npm run analyze), removes the pair from the authoring queue (npm run gaps), and, when both members share a pack, injects it into that pack's LAYER 2 (npm run packs). npm run validate and npm run build green with the empty store.

decisions.title: Harvest optimizes for diversity and novelty, not volume; re-fetching canon is not progress
decisions.body: When harvesting IS the right fix (a scored harvest gap, D-056), a harvest must broaden the corpus, not re-read it. The evidence connector's segment-qualified harvest (tools/connectors/evidence.ts, v2.3.0 → 2.4.0) is upgraded on four axes. (1) QUERY-TERM VARIATION: each term now fans out across viewpoints instead of one canon query — 'canon' (the term as-is: OpenAlex cited_by_count:desc 25 + Semantic Scholar relevance 15, unchanged), 'recent' (OpenAlex publication_date:desc, 10), and five CONTRAST ANGLES (application 'applied intervention', critique 'critique criticism', replication 'replication', boundary 'boundary conditions moderators', cross-domain 'cross-domain generalization', 10 each). The angle suffixes are generic ACADEMIC VOCABULARY — a documented constant (CONTRAST_ANGLES), the same pattern as DISSENT_MARKERS — never invented science (rule 8); they steer which slice of the literature a query surfaces, not what the evidence says. (2) SOURCE SPREAD: the contrast angles ALTERNATE OpenAlex / Semantic Scholar by index (even → OpenAlex, odd → S2) so a run draws across both wired APIs, not one; canon already uses both. (3) DEDUP-AWARE NOVELTY: after the existing DOI/OpenAlex-id/title dedupe, the deduped SEARCH records (owner pins and snowballed references excluded — they are structural completeness, not query diversity) are checked against the PREVIOUS corpus file; a harvest whose unique results are more than LOW_NOVELTY_KNOWN_SHARE (0.8) already-in-corpus sets low_novelty: true and emits RunResult.warnings.low_novelty (same manifest channel as s2_throttled). The corpus file is still written (it is honest data; the anti-regression guardrail D-038 is unchanged), but the flag prevents the loop from thinking it filled a gap by re-fetching. A first harvest (no prior file) is novelty_rate 1, never low. (4) RECENCY BALANCE: the dedicated 'recent' query keeps newer work in reach so segments tied to newer product forms aren't starved by citation sort. Every harvest writes a diversity_report into corpora/evidence/{id}.json { viewpoint_spread[] (per angle: queries, returned, unique deduped records surfaced), source_spread[] (per API, same), recent_records, recency_rate, novelty { previous_corpus_records, unique_records, already_in_corpus, new_records, novelty_rate, low_novelty, known_share_threshold } }. Attribution is exact: dedupeRecords now returns the raw clusters aligned to the merged records, and mergeCluster unions each cluster's search_angles, so a unique record is credited to every angle/API that surfaced any variant of it. quote() (D-025) is updated deterministically to the new per-term call/record math (canon 2 + recent 1 + 5 contrast angles, alternating APIs) so the /ops dry-run gate stays honest; ~8 search calls/term (3 terms ≈ 24) stays well under the per-run budget and the S2 1 rps queue (D-027) — only the canon S2 query is throttleable, contrast S2 queries keep their fixed batch. LOOP: tools/gap-planner.ts (npm run gaps) now SKIPS a candidate whose mechanism's last harvest used the SAME terms and came back low_novelty — re-fetching the same canon is pure budget burn — BEFORE it consumes a budget slot; the skip is COUNTED in research-queue.json low_novelty_skipped (never silently dropped: change the mechanism's terms or the segment qualifier and it re-enters). .github/workflows/maturation.yml (D-052) counts how many of a run's harvested mechanisms came back low_novelty (jq over their corpus files' diversity_report) into a job-summary line and passes it to tools/maturation-log.ts --low-novelty, recorded as MaturationLogEntry.low_novelty_harvests (optional, back-compatible) and shown on the /maturation cockpit weekly log. VALIDATION: tools/validate.ts gains a pass — every corpora/evidence/*.json (incl. *.regression.json) that carries a diversity_report is validated against an inline schema (viewpoint + source spread, novelty block with boolean low_novelty); a file without the block is a pre-D-058 corpus and stays valid (additive, never a new hard requirement on old data). lib/types.ts gains ResearchQueue.low_novelty_skipped and MaturationLogEntry.low_novelty_harvests (rule 13). THE POLICY: harvest optimizes for diversity and novelty, not volume; re-fetching canon is not progress. Verify: a first diversified harvest of a genuine gap writes a diversity_report with non-empty viewpoint_spread and both APIs in source_spread; an immediate re-run with the same terms collapses novelty_rate and sets low_novelty (report + manifest warning); npm run gaps then skips that candidate and counts it in low_novelty_skipped. npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Evidence exhaustion is detected and surfaced honestly; the loop never harvests indefinitely against thin literature
decisions.body: Some segment×mechanism gaps have thin REAL literature — no amount of good harvesting closes them, and the D-058 low-novelty skip only stops re-fetching the SAME terms, so a thin gap can still churn forever as segment qualifiers vary and the per-mechanism diversity_report is overwritten by other segments' harvests. This adds persistent per-gap memory and an honest give-up: the loop concludes 'the literature is thin' instead of harvesting the same canon week after week. THE LEDGER: a new tool tools/harvest-history.ts (npm run harvest-history) appends one attempt per harvested (mechanism × segment) target per weekly run to analysis/harvest-history.json { version, generated_at, entries: { 'MECH|segment': { attempts:[{week, terms, low_novelty}], low_novelty_streak, streak_since } } } — a COMPUTED projection, never hand-edited (the maturation-log precedent, D-053), recorded ONLY from artifacts the loop already produces (queue-plan.json's action:'run' entries + each corpus's diversity_report.novelty.low_novelty, D-058); it re-computes nothing. Re-running a week REPLACES that week's attempt (idempotent), then recomputes each target's trailing low-novelty streak (consecutive low-novelty weeks; a novel harvest resets it). Only tasks the plan RAN add an attempt — a deferred/skipped task did not harvest. THE RULE (analysis/analyzer.config.yaml gains exhaustion.low_novelty_attempts: K, default 3): tools/analyzer.ts marks a cell evidence_exhausted:true when it still has a SCORED harvest gap below threshold (grade_sufficiency/freshness — mirrors the D-056 harvestable test; the segment_evidence pseudo-gap alone never qualifies) AND every one of its pack's mechanisms has low_novelty_streak ≥ K for that segment in the ledger. The cell keeps its computed scores/status (exhaustion is an honest 'best available', not a status flip) and records exhaustion { attempts (total low-novelty harvests across the pack's mechanisms), weeks (min shared low-novelty streak, ≥K), since (the week from which every mechanism has been continuously low-novelty), best_scores (the cell's current harvest-criterion scores) }. Reversible: a novel harvest resets a mechanism's streak, so the next analyze drops the flag and the cell re-enters. Absent ledger or absent exhaustion block → exhaustion never fires (fresh-repo behavior). THE QUEUE (tools/gap-planner.ts): an evidence_exhausted cell is removed from the harvest path BEFORE qualifier requirements and budget sizing — no more harvesting against thin literature — and the removed (mechanism × segment) candidates (only those not still reachable via a non-exhausted cell) are counted in research-queue.json evidence_exhausted_skipped (mirror of low_novelty_skipped, never silently dropped). Each exhausted cell is instead routed to analysis/authoring-queue.json as an AuthoringTask with alternative_fill:true, fill_options:[owner_judgment, cross_domain_analogy, accept_lower_confidence], and its exhaustion summary — owner judgment is the only remaining closer, exactly what the authoring queue is for; it is added ALONGSIDE any structural gaps the cell also has, ranked by its (now unharvestable) harvest gap-size when it has no structural gap. THE WORKFLOW (.github/workflows/maturation.yml): a new step runs harvest-history.ts BEFORE the re-analyze step, so a cell crossing K THIS week is marked exhausted by the very next scoped re-analyze (same run, not a week later); the re-analyze step counts evidence_exhausted cells in the re-scored matrix into the job summary and passes it to tools/maturation-log.ts --evidence-exhausted, recorded as MaturationLogEntry.evidence_exhausted (optional, back-compatible). The existing 'git add analysis' carries harvest-history.json into the maturation: commit. THE COCKPIT (/maturation): exhausted cells render in the muted plan-slate token CELL_EXHAUSTED_META ('thin literature — best available', #7C93A8 — the existing plan-blue, no new palette) rather than the red alert; coverage counts them in a distinct 'exhausted' band (COVERAGE_BAND_ORDER) apart from red so a proven-thin gap never shows as an actionable red-forever cell; a new 'Thin literature — best available' panel lists each exhausted cell's best-achievable scores, harvest effort, and the three alternative fillers (computeThinLiterature), with an honest empty state. All status/label literals stay in lib/status.ts (CELL_EXHAUSTED_META, COVERAGE_BAND_META, ALTERNATIVE_FILL_META); app/ carries no literal (honesty rule, grep-clean). lib/types.ts gains ExhaustionConfig, CellExhaustion, SufficiencyCell.evidence_exhausted/exhaustion, ResearchQueue.evidence_exhausted_skipped, AlternativeFillOption, AuthoringTask.alternative_fill/fill_options/exhaustion, MaturationLogEntry.evidence_exhausted, and the HarvestAttempt/HarvestHistoryTarget/HarvestHistory trio (rule 13). package.json gains the harvest-history script. harvest-history.json is generated output on the /analysis surface, not validated by tools/validate.ts (the sufficiency-matrix / research-queue / maturation-log precedent, D-050/D-051/D-053). THE POLICY, logged by the planner: evidence exhaustion is detected and surfaced honestly; the loop never harvests indefinitely against thin literature. Verify: a deliberately un-fillable gap (obscure segment×mechanism) fed 3 weekly low-novelty attempts per mechanism gets marked evidence_exhausted after the 3rd, leaves the research queue (counted in evidence_exhausted_skipped), appears in the authoring queue with alternative_fill, and renders on the cockpit as 'thin literature — best available' rather than red; a single novel harvest clears the streak and it re-enters. npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Sufficiency thresholds are stage-aware and explicit; green at seed stage means seed-adequate, not final
decisions.body: An 80% interaction_coverage bar is UNREACHABLE at t=0 with 12 seed mechanisms, so a stage-blind 'mature' threshold paints honest early progress red — the red then encodes the project's STAGE, not a real knowledge gap. This makes sufficiency thresholds STAGE-AWARE in the analyzer config: a single owner-tunable knob maturity_stage (seed | growing | mature) selects which per-criterion thresholds are active. THE CONFIG (analysis/analyzer.config.yaml, version 0.1.0 → 0.2.0): the flat thresholds: block is replaced by maturity_stage: seed plus stage_thresholds: { seed, growing, mature }, each a { default } + per-criterion override map (the same shape the flat block had). seed sets default { green 0.5, amber 0.3 } and interaction_coverage { green 0.4, amber 0.2 }; growing default { green 0.65, amber 0.4 } / interaction_coverage { green 0.6, amber 0.35 }; mature default { green 0.8, amber 0.5 } — mature is the UNCHANGED final bar, so nothing about the eventual standard is lowered. dissent_completeness stays a hard hygiene bar { green 1.0, amber 0.8 } at EVERY stage: hygiene is not maturity, so one stripped dossier still reds the cell regardless of stage. THE GUARANTEE — NOT A SILENT LOWERING: tools/analyzer.ts validateConfig requires maturity_stage to be one of the three and every stage to carry a valid default (0 ≤ amber ≤ green ≤ 1), and enforces MONOTONICITY loudly — for every resolved criterion, green and amber must be NON-DECREASING seed → growing → mature; a stage that relaxed below an earlier one fails the build. The bar only ever rises. THE FLOW stays one-directional: config → analyzer → matrix header → cockpit, so no component reads a threshold that isn't in a generated file. The analyzer resolves the active stage once (activeThresholds) — thresholdFor reads it exactly as before — and STAMPS maturity_stage + the resolved thresholds map into the matrix header (analysis/sufficiency-matrix.json gains maturity_stage and thresholds alongside config_version). tools/gap-planner.ts reads the same maturity_stage + stage_thresholds to size gaps (greenThreshold), so gap distances shrink/grow consistently with what actually fails a cell at the active stage. THE COCKPIT (/maturation): a 'stage: {stage}' chip sits beside the % green chip in the header; the Sufficiency matrix panel renders a ThresholdStrip stating the active stage, its plain-language meaning ('green means seed-adequate, not final — the bar rises as the knowledge matures'), and the per-criterion green/amber bars — every value READ from matrix.maturity_stage / matrix.thresholds, nothing hardcoded (honesty rule, .cursorrules #2; grep-clean of threshold literals in app/). A matrix predating the stage-aware header renders no strip (honest absence, not a fabricated bar). lib/types.ts gains MaturityStage and StageThresholds, replaces AnalyzerConfig.thresholds with maturity_stage + stage_thresholds, and adds SufficiencyMatrix.maturity_stage + thresholds (rule 13). THE POLICY: thresholds are stage-aware and explicit; green at seed stage means seed-adequate, not final. Verify: npm run analyze at maturity_stage: seed vs mature visibly changes the green/amber/red counts and which cells are green; the cockpit shows the active stage chip + threshold strip with values matching the config; no threshold literal lives in app/ or lib/ components. npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Cockpit distinguishes gap types and filler routes; the owner sees what to harvest vs what to author
decisions.body: Red/green alone hid WHICH filler a gap needs — the owner could see a cell was failing but not whether it was waiting on an automated harvest or on their own edit in git. The /maturation cockpit now makes the fix_type routing (D-055/D-056) and the exhaustion signal (D-058/D-059) VISIBLE per cell and per queue, so the same split the loop acts on is the split the owner reads. This is a cockpit-visibility step only: no analyzer/planner/workflow change, and the honesty rule holds — every route, count, and flag is COMPUTED at render time from analysis/*.json + segments.yaml, and every new literal lives in lib/status.ts (app/ stays grep-clean). VOCABULARY (lib/status.ts): FIX_TYPE_META maps GapFixType → { harvest (amber, automated connector work), author (slate, owner edit in git) }; computeCellRoute(cell) mirrors the gap planner's routing (lib never imports tools/, so the policy is duplicated, not shared) into green | exhausted | harvest | authoring — green is saturated, evidence_exhausted routes to exhausted (D-059), a cell with ≥1 SCORED harvest gap (grade_sufficiency/freshness, the segment_evidence pseudo-gap excluded, D-056) routes to harvest, and a red/amber cell whose only gaps are structural routes to authoring. COVERAGE (lib/maturation.ts): StatusCounts gains an authoring band and tally() classifies each cell by computeCellRoute, so COVERAGE_BAND_ORDER is now red | amber | authoring | exhausted | green — the summary distinguishes green, evidence-exhausted best-available (D-059), awaiting-authoring (owner edits), and the actionable red/amber a harvest can still move; a structural or thin-literature gap no longer inflates the red-forever share. CELL HOVER (app/maturation/page.tsx CellTooltip): the flat 5-score list is replaced by two groups built from cell.typed_gaps — 'harvest gaps' (grade/freshness + the segment_evidence pseudo-gap) and 'authoring gaps' (interaction/context/dissent) — each line showing the criterion, its score vs threshold, and a route chip (FIX_TYPE_META); passing criteria stay listed with scores; below are honest flag lines for evidence_exhausted (existing copy), low novelty ('low novelty: N/M mechanisms on a repeat-harvest streak', from a new analysis/harvest-history.json reader, omitted when the ledger is absent), the segment-evidence flag, and the maturity stage. TWO QUEUES SIDE BY SIDE: the research queue is retitled 'Harvest queue — automated' (budget-bounded, connector-dispatched, content unchanged) and sits in a 2-column grid beside a new 'Authoring queue — manual' panel that reads analysis/authoring-queue.json directly — stats (cells queued, thin-lit alternative-fill count), the ranked tasks (pack × segment, status chip, importance, per-structural-gap criterion chips with route, a thin-literature marker + alternative fillers for exhausted cells) capped at 10 with an honest '+ N more in analysis/authoring-queue.json' overflow line, and a designed empty state. The existing 'Thin literature' and 'Interaction authoring' panels stay below as detail views. lib/status.ts gains FIX_TYPE_META, CellRoute + computeCellRoute, COVERAGE_AUTHORING_META and the extended COVERAGE_BAND_ORDER; lib/maturation.ts gains StatusCounts.authoring, MATURATION_PATHS.harvestHistory + loadHarvestHistory, and CellNovelty + computeCellNovelty. THE POLICY: cockpit distinguishes gap types and filler routes; the owner sees what to harvest vs what to author. Verify: hovering a current red cell shows interaction_coverage/context_coverage under 'authoring gaps' and segment_evidence under 'harvest gaps'; the coverage bar shows the current structural-only reds as 'awaiting authoring' (harvest queue honestly empty, authoring queue populated with the ranked structural tasks); no status literal lives in app/. npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: S7 Perception & comprehension added as a cross-cutting L0 taxonomy node
decisions.body: S7 added as a cross-cutting L0 node — perception precedes motivation; it applies to every generated element, not to specific funnel stages. The owner-provided node (registry/taxonomy.json) is { id: S7, name: 'Perception & comprehension', anchors.rdoc: 'Cognitive systems — attention, perception, working memory', description covering attention allocation, cognitive load, modality, processing fluency and scanning behaviour, cross_cutting: true }. The taxonomy schema gains an OPTIONAL cross_cutting boolean on a node (absent === false), and the inline taxonomySchema in tools/validate.ts widens from 6→7 nodes (minItems/maxItems 7, id pattern ^S[1-7]$) with the three size cross-checks updated to 7 and the failure message to S1–S7. lib/types.ts adds S7 to TaxonomyNodeId and cross_cutting?: boolean to TaxonomyNode (rule 13). Coverage is unaffected: computeRegistryTree() in lib/status.ts maps over loadTaxonomy().nodes, so S7 renders with zero children and an empty coverage line while the existing six nodes are byte-identical; the analyzer/gap-planner/packs never read the taxonomy. The /registry page shows a data-derived 'cross-cutting' tag beside the node name (not a status — the honesty rule holds) and the existing designed empty state for a node with no mechanisms. mechanism.schema.json parent pattern stays ^S[1-6]$ deliberately: this step only creates the node; nothing hangs off S7 yet, and widening the parent surface belongs to the step that admits S7 children. Verify: npm run validate green (taxonomy valid at 7 nodes, all cross-refs intact); npm run build green; Registry shows S7 with zero mechanisms and a cross-cutting marker; the six existing nodes' coverage is unchanged.

decisions.title: S7 seeded with six candidates covering modality, load, multimedia design, fluency, scanning and foraging; all enter via the standard dossier gate
decisions.body: Six owner-provided candidate mechanisms enter under S7 (Perception & comprehension, D-062) as honest seed stubs in /registry/mechanisms/_seed/ — the same gate as every other mechanism, no shortcuts: they stay stubs until a dossier moves them through the lifecycle gate, and no content beyond what the owner provided was invented (rule 8). The roster: PS-13 Picture superiority / dual coding (grade_draft A), CL-14 Cognitive load (A), MM-15 Multimedia design principles (A), PF-16 Processing fluency (A-), SC-17 Scanning & visual attention (B), IF-18 Information foraging (B+). Each stub carries parent: S7, lifecycle_status: candidate, cross_cutting: true, plus owner-provided evidence_terms (5 each, including replication/boundary/critique angles per D-015) and pinned_evidence (D-017) — two pins each except IF-18 which has one (Pirolli & Card). SCHEMA SURFACE (the two changes D-062 deferred to 'the step that admits S7 children'): mechanism.schema.json $defs.seedStub widens parent from ^S[1-6]$ to ^S[1-7]$ and gains an OPTIONAL cross_cutting boolean (absent === false); the sub-schema stays additionalProperties:false and the stale '11 candidate seed stubs' wording is generalized. The FULL-record parent pattern stays ^S[1-6]$ deliberately — no S7 mechanism has passed the dossier gate yet, so widening the full-record surface belongs to the promotion step, not this one. lib/types.ts adds cross_cutting?: boolean to SeedStub, mirroring the sub-schema (rule 13). The registry showcase is unchanged code: computeRegistryTree() in lib/status.ts joins loadTaxonomy().nodes × loadSeedStubs(), so S7 now renders 6 candidates / 0 full records purely from the files (honesty rule holds; no status hardcoded). The _seed/README.md roster note is refreshed: the original SPEC.md §2 seeds were promoted to full records, and the folder now holds the S7 candidate roster. Verify: npm run validate green (six stubs valid against seedStub, all candidate, all parent S7, ids unique across the roster); npm run build green; /registry shows S7 with 6 candidates and 0 full records; no invented content beyond the owner-provided stubs.

decisions.title: Full-record parent widened to S1–S7 and cross_cutting allowed on full records; the S7 promotion path is open
decisions.body: The two schema changes D-062/D-063 deferred to 'the step that admits S7 children' are made now, ahead of Step 4 (the six S7 candidates becoming full records or being rejected). mechanism.schema.json full-record parent pattern widens from ^S[1-6]$ to ^S[1-7]$, and an OPTIONAL cross_cutting boolean is added to the full-record properties (absent === false), mirroring the seedStub sub-schema (D-063) — without it, additionalProperties:false would reject a promoted S7 record that must carry cross_cutting:true. lib/types.ts adds cross_cutting?: boolean to Mechanism (rule 13). No other change: tools/validate.ts is schema-driven and its parent-in-taxonomy cross-check already passes for S7 (added by D-062); the /registry showcase is unchanged code that renders whatever files exist (honesty rule holds). This step opens the surface only — no S7 record is promoted here; authoring the six records + dossiers is Step 4 content, entered by the owner/Claude and committed verbatim (rule 8). Verify: npm run validate green (existing 12 full records + 6 stubs unaffected; schema still compiles); npm run build green.

decisions.title: Corpus digest is the standard harvest → record-drafting hand-off, replacing raw corpus files in the drafting loop
decisions.body: A harvested corpus is 280–370 records of full abstracts — too large to read by hand when drafting a record + dossier. A new reader tool tools/corpus-digest.ts (npm run digest -- <MECHANISM-ID> [--top N] | --all) projects one corpus into the compact hand-off a drafter actually needs and writes it to /corpora/evidence/digests/{id}.md (markdown, also echoed to stdout). It is a READER, not a connector: it reads only local files (/corpora/evidence/{id}.json + the registry record or _seed stub for the pinned_evidence cross-check) and makes no network call — rule 12's whitelist is untouched, and it adds no science (rule 8), only re-projects what the harvest recorded. The digest carries: corpus stats (record count, fetched_at, terms + terms_source, query count), pins resolved/unresolved (declared pinned_evidence DOIs vs DOIs present in the corpus, missing DOIs listed), snowball_added + review-anchor status + coverage note, category_counts, and diversity (recency + novelty + viewpoint/source spread); then the top N records per evidence category (foundational / meta-analysis / replication / dissent / recent), ranked by citations, each with title, authors (first + et al.), year, venue, citations, DOI, source_api, cross-listed categories and search angles. Default N=15. lib/types.ts gains read-only mirror types for the corpus file (EvidenceCorpusFile and its parts — the writer's private interfaces live in tools/connectors/evidence.ts, lib never imports from tools/) plus the digest types (CorpusDigest, CorpusDigestEntry, CorpusDigestPins), no any (rule 13). package.json gains the digest script. THE POLICY: from this batch on, the digest is the standard harvest → drafting hand-off for every mechanism; the raw corpus stays on disk as provenance but is no longer read by hand while drafting. Digest .md files are generated output on the /corpora surface, not validated by tools/validate.ts (the render-cards precedent). Legacy pre-D-058 corpora carry no diversity_report, so the mirror type and the reader treat it as optional (novelty/recency shown as 'not recorded' rather than crashing). Verify: npm run digest -- PS-13 CL-14 MM-15 PF-16 SC-17 IF-18 writes six digests for the S7 candidates with pins resolved/unresolved reported and non-empty dissent lists; npm run digest -- --all additionally digests every core corpus with a registry entry; npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Cross-cutting mechanisms are emitted into every pack automatically; pack-map stays motivational-only
decisions.body: Perception & comprehension (S7, cross_cutting: true, D-062) precedes every motivational mechanism, so its evidence must reach every generated element — but listing it per element in the pack map would duplicate the same knowledge across 11 packs and inflate the sufficiency matrix with cells that are identical everywhere. THE POLICY: cross-cutting mechanisms are emitted into every pack automatically; pack-map stays motivational-only. tools/render-packs.ts reads registry/taxonomy.json, collects the L0 ids flagged cross_cutting (today only S7), selects every FULL record whose parent is one of them (the renderer never reads _seed/, so the set is empty until the S7 candidates are promoted to full records in Step 4), sorts by id, and emits them into a distinct top-level section cross_cutting_perception in EVERY pack — same datasheet atom as LAYER 1 (id, name, fact, grade, source, boundary, active_when, realizations, forbidden via the shared buildMechanism), placed between LAYER 1 and LAYER 2, kept separate from the pack's own motivational mechanisms. lib/types.ts adds cross_cutting_perception: PackMechanism[] to PackDatasheet (rule 13). When the set is empty the section renders as an empty flow list with an honest comment pointing at docs/s7-drafting-brief.md (rule 15). LAYER 1 guard: any cross-cutting id that slips into an element's mechanism list is filtered out before LAYER 1 is built, so a perception mechanism is never duplicated as a motivational atom. LAYER 2: the authored-interaction lookup (D-057) widens its pair scope from the pack's members to members UNION the cross-cutting set, so an owner-authored interactions/{A}__{B}.json between a perception mechanism and a pack mechanism surfaces in LAYER 2; relation-derived (fallback) interactions stay members-only, matching 'where authored'. SCOPE: LAYER 3 context weights, HARD BOUNDARIES, and telemetry signals stay derived from the pack's own motivational mechanisms only — perception rows carry their forbidden ids inline but do not inflate every pack's boundary/signal sections. ENFORCEMENT: tools/validate.ts (pack-map section) now errors if any element's mechanisms list contains an id whose L0 parent is cross_cutting, so 'pack-map does NOT list S7 mechanisms per element' is a validated invariant, not a convention. Verify: npm run packs regenerates all 11 packs, each carrying the cross_cutting_perception section (empty list + comment for now); no pack duplicates a perception mechanism in LAYER 1; pack-paywall-conversion.yaml reproduces its reference structure with only the new section added; npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Perception scored as its own matrix row group; cross-cutting knowledge is not counted 11 times
decisions.body: Cross-cutting perception (S7, cross_cutting: true) is emitted into every pack by render-packs (D-066), but scoring its sufficiency per pack would multiply the SAME knowledge into all 11 pack rows — 165 identical-everywhere cells that would distort the overall-green figure up or down as a single roster changes. THE POLICY: the analyzer scores cross-cutting mechanisms ONCE per segment in their own matrix row group ('perception'), not multiplied into the pack rows; perception coverage is reported separately from pack coverage. tools/analyzer.ts reads registry/taxonomy.json, collects the L0 ids flagged cross_cutting (today only S7), selects every FULL record whose parent is one of them (never reads _seed/, so the roster is empty until Step 4 promotes the S7 candidates), and scores a single 'perception' row across the same active segments with the SAME five criteria, thresholds, and exhaustion as the packs. Its gaps are typed by the existing fix_type logic (harvest vs structural, D-055) unchanged. While the roster is empty the perception row is an honest all-red bootstrap row (every criterion 0, all five as typed gaps) rather than the vacuous greens an empty member list would score (interaction_coverage / freshness = 1). SufficiencyCell gains row_group?: 'pack' | 'perception' (lib/types.ts, rule 13; absent = legacy pack cell); the analyzer stamps every cell and bumps MATRIX_VERSION to 0.3.0. The 'perception' row id is reserved: tools/validate.ts errors if a pack-map element claims it, and the analyzer guards the same. Scoped runs (packs=a,b, the weekly loop) treat perception as a filterable pseudo-row — re-scorable via packs=perception, preserved verbatim otherwise; loadExistingCells fails loudly on a preserved cell lacking row_group, so one full npm run analyze upgrades the whole grid. COVERAGE: lib/maturation.ts computeCoverage partitions cells by row_group — overall / perPack / perSegment tally PACK cells only (denominator stays 11x15, so the overall-green figure neither jumps nor collapses), and a new perception StatusCounts reports the cross-cutting row apart. buildHeatmap bands rows into a packs group + a perception group (always one row, null cells = 'not analyzed' when the matrix predates the group); computeCellNovelty computes the perception row's low-novelty flag from the roster. app/maturation/page.tsx renders the perception row under a labelled group separator and a separate 'perception green' coverage line, never folded into the pack figure; no status literal is added (honesty rule, mapped through lib/status.ts). tools/gap-planner.ts registers the roster under the perception row id so a perception cell with a scored harvest gap expands to (mechanism x segment) harvest candidates once S7 has full records; structural gaps already route to authoring per cell. The weekly loop (.github/workflows/maturation.yml) treats a perception flip as a full re-render (its evidence lands in the cross_cutting_perception section of EVERY pack), not a scoped npm run packs. Verify: npm run analyze adds 15 perception cells (180 total) all red with all five typed gaps; the pack overall-green figure is unchanged vs the pre-change matrix and perception reports 0% separately; npm run gaps surfaces the perception cells in the authoring queue with no bogus harvest expansion; npm run validate and npm run build green; /maturation shows the perception row group red across 15 segments and the separate perception coverage line.

decisions.title: Committed pack export bundle for team testing; generated by every pack render, surfaced read-only on the cockpit
decisions.body: Step 7 of the S7 phase calls for an export of the current pack set for team testing. Options considered: a download route in the app (new code surface, artifact not versioned), a GitHub link (no artifact at all), or a committed file. THE POLICY: tools/render-packs.ts writes /packs/export/packs-bundle.yaml — a multi-document YAML stream whose first document is a manifest (bundle: pack-export, version = pack-map version, pack_count, packs list, nature, source) followed by every pack-{id}.yaml verbatim (banners and comments preserved). The bundle is emitted by EVERY npm run packs run, full or scoped: it is always rebuilt from the pack files on disk (not just the packs rendered that run), so a scoped weekly-loop regenerate (D-052) still leaves a complete, current bundle. It carries NO timestamp — it is a pure function of the packs, so it only diffs when a pack diffs, and the team can read a week-over-week git diff of one file to see exactly what the guidance gained. Rationale for a committed file over an app route: the export stays versioned and diffable alongside the packs it came from, the app keeps zero new write/serve surface (constitution: file-based, narrow write surface D-023), and git is the handoff path the team already uses. Renderer self-check: the bundle must parse back as exactly pack_count + 1 YAML documents before writing. lib/types.ts gains PackBundleManifest (rule 13). ENFORCEMENT: tools/validate.ts pass 13b — when the bundle exists it must parse as multi-document YAML, open with the manifest, and the manifest's packs list / pack_count / document count must exactly match the pack-*.yaml files on disk (a mismatch means a stale or hand-edited bundle); an absent bundle is the honest pre-first-render state, not an error. COCKPIT: /maturation gains a 'Pack export — team testing' panel (lib/maturation.ts loadPackBundleManifest, fs-only) showing pack count, pack-map version, the bundled pack ids and the repo-relative handoff path, all read from the manifest at render time — nothing hardcoded (honesty rule); absent bundle renders a designed empty state (rule 15). The weekly loop needs no workflow change: its commit step already adds the packs/ tree. SCOPE NOTE: the Step 7 owner verify (perception sections present, evidence-toned, materially constraining density/modality/load) is deferred — the six S7 candidates are still _seed stubs with no harvested corpora, so cross_cutting_perception is honestly empty; when the records are promoted, npm run packs re-fills the sections and the bundle regenerates automatically, and the verify runs against that bundle diff. Verify now: npm run packs emits 11 packs + the bundle; a scoped run (packs=entry) leaves the bundle complete at 11; pack files byte-identical to the previous render; npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Interaction-authoring AUTHORED counter reads the /interactions store, not the (authored-pruned) authoring queue
decisions.body: The /maturation 'Interaction authoring' panel showed 'MISSING PAIRS N / AUTHORED 0' even after interactions/FR-11__SP-08.json was authored and committed, and the FR-11×SP-08 pair correctly no longer appeared in the missing-pairs list. TRACE (four questions): (1) the file exists at the exact path the readers use, /interactions/FR-11__SP-08.json, with the correct convention — double underscore, ids sorted by localeCompare (FR-11 < SP-08). No naming mismatch. (2) tools/analyzer.ts interaction_coverage DOES read the store, not just registry relations: it loads /interactions/*.json into authoredPairs and marks the pair covered, so the entry pack's affected cells score interaction_coverage 0.3333 (2/6) instead of 0.1667 (1/6) — the authored record is in the score. (3) ROOT CAUSE: the AUTHORED counter was derived from the authoring queue, not the interactions directory. lib/maturation.ts computeInteractionAuthoring builds its pair list ONLY from each task's missing_interaction_pairs, then computed authoredCount = pairs.filter(p => p.authored).length. But the analyzer DROPS an authored pair from missing_interaction_pairs the instant its record lands (D-057), so an authored pair never reappears in queue.tasks — a queue-derived authored tally is structurally pinned at ~0. (4) The missing-pairs list is correctly filtered to unauthored-only (the pair is absent because it is covered — correct behaviour, not a filter bug); only the AUTHORED display was wrong.
