THE FIX: authoredCount now reads authored.size — the count of records in the /interactions store (already loaded and passed in), which is what the panel hint 'records in /interactions/' has always promised. missingCount stays pairs.filter(p => !p.authored).length and each pair's authored flag/type is still read from the store, so even a stale queue that still listed an authored pair would render it 'authored' and exclude it from the missing tally (robust to queue staleness). No analyzer/gap-planner change: interaction_coverage already counts authored records and already prunes authored pairs from the queue. VALIDATOR: the naming/schema gate the issue asks for already exists — tools/validate.ts pass 14 (added with D-057) compiles interaction.schema.json, validates every /interactions/*.json, and cross-checks pair sorted + distinct, both ids in the registry roster, filename = {pair[0]}__{pair[1]}.json, and no pair authored twice; a single-vs-double-underscore filename, a reversed FR-11/SP-08 order, or a schema-invalid record fails CI rather than being silently skipped by the app reader (which catches-and-skips by design because the validator is the gate). lib/types.ts unchanged. Verify: /maturation now shows AUTHORED 1 with the FR-11×SP-08 record present, the missing-pairs list unchanged (the pair stays absent because it is covered), and interaction_coverage on the entry cells reflecting the record; npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: Interaction batch 1 authored — 10 pairs gating the four zero-coverage packs
decisions.body: First owner-authored batch of pairwise interaction records (D-057) landed in /interactions: EN-03__VR-02, EN-03__ZE-07, VR-02__ZE-07, CG-05__FR-11, CG-05__RE-10, CG-05__SP-08, FR-11__RE-10, ID-12__VR-02, EN-03__ST-09, LA-01__ST-09 — committed verbatim (texts, grades, source lines unmodified). Grades span B+ to C by design: the C/C+ records state in their boundary and source that the interaction is inferred convergence of two literatures, not a directly studied pair, and that wording is preserved as the honest evidence signal; the B-range records (EN-03__ZE-07 endowed-progress, VR-02__ZE-07 motivating-uncertainty, EN-03__ST-09 loyalty-tier ownership, LA-01__ST-09 status-demotion loss aversion) rest on directly studied effects. These ten are exactly the unlinked member pairs that were dragging the four packs below the seed-stage interaction_coverage green bar (0.4): first-value, onboarding, entry, retention-billing. AUTHORED count 1 -> 11 (the pre-existing FR-11__SP-08 plus this batch). EFFECT after npm run analyze + npm run packs: interaction_coverage rose first-value 0 -> 1.0, onboarding 0.3333 -> 1.0, entry 0.3333 -> 1.0, retention-billing 0.3333 -> 1.0, and (bonus, already above the bar) core-ux 0.6667 -> 1.0; the other packs are unchanged (retention-return, paywall-conversion, aha-sharing at 0.6667; engagement-loops, social-proof-status, trust-friction at 1.0; the perception cross-cutting row stays 0 until S7 records exist). All four gated packs flip from red/amber to fully green on interaction_coverage and their datasheets regenerated (LAYER 2 now projects the authored records in place of the relation-derived fallbacks). Structural interaction_coverage gap pairs (pairs listed in below-threshold cells) 10 -> 0; total distinct unlinked member pairs across all packs 14 -> 4 (remaining EN-03__FR-11, EN-03__SC-06, HA-04__LA-01, RE-10__ST-09 sit only in packs already above the coverage bar, so they raise no gap). This is a stronger result than the drop-to-7 estimate: the batch cleared every gate-driving pair. render-packs emitted one instruction-voice lint warning on ID-12__VR-02 (the quoted example 'you're building something'); the record is owner content and was left verbatim (rule 8) — flagged, not modified. npm run validate green (all 11 interaction records + schema); analyzer and pack bundle regenerated.

decisions.title: Mechanism ids carry their L0 node in the UI so perception (S7) is distinguishable from motivational mechanisms
decisions.body: S7 Perception & comprehension (cross_cutting: true, D-062) reads and renders as the seventh L0 node on /registry with its six candidate stubs (PS-13, CL-14, MM-15, PF-16, SC-17, IF-18) — computeRegistryTree already maps all taxonomy nodes with no S1–S6 cap, so no fix was needed there; likewise the six S7 stubs (incl. PS-13) were already present in the /ops evidence target list via loadSeedStubs and in corpora/_ops/connectors/evidence.json. THE GAP was that bare mechanism ids gave the operator no way to tell a cross-cutting perception mechanism from a motivational one. THE POLICY: a single computed index resolves every mechanism id to its L0 parent, and the id is never shown alone where the parent matters. lib/status.ts adds MechanismNodeRef + loadMechanismNodeIndex() — reads registry/taxonomy.json + full records + seed stubs (never hardcoded), mapping each id to { parent, parentName, crossCutting } where crossCutting = the L0 node's flag OR the record's own. /ops target picker: the flat, unlabeled datalist/select/chips are replaced by node-grouped UI (app/ops/ops-client.tsx groupIdsByNode + nodeHeading) — the 'what it harvests' chips are grouped under node headings (S1–S6 motivational, S7 cross-cutting amber-tagged), the add-target control is a <select> with <optgroup> per node, and the run-target <select> is likewise grouped; a hand-typed id not in the registry falls into a trailing 'not in registry' group rather than being dropped. /maturation: the harvest queue rows and interaction-authoring pair rows render a NodeBadge after each bare mechanism id (parent id + amber 'cross-cutting' marker, full node name on hover). The matrix hover and pack-export panel show pack ids (not mechanism ids) and the cross-cutting perception row is already its own labelled row group (D-067), so they needed no change. No status literal added (honesty rule, .cursorrules #2); every label is computed from files. Verify: /registry shows S7 as the 7th node with 6 stubs + cross-cutting tag; /ops target picker groups all mechanisms under node headings with all six S7 ids present; /maturation queue and interaction pairs show the parent node on each id; npm run validate and npm run build green.

decisions.title: SC-17 and IF-18 evidence_terms corrected for polysemy; a poisoned corpus is cleared before re-harvest so the connector's first-harvest path handles a replacement, not a D-038 regression
decisions.body: The first S7 candidate harvests (D-063) produced two poisoned corpora: SC-17 'Scanning & visual attention' collided with scanning/scintigraphy microscopy and web servers (its top foundational works were SILAC proteomics, the FoldX web server, X-ray diffraction microscopy), and IF-18 'Information foraging' collided with ecological foraging and economics search costs (top works were fractional Brownian motion, agricultural economics, livestock climate). Root cause is term polysemy, not a connector bug — tools/connectors/evidence.ts resolves terms from the record's evidence_terms (D-015) and the generic terms matched the wrong literatures. FIX (owner-provided terms, rule 8 — no invented science, only search strings): registry/mechanisms/_seed/SC-17.json evidence_terms -> [visual attention web page; eye movements reading screen; banner blindness advertising; web page fixation attention advertisement; visual hierarchy attention interface; attention capture web design]; registry/mechanisms/_seed/IF-18.json evidence_terms -> [information foraging theory Pirolli; information scent user navigation; information scent hypertext browsing; web navigation cue judgment; information seeking behaviour interface]. pinned_evidence left untouched. THE GUARD INTERACTION: the corrected terms are narrower, so a re-harvest yields fewer records than the polluted corpora (SC-17 298, IF-18 316) and would trip the anti-regression guard (D-038, evidence.ts): the run would write {id}.regression.json and KEEP the bad file. That guard is correct — it cannot tell a genuine regression from an intentional replacement of a poisoned corpus. THE MECHANISM (no code change, no new machinery): the poisoned corpus files (corpora/evidence/SC-17.json, IF-18.json) and their stale digests were DELETED before re-running, so the connector took its first-harvest path (previousRecords === null): the D-038 regression guard is skipped and the D-058 novelty gate reports novelty 1 (full novelty, not a low-novelty re-read of the canon). The seed stubs are candidate with dossier_ref absent, so the D-038 validation hard rule (a dossier'd record must carry evidence_terms) does not apply and validate stays green. RESULT after re-harvest: SC-17 307 records (was 298), novelty 1 (305/305 new), category_counts foundational 3 / meta-analysis 6 / replication 24 / dissent 87 / recent 111 — foundational now led by 'Attention web designers: You have 50 milliseconds to make a good first impression!' (Behavior & Information Technology, 1073 cites) with 'WHY DO PEOPLE AVOID ADVERTISING ON THE INTERNET?' (banner blindness) prominent; ~197/307 records HCI vs ~7 off-domain. IF-18 175 records, novelty 1 (175/175 new), foundational 1 / meta-analysis 2 / replication 9 / dissent 53 / recent 58 — the Pirolli & Card pin resolved via OpenAlex (1263 cites, foundational) and the corpus is led by Information Foraging, SNIF-ACT, Scented Widgets, and 'The scent of a site'; ~100/175 HCI vs ~3 off-domain. Both runs returned status partial with warnings.capped: the keyless Semantic Scholar pool 429'd persistently and the D-027 retry/backoff passes consumed the max_calls_per_run=150 _ops budget (a graceful stop, not a failure); SC-17's two pins fell back to owner-provided metadata (D-017) because the budget was spent before the pin lookups. The residual off-domain tail (~2% of each corpus) comes from the D-058 generic contrast-angle suffixes (cross-domain generalization, boundary conditions), not from the polysemy — a known diversity-vs-precision trade-off, not a re-harvest defect. The proteomics/microscopy/ecology/agriculture domination is gone: both corpora are now human-attention / HCI literature.

decisions.title: S7 batch 1 (CL-14, MM-15, PS-13, PF-16) admitted to incubating; SC-17 and IF-18 held for re-harvest after term collision
decisions.body: The first four S7 Perception & comprehension mechanisms passed the dossier gate (SPEC §3.3: total >= 11 with evidence >= 2 and safety >= 2) and were promoted from the temp staging folder to full L1 records — CL-14 Cognitive load, MM-15 Multimedia design principles, PS-13, PF-16 Processing fluency — each cross_cutting: true, parent S7, lifecycle_status incubating, verdict incubating. Owner-authored content (texts, evidence grades, axis scores, dissent statements) was committed VERBATIM (.cursorrules rule 8): the four full records moved to registry/mechanisms/{id}.json (replacing and deleting their _seed/{id}.json candidate stubs so the roster carries one entry per id), and the four dossiers moved to dossiers/{id}.json. PF-16 is admitted at the total-11 admission FLOOR by design: safety 1 is the lowest score in S7 and among the lowest in the registry because the mechanism includes the illusory-truth effect (repeated/fluent claims judged more accurate irrespective of accuracy; Fazio et al. 2015 showed prior knowledge does not protect) — the cognitive basis of misinformation — and it is constrained by three block-severity guardrails (no fluency on unsupported claims; no deliberate disfluency to obstruct; material information at least as fluent as promotional content). This is the honest position, preserved as written, not a scoring error. PS-13's dossier carries an owner note recommending a re-harvest before any CORE promotion; preserved as written. SC-17 Scanning & visual attention and IF-18 Information foraging remain candidate seed stubs, HELD for re-harvest: their first harvests were poisoned by term polysemy and their evidence_terms were corrected but the corpora not yet re-validated for a gate (D-072). RESULT: registry now shows S7 with 4 full records + 2 candidates; 16 full mechanism records and 16 dossiers on file. render-cards emitted cards/{CL-14,MM-15,PS-13,PF-16}.md; render-packs (D-066) now finds four full records whose L0 parent (S7) is cross_cutting and emits them into the cross_cutting_perception section of EVERY generated pack (previously the honest empty [] placeholder), and the export bundle regenerated. npm run validate green (full records + seedStub, dossier totals equal axis sums, D-019 non-empty dissent on all four corpora, roster cross-references); npm run build green.

decisions.title: S7 perception node complete — six cross-cutting mechanisms admitted to incubating
decisions.body: The final two S7 Perception & comprehension mechanisms passed the dossier gate (SPEC §3.3: total >= 11 with evidence >= 2 and safety >= 2) and were promoted from the temp staging folder to full L1 records, completing the node held open at D-073: SC-17 Scanning & visual attention and IF-18 Information foraging — both cross_cutting: true, parent S7, lifecycle_status incubating, verdict incubating. Owner-authored content (texts, evidence grades, axis scores, dissent statements) was committed VERBATIM (.cursorrules rule 8): the two full records moved to registry/mechanisms/{id}.json (replacing and deleting their _seed/{id}.json candidate stubs, so _seed now holds only its README and the roster carries one entry per id), and the two dossiers moved to dossiers/{id}.json. Both were the mechanisms HELD at D-073 because their first harvests were poisoned by term polysemy; both corpora were re-harvested with corrected evidence_terms (SC-17: 390 records after discarding scanning-microscopy / web-server collisions; IF-18: 227 records after discarding ecological-foraging / economics collisions) and each dossier records that re-harvest plainly. SC-17 is admitted at the total-11 admission FLOOR by design: evidence 2 (with measurability 2, orthogonality 2, safety 2) is the weakest-evidence mechanism in the perception node because the field is heavily contaminated by practitioner folklore (F-shaped scanning, fold dogma, absolute banner blindness) — so the mechanism is claimed NARROWLY (selective, non-linear sampling and fast first impressions) with NO specific scan-pattern encoded, and the review-anchor filter found no qualifying topical review, so coverage rests on pins plus term breadth. This is the honest position, preserved as written, not a scoring error. IF-18 admitted at total 14, the most directly A/B-testable perception mechanism. RESULT: S7 is complete with 6 full records and 0 candidates; the registry holds 18/18 full mechanism records and 18 dossiers on file. render-cards emitted cards/{SC-17,IF-18}.md (18 cards total); render-packs (D-066) now finds all six full cross-cutting S7 records and emits them into the cross_cutting_perception section of EVERY generated pack, and the export bundle regenerated. The analyzer's perception row group (D-067) moved off its honest all-red bootstrap state — with a non-empty cross-cutting roster it now scores dissent_completeness 1.0 and grade_sufficiency 0.8667, and the row is green on all 15 active-segment cells (0 amber / 0 red). Pack overall: 143 green / 17 amber / 5 red of 165 pack cells. npm run validate green (full records + seedStub, dossier totals equal axis sums, D-019 non-empty dissent on both corpora, roster cross-references); npm run build unaffected.

decisions.title: Autonomy phase: LLM extraction permitted in tools/ under provenance, proposal-queue, and budget constraints
decisions.body: The constitution (.cursorrules) forbade LLM API calls everywhere in the repo from Baseline. The corpus reader / autonomy phase requires lifting that ban NARROWLY. AMENDMENT: rule 12's blanket sentence 'LLM API calls remain forbidden everywhere in this repo' is replaced by a scoped permission — LLM API calls are permitted ONLY in the tools/ corpus-extraction pipeline, via the existing OpenRouter setup, and ONLY under ALL of these conditions: (a) extraction runs solely in GitHub Actions or as an explicitly dispatched job, never from the Next.js app (app/, middleware, server actions); (b) every extracted item carries provenance (source corpus record ids + DOIs) and a confidence score; (c) extracted items land in a PROPOSAL QUEUE and never directly in the registry, dossiers, interactions, or packs; (d) all LLM spend is counted by the budget system against the monthly cap (/corpora/_ops/budget.json — $5 / 20000 calls). LLM API calls remain forbidden everywhere else; the app makes no LLM calls, ever, and makes no external calls beyond the D-023 GitHub allowlist. Rule 8 is restated accordingly: NO COMPONENT INVENTS SCIENCE — the app never invents science, and the extraction pipeline may only PROPOSE claims grounded in harvested sources, each with provenance and a confidence score, into the proposal queue; the owner (Igor) approves or rejects, and unapproved proposals have NO effect on any artifact (registry, dossiers, interactions, packs, cards). The Phase-2 header phrase and the 'Never do' LLM bullet were aligned to the same scope so the constitution stays non-contradictory. RATIONALE: the reader needs machine extraction to scale corpus-to-claim work beyond hand entry, but the knowledge layer's integrity depends on the same guarantees that governed harvesting — provenance, human approval, and a hard spend cap — so extraction is admitted as a PROPOSER only, never as a writer of truth. Scope of this change: .cursorrules and decisions.json only; no app code, schema, or other data files touched.

decisions.title: First-class L2 effects and a universal provenance-gated proposal store
decisions.body: L2 effects become first-class records at /effects/{mechanism_id}/{effect_id}.json, referenced by mechanism.effect_refs; L3 remains mechanism.implementations, with optional implementation.effect_id linking a realization to the scientific effect it embodies. Effects are deliberately NOT stored in implementations[].observed_effects: that field remains reserved for measured product outcomes from telemetry (baseline, treatment, sample size), while an L2 effect is a scientific phenomenon; conflating the two would corrupt the learning loop. Every proposed effect, realization, interaction, mechanism, dossier section, or segment enters through /proposals/{type}/{id}.json with non-empty source provenance, confidence, pipeline-run identity, timestamps, and an auditable pending|approved|rejected|edited status envelope. Unapproved proposals have no effect on authoritative artifacts. The owner-facing /review flow is the authorized primary knowledge-approval write surface: when implemented, its server action may use the existing GH_OPS_TOKEN GitHub path, but approval must validate the proposal and resulting artifact and commit proposal status, artifact mutation, and the append-only decision entry atomically. GitHub Actions and a recovery CLI may later call the same shared approval library; no approval logic, UI, or callers are introduced by this schema decision.

decisions.title: Owner approval runs through a provenance-verifiable Control Center with atomic batch decisions
decisions.body: The /review room is the owner's control surface for pending knowledge proposals: proposals are grouped by type and target, filtered by type/target/confidence, rendered in plain language with their projected before/after artifact changes, and cannot be approved unless every provenance reference resolves visibly. Evidence corpus records now carry a stable record_id: cr_ plus the first 24 hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 over the normalized DOI, or over normalized Unicode title plus publication year (undated when absent). Existing evidence corpora are backfilled idempotently, future evidence harvests assign ids after final deduplication, validation requires the derived id to be unique per corpus, and proposal provenance names both mechanism_id and corpus_record_id so every citation opens at /corpus/{mechanism_id}/{record_id}; that read-only page shows title, authors, year, venue, abstract, citations, categories, source identifiers, and an external DOI link. Single approve, reject, and edit-then-approve actions continue to commit proposal state, validated artifact mutations, and the append-only decision trail through GH_OPS_TOKEN in one Git Data transaction. Batch approve/reject is all-or-nothing: every selected proposal is prevalidated against the cumulative projected tree before any write; one invalid item rejects the whole batch with per-item errors and no commit. A valid batch produces one atomic commit and one decision entry, both enumerating every proposal id and outcome, preventing partial owner choices and silent mixed states. Overview queue counts are computed from proposal files. Verify with npm run backfill:corpus-record-ids (second run changes zero files), npm run test:proposals, npm run validate, npm run build, and UI acceptance against a GH_OPS_TOKEN-enabled branch.

decisions.title: Actions-only grounded extraction; descriptive realizations remain distinct from product implementations
decisions.body: STEP B1 turns harvested evidence corpora into proposals through tools/extract.ts and a dispatch-only GitHub Actions workflow. Each run has exactly one mode — effects, realizations, interactions, or dissent — and one mechanism, pack, or segment scope. Cheap-tier OpenRouter calls extract batches; the strong tier only synthesizes, deduplicates, and grades. Routing, model ids, per-token prices, per-call/per-run/monthly token caps, batch size, and prices_verified_on live in corpora/_ops/extraction.json; OPENROUTER_API_KEY is the only secret. A zero-call quote computes a conservative token/USD upper bound before a real run. Real usage is written to corpora/extraction/manifest.json and joins the existing monthly calls/USD budget rollup; prices older than 90 days are visibly stale. GROUNDING IS FAIL-CLOSED: every output citation must resolve to a supplied corpus record, match its metadata, and quote an exact normalized span from its title or abstract. Invalid or ungrounded items are counted and dropped, never softened. Deterministic identities deduplicate within the run, against actionable proposals, and against authoritative artifacts. The pipeline writes only pending proposals plus its operational manifest; owner approval remains the sole route into authoritative knowledge. REALIZATIONS AND IMPLEMENTATIONS ARE DISTINCT: realizations/{MECH-ID}/{id}.json stores descriptive, source-grounded evidence about interface/copy/flow embodiments (neutral term, what the source reports, context, provenance, confidence). mechanism.implementations remains the prescriptive, product-authored generator layer (artifact types, directives, metrics) and may cite realization_ids. Pack generation renders realizations as an evidence palette and implementations as directives, preserving evidence/instruction separation. Dissent uses the existing grounded dossier_section proposal for the dossier dissent field. Verify with mocked extraction tests, proposal tests, validation, build, then an owner dry-run and real CL-14 or MM-15 run with three manual source spot-checks, dropped-item accounting, and token/USD visibility in /ops.

decisions.title: Proposal quality gates preserve evidence without turning review into a noise queue
decisions.body: STEP B2 makes proposal admission fail-closed and review-volume bounded. Every extracted citation must resolve to an actual evidence-corpus record, carry that record's non-null DOI and exact title, and quote a normalized span from its title or abstract; fabricated or mismatched provenance is counted as dropped_ungrounded. Deterministic normalized token similarity compares compatible proposal/artifact fields using the owner-configured duplicate_similarity threshold. A match against an actionable or held proposal unions provenance and additive content into that one proposal. A match against authoritative knowledge never mutates it directly: extraction emits an operation=enrich proposal containing the projected merged artifact, and /review shows the authoritative before/after diff before the owner may approve it atomically. Enrichments with no novel provenance or material field change, and all items below limits.confidence_floor, use the non-actionable held_low_confidence status and remain visible in a collapsed review bucket. Grounded actionable proposals are ranked deterministically by confidence and identity; at most limits.max_proposals_per_mechanism new or authoritative-enrichment proposals pass per mechanism, while merges into an already-pending proposal do not consume a new queue slot. Every run records proposed, merged, dropped_ungrounded, held_low_confidence, dropped_volume_cap, and dropped_volume_cap_high_confidence (overflow at confidence >= 0.80) in its manifest, console output, and /ops summary. The quality settings remain versioned operational config under corpora/_ops/extraction.json; authoritative artifacts remain owner-gated git data. Verify with a fabricated DOI/record citation being rejected, a near-duplicate realization producing one enrichment rather than a second artifact, pending provenance union, deterministic cap tests, all run-summary counters, npm run test:extract, npm run test:proposals, npm run validate, and npm run build.

decisions.title: Saturation harvesting is resumable, balanced, and explicitly storage-gated
decisions.body: STEP C1 replaces the evidence connector's fixed one-pass depth with a deterministic saturation frontier over owner-authored evidence terms, generic search angles, and balanced relevance/recency/citation retrieval shares. OpenAlex expands both backward references and forward citations only from records that pass the metadata-only topical gate; Semantic Scholar remains relevance-only and globally serialized under D-027. A run stops when rolling novelty over the configured last K queries falls below threshold after the minimum query count, or when its call, storage-tier record, or Actions time-slice cap is reached. Every v3 harvest writes saturation_report with the query novelty curve, records added, retrieval counts, topical-confirmation rate, saturation_reached, and the honest stop reason. Multi-hour logical runs checkpoint atomically under corpora/_ops/checkpoints/evidence and resume across explicit sub-six-hour Actions slices without resetting the logical call cap; unfinished slices do not count as maturation progress. The requested full-depth harvest would create thousands of rows, so the architecture's Postgres escalation trigger has fired exactly as designed. Storage migration is now a named prerequisite for the first 3,500+ record harvest and is deliberately separate work. Until it is complete, git-backed evidence is capped at 1,000 unique records per mechanism; the bounded C1 proof must report saturation_reached false and storage_tier_record_cap if that boundary stops it. No guardrail exception is authorized.

decisions.title: Interface realization corpora preserve the manual-source licence boundary
decisions.body: STEP C2 adds mechanism-scoped interface evidence under /corpora/realizations/{mechanism_id}/records.json. Harvested records may come only from legally permitted public sources already inside the tools whitelist; the first automated path is bounded Wayback replay text derived from the existing CDX index, with raw HTML and binaries discarded. Manual connection_mode sources, including Mobbin, ScreensDesign, Page Flows, and editorial cite-but-do-not-scrape sources, are NEVER fetched by tools or the app. Their only C2 path is an authenticated owner-authored structured observation submitted through /review with source id, item locator, licence note, and owner attribution. /review may atomically commit that validated corpus observation and dispatch the Actions-only extraction workflow, but it may not call an LLM or the licensed source. Both harvested and owner records are merely corpus inputs: extraction may create pending realization proposals, and only the existing owner approval transaction may project them into /realizations. Screenshots and other binaries remain outside git in the object-store tier; C2 stores notes and locators only.

decisions.title: Sufficiency requires breadth, depth, and quality with traceable unknowns
decisions.body: STEP D1 supersedes the five-criterion sufficiency figure with three independently gated groups for every pack × segment cell. BREADTH is saturation_reached, corpus_size_vs_field_estimate, source_diversity, and recency_balance. DEPTH is effect_coverage, realization_density, interaction_coverage, and extraction_completeness. QUALITY retains dissent_completeness, grade_sufficiency, context_coverage, and freshness. A cell is green only when every criterion in all three groups clears the active maturity-stage threshold; pending proposals never count toward authoritative L2/L3 depth. Field size is not hand-guessed: OpenAlex meta.count and Semantic Scholar total are persisted per query, and the connector computes a reproducible sample-overlap-adjusted union estimate across distinct API/query universes. analyzer.config.yaml may override an obviously inflated estimate only with an explicit estimate, rationale, and review date; generated cell metadata records when that override is active. Missing upstream totals or reader history are NULL/unmeasured explicit gaps, never numeric zero. Successful Actions-only extraction maintains corpora/extraction/coverage.json as an exact cumulative record-id ledger, letting extraction_completeness intersect what the reader processed with the current eligible corpora. Every criterion records its repository source paths in the matrix. Pipeline gaps are kept distinct from connector harvest and owner-only structural work so the maturation loop cannot dispatch the wrong filler. The cockpit states that prior green figures are superseded; the expected sharp initial fall is the honest consequence of measuring depth for the first time.

decisions.title: Gap routing dispatches the filler that can close each criterion
decisions.body: STEP D2 extends the gap planner from harvest-versus-authoring into three explicit routes. Breadth plus grade and freshness create deep evidence-harvest tasks. Effect coverage, realization density, extraction completeness, and grounded dissent create deduplicated mechanism-scoped Actions-only extraction tasks; extraction-completeness routing follows the corpus kind actually present. Interaction and context coverage remain structural because they require owner judgment, and evidence-exhausted cells retain their explicit alternative-fill handoff. The generated analysis/extraction-queue.json is ranked and capped, but every task is quoted again immediately before execution against corpora/_ops/extraction.json and the shared monthly USD/call rollup; blocked or unconfigured tasks defer and are never forced. The weekly maturation workflow runs allowed harvest and extraction work, regenerates all queues after re-scoring, records both automated and human routes, and writes extraction only to pending proposals plus the exact reader ledger. Owner approval remains the sole path from proposals to authoritative knowledge. This routing deliberately makes the authoring queue small: it contains only gaps automation cannot genuinely close.

decisions.title: Interaction and agency is a first-class pack-scoped system
decisions.body: STEP E1 adds non-cross-cutting L0 node S8 Interaction & agency and eight owner-authored candidate stubs: CO-19 competence and mastery, AU-20 autonomy and control, FB-21 feedback and responsiveness, ER-22 error recovery and forgiveness, DE-23 defaults and effort, FL-24 flow and challenge balance, RR-25 recognition over recall, and AE-26 aesthetic-usability effect. Their supplied oneliners, evidence terms, grades, and pinned works are preserved verbatim. The owner explicitly assigns S8 candidates to core-ux, onboarding, first-value, paywall-conversion, and retention-billing in pack-map; these are judgments, not derived science. A declared candidate dependency fails closed immediately: analyzer scores authoritative full members only, forces the cell red, and records the exact seed path and reason that the member is still a candidate. Candidate pendency is not evidence exhaustion. The gap planner may harvest a candidate's owner-provided terms, but generated pack guidance omits every candidate until dossier-gated promotion, preventing partial unapproved S8 content from leaking into team guidance. The matrix remains the 180-cell pack/perception grid; 75 cells across the five owner-selected packs now carry candidate-pendency traces.

decisions.title: S8 is populated end-to-end by the pipeline; the machine drafts, the owner decides
decisions.body: STEP E2 makes the automated chain able to compose first-time L1 records and dossiers, so no S8 content is authored outside the system. New extraction modes mechanism and dossier draft a whole artifact from the harvested evidence corpus: the cheap tier extracts sectioned grounded claims, the strong tier composes exactly one draft per mechanism, and every claim carries corpus record ids, DOIs, verbatim quote loci, and a confidence score. Seed content (name, oneliner-derived terms, pinned evidence) is preserved verbatim; ids, slug, version, level, parent, dossier_ref, telemetry, and prior_weight (a fixed conservative grade-to-weight map) are code-filled, never invented. A new dossier proposal type carries five axes of {score, rationale, provenance}; an axis the pipeline cannot ground is emitted unscored (nulls, empty provenance) and flagged for owner judgement — never guessed — and /review blocks approval until the owner edits a score and rationale in. total, verdict, decided_by, and date are absent from the draft by design: projectDossier computes the total, derives the verdict from the admission gate (total >= 11 with evidence >= 2 and safety >= 2 gives incubating, else hold), and stamps the deciding owner at approval. A dossier proposal can never auto-approve. Mechanism projection now derives lifecycle_status from the approved dossier verdict when the dossier exists (including one applied earlier in the same atomic batch — dossier paths sort before mechanism paths), because the verdict IS the lifecycle decision and statuses are computed from data, not proposed. The D-023 write surface widens by one action pair: /ops dispatches extract.yml dry-run for a deterministic token/USD quote, polls the run by dispatch_id, downloads the quote artifact, and only after explicit owner confirmation dispatches the real run; the workflow re-runs the quote gate itself and fails closed on any cap. Model routing configured with live OpenRouter prices verified 2026-07-23: cheap tier google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite ($0.25/M in, $1.50/M out) — flash-class, cheap enough to read whole corpora batch-by-batch with grounded-quote discipline enforced by post-hoc verification, so per-claim quality risk is caught by the grounding gate rather than paid for twice; strong tier anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 ($2/M in, $10/M out) — frontier-class synthesis where composition quality (merging, conservative grading, one-draft coherence) matters most and volume is one call per mechanism. Both ids and prices live in corpora/_ops/extraction.json with prices_verified_on, so the choice is reviewable and swappable without archaeology. The eight S8 candidates joined the evidence connector targets. npm run report -- shelf=S8 computes the per-mechanism population report (corpus size, saturation status, proposals by type and status, approval rate, record and dossier completeness) from repository files only. Realization corpora for S8 are honestly empty until wayback targets or owner observations exist (D-081); the report shows that rather than faking coverage.

decisions.title: Live operations view: run artifacts plus a published progress heartbeat, no new infrastructure
decisions.body: STEP F1 adds a live operations view at the top of /ops that shows what the fleet is doing and when: jobs running now (harvest, extraction, analysis) with phase, elapsed time, progress against caps, and current spend; recent runs with their outcomes and (for evidence) the saturation report; the next scheduled runs; and the four queues (harvest, extraction, review, authoring) with counts. Every value is COMPUTED (rule 2) — from in-flight Actions runs, committed manifests' run_history and saturation_report, the analysis/*-queue.json files, the proposal store, and the pending evidence checkpoints — with a designed empty state when a source is absent (rule 15). Two liveness layers, both read-only and within the D-023 poll surface: (1) the app lists queued/in-progress runs of harvest.yml, connectors.yml, extract.yml, and maturation.yml via the Actions API and reads each run's jobs for the current phase (step name) and elapsed time; (2) long jobs report progress CHECKPOINTS, not just start/end — the evidence connector writes a standardized heartbeat after every query and extract.ts after every LLM batch, to a gitignored working file (.ops-progress/run-progress.json). tools/progress-publisher.ts wraps the long step and force-pushes that single file to a dedicated ops-progress git ref every ~2 minutes as an ORPHAN single-file commit, so main history stays clean and — because the orphan tree carries no .github/workflows — heartbeat pushes trigger no CI. The app reads the heartbeat via the Contents API with ref=ops-progress and matches it to the in-flight run by GITHUB_RUN_ID; a heartbeat with no matching active run is ignored. This widens the D-023 read surface by exactly three read-only calls (list workflow runs, read a run's jobs, read the ops-progress ref) and adds no write path: the app never harvests, never writes the heartbeat, and only the Actions job (contents: write via the checkout token) publishes it. No database, queue, or new service (rule 5); the heartbeat is a file in the repo, just on a side ref. The shape is documented at corpora/_ops/run-progress.schema.json and mirrored by lib/types.ts RunProgress; it never lives on main. When GH_OPS_TOKEN is absent the live section degrades to an honest empty state while the file-based recent/queues/schedule sections still render.

decisions.title: Paid extraction is capped, model-accounted, estimated first, and paused fail-closed
decisions.body: STEP F2 establishes the paid-era operating envelope without adding infrastructure. Harvest and OpenRouter extraction share a $100 UTC-month USD cap and the existing 20,000-call cap; extraction additionally keeps a 1,000,000-token monthly guard and a conservative 50,000-token hard cap per run. Every successful extraction manifest cost block records total calls, input tokens, output tokens, and estimated USD plus a per-tier breakdown naming the exact configured model and its calls, tokens, and cost; cockpit rollups remain computed from those committed manifests. Every extraction path computes and evaluates a deterministic quote before any model call. The manual /ops path still exposes the quote artifact for owner confirmation, while direct and scheduled paths re-quote fail-closed immediately before execution. The cockpit enters an explicit warning state when either monthly USD or extraction-token usage reaches 80%, and an explicit paused state when either cap is exhausted; scheduled extraction is then paused until the next UTC month or an owner-reviewed cap change. A denied scheduled quote is recorded as a pause with a concise budget reason and is never forced. Prices and model routing remain versioned in corpora/_ops/extraction.json, knowledge remains owner-gated, and no runtime database, queue, or app-side LLM call is introduced.

decisions.title: A blocked extraction quote is an informative result, not a failed dry-run job
decisions.body: The /ops extraction estimate for effects/SC-06 reported 'the quote job failed at step Compute deterministic extraction quote' with no actionable detail. The failed run's log showed the quote step had in fact computed a complete, valid quote — corpus corpora/evidence/SC-06.json found, corpora/_ops/extraction.json present and prices current, no OPENROUTER_API_KEY touched, inputs correctly resolved — whose verdict was simply allowed=false because the upper-bound estimate (646,907 tokens) exceeds the 50,000-token per-run cap (D-087). None of the four suspected causes (missing corpus, malformed config, key requirement, input mismatch) applied. The real cause was in tools/extract.ts main(): the quote command exited 1 whenever the verdict was not-allowed, reddening the dry-run quote job; because the upload-artifact step had no if:always(), the skipped upload dropped quote.json, so /ops fell back to lib/github.ts getRunFailureSummary, which reported only the job/step name. The fix separates a computed-but-blocked verdict from a genuine compute error: the quote command now exits 0 whenever it successfully computes a quote and exits non-zero on a blocked verdict ONLY under an explicit enforce=true argument, which just the real run's pre-flight budget gate passes (keeping D-087 fail-closed before any OPENROUTER_API_KEY process starts). The dry-run quote job runs without enforce and its upload-artifact step is if:always(), so quote.json always reaches /ops and the UI renders the reason ('This run is blocked … upper-bound 646907 tokens exceeds per-run cap 50000') from the existing quote panel. The quote/run path now also runs the shared validateExtractionOpsConfig guard before building a quote, so a missing, stale, or malformed extraction.json field fails with an explicit named message (e.g. 'limits.per_run_tokens must be an integer ≥ 1') instead of silently driving the estimator to NaN. Finally getRunFailureSummary now best-effort fetches the failed job's raw log and appends the real thrown error line (capped, timestamp- and noise-stripped) so operators see WHAT broke, not just which step. No new infrastructure, no widening of the write surface, knowledge stays owner-gated.

decisions.title: Extraction is incremental and funnel-filtered
decisions.body: Extraction is incremental and funnel-filtered; caps are respected by reading in ranked slices, not raised to swallow whole corpora. Before any model call, the reader removes records already terminal for the requested mode and applies a deterministic title-plus-abstract topical gate derived from the mechanism's versioned evidence terms; owner-pinned evidence always survives. Topically confirmed records are ranked ahead of the relevant tail, with citation count and stable record id providing deterministic order. Records that fail the gate are recorded as skipped_irrelevant and never sent to either model. The quote and run share one planner that reserves both cheap extraction and strong synthesis before admitting each ranked record, selecting only the largest prefix whose conservative upper bound fits the unchanged 50,000-token per-run cap. A run with relevant records left is a successful resumable slice: it commits proposals and exact per-mode record state, records manifest status partial with warnings.capped=true, and the next run reads only records without a terminal state for that mode. The coverage ledger retains its aggregate processed_record_ids projection so analyzer extraction_completeness counts both model-read and cheaply triaged records, while per-mode state prevents one extraction task (for example effects) from suppressing another (for example dissent). True configuration, monthly-budget, API, and minimum-record-fit failures remain fail-closed. No cap, app-side LLM permission, knowledge write surface, or owner approval boundary is widened.

decisions.title: Extraction slices consume the real cap and report their funnel on /ops
decisions.body: The first paid extraction run (effects/SC-06) concluded green with 'slice completed - 0 proposals' after sending only 5 of 166 eligible records to the model, then stopping. The pre-filter was not the cause (it skipped a modest 23 records): the token estimator in tools/extract.ts counted prompt UTF-8 bytes 1:1 as tokens (~4.5x overshoot) and reserved the strong synthesis input at batches x 6000 x 4 tokens, so roughly 40,000 of the 50,000-token per-run cap was consumed by fixed overhead before any record was counted. The run predicted 46,797 tokens but actually spent 3,036 - a ~15x overshoot that starved every slice to a handful of records and would have needed ~29 more paid runs to finish one corpus. Three fixes, widening no boundary. First, the estimator (and the runtime per-call guard, which must agree with it) now counts input as ceil(bytes/4) tokens and reserves strong input at the sum of the cheap output reserves capped by the strong tier ceiling; the quote stays a conservative upper bound with honest units and the 50,000-token cap is unchanged. Second, runExtraction now processes multiple ranked slices in the SAME Actions job: after each slice it re-plans against the in-memory coverage delta with per_run_tokens reduced to the actual remaining headroom, and continues while relevant records remain and headroom is left, stopping when the corpus is exhausted, the cap is consumed, or the next record cannot fit. A run that reads only pre-filtered noise now advances instead of reporting a misleading zero; the manifest persists the full funnel (records_eligible, records_relevant, records_processed, records_skipped_irrelevant, candidates, records_remaining) alongside the five gate counters, and status stays partial with warnings.capped=true only when relevant records genuinely remain. Third, the operator sees results where they work: the terminal progress heartbeat now carries a summary object with the five counters plus the funnel, and getLiveOpsSnapshotAction surfaces a just-finished extraction run from that heartbeat in /ops recent runs the moment the job ends - deduped against the committed manifest row within a ten-minute window - so no one must open GitHub Actions to learn what a run produced. Recent-run rows and the extraction quality panel render the counters and funnel from the heartbeat summary or committed params. This stays Actions-only, adds no infrastructure or dependency, makes no app-side LLM call, and leaves the knowledge write surface and owner approval boundary untouched.

decisions.title: Review schema assets are explicit server-function dependencies
decisions.body: The first-class effect and realization schemas required by D-076/D-078 already existed at effects/effect.schema.json and realizations/realization.schema.json and matched their decided artifact shapes. /review approval nevertheless failed on Vercel with ENOENT for effects/effect.schema.json because lib/proposals.ts loads validator schemas through a runtime-computed fs path; Next.js output file tracing could not infer those dynamic file dependencies, so the deployed review server function omitted schemas that were present in git. next.config.mjs now explicitly includes every schema consumed by the approval validator in the /review trace, preserving schemaRoot-based filesystem validation and the atomic proposal/artifact/decision transaction. The SC-06 extraction run was not affected by that deployment-only omission: Actions ran from the repository checkout and reported two candidates under dropped_ungrounded. However, extraction also placed every Ajv failure in that same bucket and discarded it without diagnostics, making the run unable to distinguish grounding failures from schema failures. Extraction summaries and terminal heartbeats therefore add failed_validation as a separate quality counter, manifests raise validation_failed, /ops renders the counter, and each failed schema validation prints its Ajv errors. No validation gate is weakened and no app write surface is widened.

decisions.title: Proposal realization-ze-07-language-learning-landing-hero-b8d0d1b852e0 approved
decisions.body: Owner owner approved realization proposal realization-ze-07-language-learning-landing-hero-b8d0d1b852e0 for ZE-07. The validated proposal status and authoritative projection were committed atomically.

decisions.title: Extractor tolerates response form but remains strict on content
decisions.body: Extractor is tolerant to response form, strict on content; single malformed responses cost a batch, never a run. OpenRouter calls use strict mode-specific JSON Schema with the exact {items: [...]} envelope and require a provider endpoint that supports the requested parameters. The system prompt repeats the envelope explicitly. Responses are parsed strictly first, then may recover from a markdown code fence, a bare top-level array, or the first balanced valid JSON block in surrounding prose; every recovery logs the exact model, tier, and strategy. Recovery changes form only: item grounding, confidence, proposal schemas, deduplication, and owner approval remain fail-closed. An unrecoverable response increments the existing failed_validation sixth counter and processing continues with the next cheap batch or mechanism synthesis. Failed records are excluded from committed reader coverage and from same-run replanning, so extraction completeness stays honest without retry loops. Transport, API, usage-accounting, and budget failures still abort immediately. A run fails for response validation only when every attempted response batch fails; any successfully parsed batch allows a partial or successful run to persist its honest counters.

decisions.title: OpenRouter response strictness follows verified endpoint capability
decisions.body: D-094 narrows D-093's request-routing statement after the first CG-05 verification run returned OpenRouter 404 before inference: google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite advertised response_format but no routed endpoint accepted strict json_schema with require_parameters=true. Response capability is therefore explicit per extraction tier in corpora/_ops/extraction.json. The cheap Gemini tier uses response_format=json_object plus the exact-envelope system prompt and the same tolerant parser; the strong Claude Sonnet 5 tier uses strict mode-specific json_schema and provider.require_parameters=true. validateExtractionOpsConfig rejects missing or unknown response_format values, so changing a model requires an owner-reviewed capability choice rather than a hardcoded model-name guess. Content remains equally fail-closed in both modes through grounding and proposal validation.

decisions.title: Claude extraction routing currently uses OpenRouter JSON mode
decisions.body: D-095 further narrows D-094 from live endpoint evidence. The capability-aware CG-05 rerun completed both Gemini cheap batches (31 records, 2 calls, 13,220 input and 697 output tokens) and reached phase composing CG-05, then OpenRouter returned the same no-compatible-endpoint 404 for Claude Sonnet 5 with strict json_schema plus require_parameters=true. The configured strong tier therefore also uses response_format=json_object for the current route. The extractor retains tested json_schema support and will require a compatible endpoint when a future verified tier is configured for it; current strictness comes from JSON mode, the exact-envelope system prompt, tolerant form normalization, and unchanged fail-closed content gates. OpenRouter HTTP errors now name model and tier so future capability failures are attributable without heartbeat forensics.

decisions.title: Saturation checkpoints are identified by mechanism and run fingerprint
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: the scheduled weekly maturation run 30258583117 (2026-07-27T10:34Z) failed after 4m36s and opened ops issue #1. Harvest of DE-23 and CO-19 exited 1 with 'stale saturation checkpoint ... terms, config, or base corpus changed' at 0 api_calls, on the first attempt and on the D-022 retry alike. ROOT CAUSE: checkpointPath keyed a checkpoint by mechanism id alone while runFingerprint mixes in the segment-qualified terms. The maturation queue harvests one mechanism once per segment, so the second segment read the first segment's file and readCheckpoint threw. The log confirms DE-23 ran at queue position 4 with b2b-enterprise terms and again at position 13 with subscription-retention terms, and CO-19 at positions 3 and 11. An OpenAlex 48,197s upstream cooldown made nearly every target write a checkpoint that week, which is what turned a latent collision into a fatal one. FIX (applied): a checkpoint is addressed by mechanism AND fingerprint, filename <mechanism>.<first 12 chars of fingerprint>.json. An address with no file is a clean fresh slice; the hard throw is reserved for a file whose contents disagree with their own fingerprint address, so the D-022 review-before-delete contract survives for genuinely corrupt files. The one existing CL-14 checkpoint was renamed to its fingerprint address, preserving its resumable slice (cursor 70/1090, 92 calls spent). Every consumer of the directory was updated: the maturation defer step and both queue-continuation steps cut the mechanism id at the first dot and carry the fingerprint into the dispatch id so per-segment continuations stay distinct; harvest.yml globs for any slice of its target; countCheckpointResumes reports distinct mechanisms so the /ops tile is not inflated by a multi-segment mechanism; and tools/validate.ts now requires the filename to agree with both mechanism_id and fingerprint. VERIFICATION: tools/connectors/evidence.test.ts proves two segment-qualified term sets for one mechanism yield different fingerprints, different checkpoint paths in the same directory, mutual incompatibility, and a clean null (no throw) for an unwritten address; a second test covers a changed base corpus. Confirmed operationally when the next weekly run passes its harvest step with both DE-23 segments queued.

decisions.title: Analysis is committed independently of harvest outcome
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: analysis/sufficiency-matrix.json and all three queues were a week old (generated 2026-07-23T09:04Z) even though the Monday cron did fire, and analysis/maturation-log.json had no 2026-07-27 entry at all — the surface looked as if the schedule had never run. ROOT CAUSE: 'Analyze sufficiency and plan gaps' runs before any evidence is fetched and had already computed a fresh matrix and queues, but eight downstream steps including 'Commit maturation results if changed' were gated on if: steps.harvest.outputs.failed != 'true'. The D-096 harvest collision therefore discarded the entire week's computed analysis with the runner, and the partial corpora that succeeding targets had already written were thrown away too. FIX (applied): the gate now follows the actual dependency. Steps that genuinely need harvested evidence keep it — defer checkpointed tasks, count low-novelty harvests, record the harvest ledger, run extraction. Re-analysis, the job summary, the log entry, the commit, and the checkpoint continuations run regardless of harvest outcome. Pack regeneration is gated on a cell actually flipping green rather than on harvest success, so a committed matrix can never claim green from a stale pack export (invariants 2 and 3). An empty extraction plan is created in the always-run gate step so the downstream steps read a real file when extraction is skipped. The job still goes red through 'Fail the job on persistent failure' and still opens the deduplicated ops issue; the commit message is marked '(partial — harvest failed)', the job summary leads with a PARTIAL WEEK notice, and the log entry carries harvest_failed so /maturation reads 'no cell changed status this week — harvest failed, so no gap was attempted' instead of presenting a degraded week as a clean one. VERIFICATION: a deliberately failed harvest, or a re-run of the DE-23 scenario, must still produce a commit refreshing the matrix and queues, with the partial week visible on /maturation and the job still red.

decisions.title: Ungrounded extraction drops are attributed per reason
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: the four post-tolerance extraction runs produced 30 candidates and 0 proposals. dropped_ungrounded equalled candidates every single time (RE-10 10/10, FR-11 10/10, CG-05 8/8, SC-06 2/2) with failed_validation 0, so the D-093 tolerance fix demonstrably works and Ajv rejects nothing — every candidate dies at the grounding gate instead. effects/ still contains only its schema, which is why effect_coverage is 0 across all 180 cells and no cell can leave red. ROOT CAUSE: not yet determined, and deliberately not guessed. groundedProvenance and lib/proposal-quality.groundingErrors apply four distinct checks — unknown corpus record id, record.doi === null, exact title equality, and an exact normalized-substring quote match — and every failure incremented one opaque counter, so the committed data cannot say which check fires. The DOI-null rejection (any DOI-less OpenAlex or S2 record) and the exact substring quote match are the leading suspects. This is the same class of blind spot D-093 fixed for Ajv failures; the bucket was still too coarse. FIX: the gate itself is unchanged — no candidate that was admitted is now refused and none that was refused is now admitted, per rule 8. Instrumentation only: groundingOutcome returns a discriminated result carrying one of nine reasons (no_citations, malformed_citation, unknown_record_id, quote_not_in_source, wrong_corpus_kind, doi_unresolved, title_mismatch, provenance_mismatch, proposal_not_built), groundedProvenance is now the boolean-shaped view of the same decision, and the existing per-error strings from groundingErrors are classified rather than rewritten. Run stats carry dropped_ungrounded_reasons beside the unchanged total, the first five concrete offenders per mechanism are logged with record id and failing check, and the breakdown reaches /ops through run-progress.schema.json, lib/types.ts and lib/ops.ts. The /ops funnel renders the causes when present and an explicit 'cause not attributed — this run predates the per-reason breakdown' state otherwise, never zeros. The reason list is declared once in lib/types.ts and tools/validate.ts fails if it drifts from the schema. The decision about whether to change any gate is DEFERRED until a real run names the dominant cause. VERIFICATION: tools/extract.test.ts asserts each reason is returned by its own refusal path, that counts are attributed per key, that they always sum to dropped_ungrounded, and that a clean run carries no breakdown field at all. Operationally, one owner-dispatched extraction run from /ops whose funnel names the dominant reason; that reading then drives a separate decision.

decisions.title: Extraction spend is recorded even when a run fails
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: runs 30102079781 and 30102271340 called OpenRouter, burned tokens, and then failed on a strong-tier 404. Because 'Commit proposals and extraction accounting' only runs on success, their spend is absent from corpora/extraction/manifest.json and therefore invisible to the monthly cap — roughly $0.0044 of real spend that month-to-date does not know about. ROOT CAUSE: the gate was never the problem and is not changed here. The cap is already config-driven and hard-enforced in code (corpora/_ops/budget.json monthly_caps.usd 100 and calls 20000; corpora/_ops/extraction.json limits.per_run_tokens 50000 and monthly_tokens 1000000), enforced by a deliberately separate quote step with enforce=true before any process holding OPENROUTER_API_KEY can call a model (D-087), and it demonstrably works — run 30017377589 was blocked pre-flight at estimated_usd 0.170594 and exited 1 without calling a model. The hole is the COUNTER: computeBudgetSnapshot derives month-to-date from computeMonthlyRollup over committed corpus manifests, and the manifest was only ever written on a clean finish, so a run that died had no cost block to count. FIX (applied): tools/extract.ts persists the manifest run-history entry with its cost block after every completed batch and once more on the way out of a throw, marking that entry status failed. Entries are keyed by the run's start timestamp and mergeExtractionRunHistory replaces rather than appends, so repeated in-flight writes cannot double-count one run; writeManifest tolerates a coverage file that does not exist yet; and a failure to record accounting is logged but never masks the error ending the run. extract.yml adds a 'Commit extraction accounting even on failure' step with if: always(), scoped to corpora/extraction only — proposals stay fail-closed, and the step discards the failed run's partial proposals and re-runs npm run validate before committing, so an invalid manifest can never land. No cap VALUES change in this pass. VERIFICATION: tools/extract.test.ts asserts a run that dies mid-way still yields a failed run-history entry whose cost.estimated_usd, api_calls, and token counts are non-zero, that a second write for the same run supersedes the first while a genuinely different run is preserved, and that summing the history gives the figure the monthly rollup would read. computeMonthlyRollup counts every history entry regardless of status, so such an entry does reach the cap.

decisions.title: Evidence checkpoints are fingerprinted, and the validator had to learn the naming
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: main at 2a07e0f failed npm run validate. Commit 2a07e0f added corpora/_ops/checkpoints/evidence/CL-14.fb7776284875.json but neither deleted the superseded CL-14.json nor shipped the validator that understands the new name. The committed validator asserted basename(file, '.json') === value.mechanism_id, and basename('CL-14.fb7776284875.json', '.json') is 'CL-14.fb7776284875', which is not 'CL-14'. So the new file failed a rule written for the old naming, and the stale file remained as a second checkpoint for the same mechanism. ROOT CAUSE: a naming change landed in the data before the rule that validates it. DECISION: checkpoint filenames are <mechanism_id>.<fingerprint>.json, where the fingerprint identifies the corpus state the checkpoint describes; the validator parses the stem up to the first dot and requires that to equal mechanism_id, and a mechanism may have at most one checkpoint file. The stale CL-14.json is deleted rather than kept, because two checkpoints for one mechanism have no defined precedence. RULE: a schema or naming change and the validator that enforces it land in the same commit. A red tip is not a pending task, it is a broken invariant, and the fix is not to relax the rule.

decisions.title: importance cannot rank effects tasks — all 18 tie
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: the authoring queue's importance score has no discriminating power for mode=effects. All 18 effects tasks score exactly 1.5, so ordering falls through to the tiebreak, mechanism.localeCompare, and the queue is alphabetical by mechanism id. A ranking that cannot rank is not a ranking; it is an alphabetical list wearing a score. CONSEQUENCE: the operator picking 'the top task' is picking the alphabetically first mechanism, and the score's presence actively misleads by implying a judgement was made. DECISION: recorded as a known defect, not silently patched with a plausible-looking weight. OPEN QUESTION, deliberately unresolved: the natural discriminator is corpus readiness — how many of a mechanism's records carry BOTH a DOI and an abstract, expressed absolutely and as a share of the corpus — because that is what determines whether extraction can ground anything at all. That needs measuring across all 18 before it becomes a term, since a readiness weight that correlates with corpus SIZE rather than corpus quality would just reorder the same non-ranking. Until then /maturation must not present importance as an ordering for effects.

decisions.title: 165 versus 180: two denominators, both correct, only one labelled
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: /maturation reports 165 while the analyzer counts 180 for what reads as the same coverage figure. Neither is wrong. 165 is the pack grid, 11 packs x 15 segments. 180 is 12 x 15, adding the perception row that D-067 deliberately excludes from the pack figure because perception is not a pack. ROOT CAUSE: two legitimate denominators presented as one unlabelled number, so a reader cannot tell which population a percentage is over, and the two surfaces appear to disagree about a fact they agree on. DECISION: every coverage figure names its denominator at the point of display — either both surfaces adopt one denominator, or each states which of the two it is using. An unlabelled ratio is not an honest status (rule 2): a computed number is only honest if the reader can tell what it was computed over.

decisions.title: per_run_tokens truncates the plan; the truncation must be reported
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: per_run_tokens is enforced by TRUNCATING the extraction plan, not by refusing the run. A run that cannot fit its slice silently reads fewer records and reports success. The records it dropped to fit are invisible, so a run that covered a third of its scope and a run that covered all of it look identical in the report. ROOT CAUSE: truncation is the right enforcement mechanism — refusing would make a large scope permanently undispatchable — but it changes what the run MEANT without changing what the run SAID. DECISION: the count of records the planner dropped by truncation is surfaced in every run report and every quote, next to records_selected and records_remaining. Truncation stays; silence about it does not. A cap that quietly changes the question is worse than one that answers a smaller question out loud.

decisions.title: Provenance was authored by a pass that never saw the source
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: four consecutive runs (CG-05, FR-11, RE-10, SC-06) dropped 100% of candidates as ungrounded — 30 for 30 — with no proposal produced and roughly $0.12 spent. ROOT CAUSE, established by reading the code and not by hypothesis: strongPrompt sent only CANDIDATES, never RECORDS, and the grounding gate ran solely on the strong pass's output. A model that has never seen an abstract cannot reproduce a verbatim span of it, so 'copy the citations verbatim from the candidates' was a prompt instruction with nothing enforcing it and the gate correctly refused every item. The gate was right. The authorship was wrong. A zero-spend control (tools/replay-grounding.ts synth) confirms this from the other direction: candidates grounded BY CONSTRUCTION from real CL-14 records pass the gate 10 for 10, and the mutation matrix shows the matcher tolerates every mangling axis it was accused of — hyphen variants, curly quotes, ligatures, non-breaking space, doubled whitespace, ellipsis, edge punctuation — because normalizeQualityText folds them all. The matcher was never the weak link. DECISION: structural provenance. Only the pass that reads a record may establish provenance for it, and it does so mechanically: lib/span-locate.ts resolves the quote to raw character offsets [start, end) using the gate's own normalization, and from then on the quote is DERIVED by slicing the record at those offsets — the model's string is discarded. The synthesis pass receives the claim plus opaque refs (p1, p2, ...) and no quote text, record ids, or offsets; its response schema offers provenance_refs and nothing else, with additionalProperties false, and refs are validated as a subset of exactly what that item was supplied. So the worst a synthesis model can do is name a span already verified, or name nothing. Offsets are never asked of a model — models are unreliable at character arithmetic, so the reading pass still emits a quote string and the CODE locates it. The gate is untouched: nothing previously admitted is now refused and nothing previously refused is now admitted (rule 8). What changed is who is allowed to write the string the gate inspects.

decisions.title: Cheap-pass candidates were discarded ungated, with no counter
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: only the strong pass's output was ever gated. Cheap-pass candidates flowed into synthesis ungated and any that synthesis dropped left no trace, so a valid extraction lost between the passes was indistinguishable from one never extracted. dropped_ungrounded counted one pass and was read as if it described the pipeline. ROOT CAUSE: the funnel had two stages and one counter. DECISION: groundingOutcome runs on cheap candidates too, before synthesis, and the funnel splits into cheap and strong throughout — ExtractionStats, run-progress.schema.json, lib/ops.ts, and the /ops surface. dropped_ungrounded keeps its old meaning as the total, and the two per-pass counters sum to it, so no existing figure changes meaning. Both per-pass candidate counts are written unconditionally, including at zero: presence-at-zero is what lets /ops tell 'gated, nothing lost' from 'this run predates the split', and a fabricated zero for an older run would be a measurement claim about something never measured. Gating the cheap pass admits nothing new — it refuses earlier what the strong gate would have refused later, and now says which pass lost it.

decisions.title: Cost attribution requires a usage block; pre-routing rejections are zero
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: runs 30102079781 and 30102271340 (2026-07-24 14:41:26Z and 14:44:08Z) are absent from corpora/extraction/manifest.json. Both died on their first strong-tier call with a routing 404. ROOT CAUSE: cost is derived from the usage block in an OpenRouter response. A 404 means no provider accepted the request, so no model ran, no completion exists, and no usage block was returned — the spend is unattributable BY DESIGN, not by an accounting bug. The Actions logs cannot fill the gap either: the error format at that commit was 'OpenRouter ${status}: ${text}' with no model or tier field. DECISION: both runs are recorded as status failed with cost, tokens, and api_calls all zero and error 'routing_404 — no model invoked, no usage block', keyed by run start timestamp so mergeExtractionRunHistory cannot double-count them. Zero is the accurate value for a request no provider accepted, not a placeholder. An earlier $0.0044 figure was arithmetic, not an observation, and is deliberately NOT written: an estimate in a cost ledger is worse than a documented gap, because the ledger's whole value is that its numbers were measured. openrouter.ai/api/v1/generation stays off the whitelist — rule 12 does not move for a fraction of a cent against a $99.88 remaining cap. LIMITATION, recorded rather than worked around: any request rejected before routing is permanently unattributable.

decisions.title: Send a parameter only where the model advertises it
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: the two 404s above, and a live landmine. provider.require_parameters true instructs OpenRouter to route only to a provider that honours EVERY parameter in the request — a fail-closed guard, and the right one, since the alternative is a provider silently ignoring the response format. But temperature 0 was sent unconditionally, and anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 does not advertise temperature. The intersection is empty, so there is no eligible provider and the request 404s with 'no endpoints found' before any model is invoked. Commit 973b069 enabled json_schema with require_parameters on both tiers; the next commit made it config-driven but left the strong tier on json_schema; the commit three minutes later dropped to json_object and CG-05 immediately succeeded. The config that ships today works only because json_object skips the provider block — the moment json_schema returns to the strong tier, and D-104's strict provenance schema is exactly why it must, the 404 returns with it. DECISION: capability is declared per tier in corpora/_ops/extraction.json as a supports block (temperature, structured_outputs), and openRouterSamplingOptions omits any parameter the tier does not advertise. require_parameters stays true — omitting the parameter is the fix, loosening routing is not. Capability is declared rather than probed because the pipeline is file-based (rule 12) and a runtime capability lookup would be a new endpoint; validateExtractionOpsConfig rejects a tier asking for json_schema without structured_outputs, and tools/openrouter-preflight.ts proves the declaration by sending the EXACT production parameter set with max_tokens 1 to each tier for roughly $0.0001, in Actions only. Sharing openRouterRequestBody with the real path is the point: a preflight that approximated the parameters could pass while production 404s.

decisions.title: dispatch_id is recorded in the manifest, not inferred from a run name
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: linking a manifest entry back to the dispatch that produced it required findRunByDispatchId, which substring-matches a workflow run NAME. A run name is a display string: editing run-name, or dispatching two ids that share a prefix, silently misattributes spend, and nothing fails when it does. Reconstructing which commit configured the two 404 runs meant reading dispatch ids out of run titles. DECISION: buildExtractionManifestRun records dispatch_id from OPS_DISPATCH_ID and github_run_id from GITHUB_RUN_ID on every entry it writes. Live polling still matches on the run name, because it necessarily runs before any manifest exists; everything after the run reads the recorded field. Both are nullable and optional: absent means written before D-108, null means the run carried no correlation id, and those are different facts that stay distinguishable rather than collapsing into one ambiguous blank.

decisions.title: Grounding pass rate is arithmetic, not evidence, and is not a quality figure
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: since D-104 the grounding gate cannot fail by construction. The quote a proposal carries is a SLICE the pipeline cut out of the source text itself (anchorCitations, resolveRefs), and a slice is a substring of its source as a matter of arithmetic, not of fact. A pass rate computed over slices therefore measures the slicing code, not the model, and it will read 100% no matter what the model claimed. Reporting it as quality invites exactly the inference it cannot support: that a high number means the extractions are sound. DECISION: run reports must not cite grounding pass rate as a quality metric. The gate keeps running — it still catches unknown record ids, DOI-unresolved records, title mismatches, malformed citations, and stale spans, and those are real refusals worth counting — but the pass rate itself is reported as a mechanical check, not as evidence about content. The risk that remains is that the CLAIM does not follow from the cited span: the quote is genuinely in the paper and the sentence built on top of it still misstates what the paper found. NO automated check in this repo covers that, and none is proposed here, because a check that cannot detect the failure would be worse than an acknowledged gap — it would launder the gap into a green tick. The remedy is the owner reading proposals against their sources by hand, which is why /review links every provenance item to /corpus/{mechanism_id}/{corpus_record_id}. Reports state the uncovered risk by name rather than filling the space with a number that happens to be measurable.

decisions.title: Evidence provenance persists a source span and the hash of the text it was resolved against
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: the pipeline knew exactly where each quote came from and threw the information away. locateSpan resolved character offsets, SpanLedger held them for the length of the run, and the proposal was written with the quote text alone. Verifying a stored quote afterwards therefore meant SEARCHING the source for it again — re-deriving the location from the quote, which is circular: it can only confirm that the string appears somewhere, and it cannot distinguish a faithful slice from a phrase that happens to occur elsewhere in the abstract. Criterion (d) of the CL-14 validation asks for the opposite direction: re-slice the stored offsets and see whether the bytes come back identical. DECISION: source_span {start, end, source_text_sha256} is persisted on the evidence provenance item in all three schemas (proposals, effects, realizations) and in EvidenceProvenanceItem. Offsets index the string lib/proposal-quality.evidenceSourceText returns — extracted as ONE shared definition first, because tools/extract.ts and groundingErrors each had their own copy of the title-plus-abstract concatenation, and two definitions of 'the source text' is precisely how offsets come to index one string while the gate reads another. Approval copies provenance verbatim, so the authoritative effect or realization record stays independently verifiable on its own, without the proposal it came from. AMENDMENT ONE — optional in the schema, required in code. The field is not in any required list, so the hand-authored records written before today stay valid; making it required would have forced fabricated offsets onto records nobody ever resolved offsets for. But optionality cannot be allowed to leak into new output, and a convention that new items 'should' carry it is a convention that will be forgotten. Authorship is therefore made structural: lib/proposal-meta exports EXTRACTION_RUN_ID_PREFIX 'extraction:' and isExtractionAuthored, runExtraction prefixes its runId, and tools/validate.ts FAILS any extraction-authored proposal whose evidence provenance lacks a span. Old unprefixed ids read as legacy, so no existing proposal fails retroactively. Enforced twice: the provenance builder refuses an unanchored citation on the call whose provenance becomes a proposal, using the existing malformed_citation reason so D-104's nine causes stay nine. The validator prints coverage every run — items with a span, items without, items stale — because 'optional for legacy, required for new' is only an honest policy if the size of the legacy remainder is visible rather than assumed. AMENDMENT TWO — offsets are meaningless without a text version. A re-harvest or a re-normalisation can leave [start,end) pointing at different words with nothing to announce it, and an edit earlier in the abstract shifts every later offset while leaving each one slicing cleanly, so re-slicing alone cannot detect drift. source_text_sha256 pins the exact string the offsets were resolved against, and verification checks the hash AND re-slices. Three named conditions replace one opaque 'quote does not resolve': span_out_of_range (offsets do not fit), span_does_not_reslice (they fit but the slice differs from the stored quote), span_stale (the text no longer hashes to what they were resolved on). They live in groundingErrors, which the extractor, lib/proposals approval, and tools/validate.ts all share, so a stale span blocks approval and is reported by name rather than being silently copied forward. DELIBERATELY UNCOVERED: realizationProvenanceItem gets no span, so mode=realizations output is not span-verifiable. Realization observations are owner-authored notes rather than fetched documents, so there is no stable harvested text for offsets to index; stating the gap in the schema is better than a span that cannot be trusted. And per D-109, a verified span proves WHERE the quote came from, never that the claim built on it follows.

decisions.title: D-102 is satisfied by labelling the denominator, not by unifying it
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: /maturation displayed '76% green' while the analyzer printed '180 cells', and the two looked like a contradiction about one shared fact. They are not: 165 is the pack grid (11 packs x 15 segments) and 180 adds the 15-cell perception row. DECISION: D-102 is closed by its labelling branch, not its unification branch.
