Unifying the denominator would fold the cross-cutting perception row into the pack figure, which is exactly what D-067 forbids — the row is scored once per segment, and counting it 11 times would inflate or deflate pack coverage depending on its status. So each surface names the population it is over instead: the /maturation header pill reads 'N% green of 165 pack cells', the heatmap footer reads '180 cells = 165 pack + 15 perception', every coverage row states the population it was computed over, and the analyzer prints the same split so the tool and the screen agree in wording as well as in arithmetic. Both figures already existed as coverage.overall.total and coverage.perception.total; nothing new is computed and no number is hardcoded, which keeps rule 2 intact. D-101 stays deferred.

decisions.title: A realization may be inferred from an effect, and must say so in the record
decisions.body: PROBLEM: the L3 shelf could only hold realizations DESCRIBED by a source (D-078), so the one thing the generator actually needs from an accepted effect — a buildable UI pattern — had nowhere to live. Every cognitive-load effect in the queue was measured in instruction and education; no source measured it in a product interface. Writing the transferred pattern into description_as_reported would have laundered an inference into evidence, which rule 8 forbids. DECISION: realizations carry the transfer explicitly. (1) realization.schema.json gains derivation ('reported' | 'inferred'), domain_transfer {source_domain, application_domain}, pattern (the imperative product-UI directive, present only when derivation='inferred'), and effect_refs — an ARRAY replacing the single optional effect_id, since one pattern can follow from more than one effect. description_as_reported keeps its old meaning in both cases: what the source says, in the source's domain. The generator reads pattern; a reviewer reads both and can see the seam. (2) A new provenance item kind, corpus_kind='inference', records the transfer step itself: it quotes the effect's own fact verbatim, points at an evidence record the effect cites, and carries span_absent_reason='no direct span — inferred from effect'. It is written by CODE from the effect record, never by a model, and it is the only provenance item permitted to have no source_span — declaring the absence beats leaving the field empty and letting a reader assume a check happened. groundingErrors() fails closed on an inference item so it can never be span-checked as evidence by accident; inferenceGroundingErrors() checks it against the effect instead. (3) mode=realizations accepts scope_kind=effect, which switches the run from describing observed interfaces to transferring one effect, reads the EVIDENCE corpus (so its quotes are span-verifiable, which realization-corpus provenance never is), anchors both prompt passes on the effect text, ranks records by affinity to that effect, and stamps every proposal derivation='inferred'. Derivation is fixed by the scope, one per run, so no proposal is half reported and half inferred. Coverage for such a run is filed under the evidence corpus it actually read. (4) Extraction may be anchored on an effect that is still a PENDING proposal — otherwise the value of an effect could never be tested before accepting it — but approval is gated: /review refuses to approve a realization whose effect_refs point at anything other than an APPROVED effect record, and re-checks the inference item against that authoritative record. So a transfer can be proposed and read at any time, and can only enter the knowledge layer behind the effect it rests on. LIMIT, stated rather than discovered: reader coverage is keyed by corpus and mode, not by effect, so records read for one effect are terminal for mode=realizations and a second effect on the same mechanism will not re-read them. Per-effect coverage would mean a schema key per effect; re-reading is the spend the ledger exists to prevent. AMENDMENT, from the first run: a realization's id is derived from its TERM, never from the id the model returns. The first effect-anchored run labelled two different patterns "cl-14-002-p1", and that id is a filename and the handle an implementation points at — neither unique nor readable. The term is both, and it is the string the proposal id is already hashed from, so one term can only occupy one file. The two colliding proposals from that run were left exactly as extracted; the validator now WARNS when several undecided proposals would be written to the same record path, because both are individually valid, nothing authoritative is wrong yet, and failing there would discard a whole run over a naming clash. The owner resolves it by approving one and rejecting or renaming the other.

decisions.title: An owner's reason is part of the record, on every decision, not only on rejections
decisions.body: prepareProposalDecision accepted a reason for every action but wrote it into the decision log for rejections alone; the approve and edit branches emitted a fixed sentence and discarded it, and applyProposalDecision additionally nulled decision_note on edit. That made the one action where an owner OVERRIDES the pipeline — editing a payload before approving it — the one action that recorded no justification. An owner-corrected value with no stated basis is exactly as ungrounded as the model-asserted value it replaced (see D-114, same defect class), so the correction would have inherited the defect it was meant to remove. The reason is now appended to the decision body for approve, edit and reject alike whenever one is supplied, the batch path does the same, and an edit keeps the reason in decision_note while decided_by and decided_at stay null, because an edit is a change of the proposal and not yet a decision about it. Effects gain an optional grade_basis field for the same reason at the artifact layer: a decision entry explains why a grade CHANGED, but the record itself must be able to say what its grade rests on to a reader who never opens decisions.json. It is optional while grades are owner-corrected by hand and becomes required when computed grading lands (D-114).

decisions.title: Grade, boundary and confidence are model assertions today, and no rubric exists anywhere
decisions.body: Asked where an effect's grade comes from, the honest answer is that nothing computes it. The entire specification is one parenthetical in the effects prompt, 'grade (A+..C-)' in tools/extract.ts taskInstruction; the value is copied through verbatim in toProposal and checked only for enum membership by evidenceGrade. boundary is item.boundary.trim() with no prompt instruction beyond the field name and no check against anything. confidence is the model's own number, gated only by limits.confidence_floor = 0.5, and effects mode — unlike realizations mode, which defines confidence as confidence in the TRANSFER and caps it at 0.8 — never tells the model what the number means. The synthesis pass says 'grade conservatively', which is an adjective, not a criterion. No rubric exists in code, in docs, in SPEC.md, or in the schemas: effect.schema.json and mechanism.schema.json define grade as a bare nine-value enum, and docs/s7-drafting-brief.md calls it 'the author's committed grade', a human-judgement contract the pipeline silently inherited when the model became the author. The letter does not stay a letter: PRIOR_WEIGHT_BY_GRADE turns it into a numeric prior_weight on the mechanism record, so an assertion becomes a weight a generator reads. This is the same defect class as D-115: a number or letter presented with the authority of measurement, traceable to nothing. INTERIM, applied now: cl-14-002 was regraded A- to C+ by owner edit before approval, with the basis stated in grade_basis (D-113) — one secondary source, a narrative review, is a C+ corpus whatever the literature at large says, and OUR grade describes OUR corpus. PROPOSED, not implemented: docs/computed-grading.md specifies a grade computed from countable corpus facts, with the model reporting only per-record study design and direction; single-record bases capped below the A band, and a cited record whose own conclusions contradict the proposed fact treated as a refusal rather than a downgrade. Nothing re-grades automatically until that rubric is approved.

decisions.title: A numeric threshold in an inferred pattern is a named tunable parameter, never prose
decisions.body: All three realizations from the first effect-anchored run told a generator to switch behaviour after 'three times' or 'three completions'. No source measured three, or any number: the cited studies compared worked examples against exploration and reported no significant difference for experienced learners, with nothing said about how many repetitions build a schema. The number was invented by the model and then written in the register of a finding — the same defect as D-114, an unmeasured value carrying the authority of measurement, differing only in that a grade at least LOOKS like a judgement while '3' looks like data. Realizations therefore gain a `parameters` array of {name, value, unit, evidence_basis}. The pattern text carries {snake_case_name} and the default lives in the parameter, so a reader sees the number is tunable and a generator can override it without editing prose. evidence_basis is an enum whose only member today is 'none — default heuristic', following the span_absent_reason precedent in the same schema: a literal a reader can filter on, not a sentence a writer can reword into sounding measured, and a second member is added the day a source actually measures a threshold. It is code-filled at extraction, never read from the model, because letting a model write it would let a model claim its own guess was measured. Enforcement sits at three depths, deliberately unequal: the extractor DROPS a candidate whose pattern states a bare digit or number-word rather than repairing it, since guessing which number the prose meant reinvents the same precision one layer down; approval REFUSES such a payload in projectRealization, which is the boundary the number would cross to become knowledge; and the validator FAILS a record but only WARNS on an undecided proposal, because a decided proposal keeps the payload it was decided on — rewriting a rejected pattern would erase the evidence of what the pipeline produced — and failing an undecided one would discard a whole run over a number the owner is about to fix. parameters is forbidden when derivation='reported', which describes what a source observed and has no pattern to parameterise. Applied immediately to expertise-based-guidance-toggle, whose 'three times' became {core_task_completions_before_exploration}.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-expertise-reversal-effect-72a394e20f30 edited
decisions.body: Owner owner edited effect proposal effect-cl-14-expertise-reversal-effect-72a394e20f30 for CL-14. The validated proposal payload was updated for further review. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Provisional grade. Corpus evidence = one secondary source (narrative review, AMEE Guide 86). Model-asserted A- rejected as ungrounded. To be re-graded when the computed rubric (grade-provenance defect) lands. Grade reflects OUR corpus provenance, not the literature at large.

decisions.title: Proposal realization-cl-14-expertise-based-guidance-toggle-d86bcf53c129 edited
decisions.body: Owner owner edited realization proposal realization-cl-14-expertise-based-guidance-toggle-d86bcf53c129 for CL-14. The validated proposal payload was updated for further review. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Three corrections before approval. (1) Wording: the cited span reports NO significant difference for learners with prior domain familiarity, not harm — description_as_reported now says so explicitly. The pattern stands, because removing guidance that has stopped paying for itself is justified at neutrality, but the rationale must not claim this study showed interference; the "may even interfere" sentence belongs to the effect and stays labelled as the effect's, in the inference provenance item. (2) Id: cl-14-002-p1 was returned for two different patterns, so the term-derived id expertise-based-guidance-toggle replaces it and resolves the collision. (3) Threshold: "three times" was model-invented precision; it is now the named tunable parameter core_task_completions_before_exploration with evidence_basis "none — default heuristic" (D-115). Confidence 0.75 to 0.6, since the transfer rests on a neutral result rather than a measured reversal.

decisions.title: Proposal realization-cl-14-expertise-based-guidance-toggle-d86bcf53c129 approved
decisions.body: Owner owner approved realization proposal realization-cl-14-expertise-based-guidance-toggle-d86bcf53c129 for CL-14. The validated proposal status and authoritative projection were committed atomically. Reason: Accepted after the wording, id and threshold corrections in D-118. The transfer is a hypothesis for a generator, not evidence that it works — it rests on a neutral result for experienced learners, and its threshold is a declared default nobody measured.

decisions.title: Proposal realization-cl-14-context-aware-tool-simplification-c403738e29d7 rejected
decisions.body: Owner owner rejected realization proposal realization-cl-14-context-aware-tool-simplification-c403738e29d7 for CL-14. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Duplicate. Same trigger and same action as expertise-based-guidance-toggle: both replace a guided walkthrough with the unguided interface once the user has repeated the core workflow, differing only in which surface they name. A generator would read them as one rule with two surfaces. No independent evidence either — its only quote is the effect's own sentence, so its reported half adds nothing the effect does not already say.

decisions.title: Proposal realization-cl-14-progressive-disclosure-of-advanced-f-7a339e24183c rejected
decisions.body: Owner owner rejected realization proposal realization-cl-14-progressive-disclosure-of-advanced-f-7a339e24183c for CL-14. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Mis-anchored. Expertise reversal states that SUPPORT harms EXPERTS; this pattern withholds advanced FEATURES from NOVICES, which runs the effect backwards. Hiding complexity from a beginner is justified by general cognitive load, not by cl-14-002, and its only quote is the effect's own sentence, so nothing in its evidence half supports the direction it takes. If it returns it must anchor to a CL-14 load effect, not to expertise reversal.

decisions.title: Envelope confidence is corrected inside the decision transaction, never by hand in git
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: the edit action replaced payload and nothing else, so an owner who judged the pipeline's confidence unearned had two options: leave a number they disbelieved, or open the proposal file and change it in a separate commit. The second is what happened, and it breaks the one property the transaction exists to hold. D-113 requires a reason on every decision, and a hand-edited file carries no reason, no actor and no decision id — the corrected number becomes exactly as unexplained as the asserted one it replaced, and cl-14-002's regrade only reads as justified because the grade travelled with the payload while its confidence did not. DECISION: ProposalDecisionRequest gains an optional editedConfidence, applied to the envelope in the same atomic transaction as editedPayload, exposed as --confidence on the proposal CLI. Refused on approve and reject: the payload an approval commits is the one that was reviewed, and a number changed at approval time was reviewed by nobody. Refused outside [0,1] with the flag named in the message rather than a JSON Schema path, because a nonsense value should blame the input that carried it. Omitting the flag leaves the existing number untouched, so absent and corrected stay distinguishable. The confidence FLOOR is unchanged and still an extraction-time gate — an owner may set a value below it, since a held proposal and an owner-corrected low confidence are different facts. /review keeps its payload-only edit form; adding a confidence field to the UI would be a knowledge-editing surface the constitution does not allow, and the CLI is the recovery path the library already documents.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-modality-effect-c16093817de1 rejected
decisions.body: Owner owner rejected effect proposal effect-cl-14-modality-effect-c16093817de1 for CL-14. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Inverted. The sole cited paper (Tabbers, Martens & van Merrienboer 2004) found the OPPOSITE of this fact. The quoted span at offsets 369-638 sits in the abstract's BACKGROUND section, where the paper restates what cognitive load theory and Mayer's theory PREDICT. Its own RESULTS report that replacing visual text with spoken text produced LOWER retention and transfer scores, and CONCLUSIONS names the finding 'a reverse modality effect', attributed to the instructions being learner-paced rather than system-paced. The model quoted the paper accurately, from the part of the paper the paper went on to refute. This is not a weak effect to be downgraded: an effect whose only source reports its reversal is evidence against, and filing it at any grade would put a false claim in the registry under a humble-looking label. Approving the reverse effect instead would need a fresh extraction anchored to the RESULTS span, not an edit of this one.

decisions.title: For effects and realizations, an edited payload's provenance is the envelope's provenance
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: found while executing the two CL-14 edits the owner ordered. effect.schema.json and the proposal envelope require payload.provenance and envelope provenance to be EXACTLY EQUAL (assertPayloadProvenance), and the edit action replaces payload only. The two are therefore jointly unsatisfiable for any edit that touches provenance: dropping a mis-anchored citation, or re-anchoring a quote to a different span of the same record, fails an equality check the edit has no way to reach. That is not a narrow inconvenience — the two commonest owner corrections on an extraction-authored proposal are 'this citation is not evidence' and 'this quote is from the wrong part of the paper', and neither was expressible. The only routes left were to reject a proposal that was substantially right, or to hand-edit the file in git, which is precisely what D-122 closed. DECISION: for effect and realization, the two types whose schema declares the equality, the envelope provenance is a PROJECTION of the payload's and an edit carries it up automatically. Every other type keeps an independently authored envelope: dossier axis provenance is a SUBSET of the envelope rather than equal to it, so mirroring there would silently widen what the envelope claims. This cannot mask a divergence, because the proposal as read on disk is checked for one before the edit is applied, and the mirrored provenance is re-grounded against the corpus by assertResolvableProvenance — including span re-slicing and hash verification under D-110 — before any artifact is projected. What an owner still cannot do is invent provenance: a re-anchored span must resolve in the corpus, so the edit can move a quote to another part of a cited record but not to a record the pipeline never read.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-cueing-effect-01aaa2ec2e72 edited
decisions.body: Owner owner edited effect proposal effect-cl-14-cueing-effect-01aaa2ec2e72 for CL-14. The validated proposal payload was updated for further review. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Gutted to what the paper actually found, and kept rather than rejected. The direction survives contact with the data: the paper's RESULTS report that adding visual cues raised retention scores, which points the same way as the proposal — unlike the modality half, which reversed. What does not survive is the magnitude and the generality, so the fact now says the study found only a weak cueing effect that does not easily generalise beyond the laboratory, and the boundary names the learner-paced non-laboratory setting where that was observed. Both provenance items are now findings spans (RESULTS 1190-1260, CONCLUSIONS 1369-1527) on the same record; the model's original BACKGROUND span at 434-638, which restated theory the paper went on to qualify, is gone. Grade B+ to C, confidence 0.85 to 0.55. Kept rather than rejected for two reasons: a weak positive with a named boundary is usable by a generator as a constraint — do not spend design budget on cueing as a primary lever — and an empty queue invites the next extraction run to re-propose cueing at B+ from the same BACKGROUND sentence.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-cueing-effect-01aaa2ec2e72 approved
decisions.body: Owner owner approved effect proposal effect-cl-14-cueing-effect-01aaa2ec2e72 for CL-14. The validated proposal status and authoritative projection were committed atomically. Reason: Accepted at C after the re-anchoring in D-125. What is being filed is a weak positive with a named boundary, not a robust effect: one classroom study, cues raised retention but not transfer, and the authors themselves call the cueing effect weak and say it does not easily generalise beyond the laboratory. A generator should read this as a reason NOT to treat cueing as a primary lever, and as the boundary that a future proposal claiming a strong cueing effect has to argue past. Both citations are findings spans on the same DOI, so the record is consistent with the span_role gate rather than grandfathered against it.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-split-attention-effect-04b908b55654 edited
decisions.body: Owner owner edited effect proposal effect-cl-14-split-attention-effect-04b908b55654 for CL-14. The validated proposal payload was updated for further review. No authoritative artifact was changed. Reason: Narrowed to the evidence that survives. Three changes. (1) The clause 'which increases extraneous working memory load' is gone: it appears in no cited span. It comes from the Ayres and Sweller chapter's theoretical rationale, and the model welded it onto a sentence from a different paper. (2) The second citation is dropped from provenance AND from source. Its span states a design prescription -- 'it is important to avoid formats that require learners to split their attention' -- which is what an instructional designer SHOULD do, not what a study FOUND. A prescription cannot be evidence for a phenomenon. (3) Grade A to C+, confidence 0.95 to 0.7, because one DOI remains and a single-record basis is capped below the A band. Added, beyond the literal narrowing: a second span on the SAME record at 871-925, 'The results of 6 experiments supported this hypothesis'. The surviving 314-469 span is the paper's own premise -- the abstract says 'The logic was based on the split-attention effect' -- so on its own this record is exactly what the span_role gate exists to drop. The 871-925 span is the paper's finding that the prediction built on that premise held. With both, the record rests on a premise the paper went on to confirm rather than on a premise nobody checked, and it survives the gate instead of being grandfathered past it.

decisions.title: Proposal effect-cl-14-split-attention-effect-04b908b55654 approved
decisions.body: Owner owner approved effect proposal effect-cl-14-split-attention-effect-04b908b55654 for CL-14. The validated proposal status and authoritative projection were committed atomically. Reason: Approved at C+ after the narrowing in D-127. This is the first CL-14 effect resting on a primary experimental paper rather than a review, and it is still capped in the C band because the corpus holds exactly one DOI for it -- the split-attention literature is far larger than our corpus of it, and the grade states what WE hold, not what the field holds. The record is deliberately less than the model claimed: no extraneous-load mechanism, no second source, no A.

decisions.title: A span must declare what it is DOING in its source, and only a finding can ground a fact
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: the first extraction run produced three effect proposals. Two of them quoted a BACKGROUND premise as though the cited study had found it, and one of those papers (Tabbers, Martens & van Merrienboer 2004) went on to report the OPPOSITE — its own CONCLUSIONS section names 'a reverse modality effect'. Every quote was verbatim, every span re-sliced, every hash matched. D-110 was working perfectly and had nothing to say, because the defect was not in the text but in the text's ROLE: a paper is not one voice, and 'replacing visual text with spoken text ... increase[s] the effectiveness of multimedia instructions' is what cognitive load theory PREDICTS, restated by a paper whose data refuted it. Grounding proves the words are the source's. It cannot prove the source was asserting them. DECISION: every extraction-authored citation asserts span_role from a closed vocabulary — background, hypothesis, method, finding, limitation — and the assertion is then ARGUED WITH, using the source text alone, in lib/span-role.ts. (1) STRUCTURE: when an abstract labels its own sections, the label constrains the role; a span inside BACKGROUND or METHOD cannot be this paper's finding. Labels are matched against a closed vocabulary, so the DOI:, ORCID:, ISBN: and STOP-IT: headings that also appear before colons in this corpus create no sections. (2) DOWNSTREAM CONTRADICTION: a span asserted as a finding, followed in the same text by a sentence that reverses it AND shares at least three distinctive words with it, is a premise the paper overturned. Skipped when the span itself carries a reversal marker, because a quote that states the qualification cannot be undone by it — without that rule the honest quote 'Only a weak cueing effect and even a reverse modality effect have been found' would be refused for being followed by the sentence explaining it. (3) THE FINDING REQUIREMENT is a property of the ITEM, not of a citation: at least one citation must be a finding, but an item may cite the premise its finding confirms — which is the shape cl-14-001 was narrowed to in D-127, where the paper's own 'The logic was based on the split-attention effect' sits beside 'The results of 6 experiments supported this hypothesis'. Requiring every citation to be a finding would have forbidden the most honest record in the repo. MEASURED, not asserted: across 3192 abstracts in the evidence corpora, only 3.8% carry two or more recognised section labels, so the structural check is silent on 96% and the downstream check is the workhorse there. A probe quoting the OPENING 200 characters and claiming a finding is refused 6.1% of the time (3.1% structural, 3.1% downstream); a probe quoting the LAST 200 characters, where results and conclusions live, is admitted 99.8% of the time, and every one of the six refusals is a full-text record whose tail genuinely sits in a Method, Rationale or Context section. Zero downstream false positives on findings-region text. The one spurious marker found while measuring — 'reverse-engineering' read as a reversal — is excluded by name. PERSISTED, not merely checked: span_role travels on the provenance item through the ledger, the extract-to-synthesize round trip, the proposal and the approved record, because a reader asking why an effect is graded as it is needs to see that a citation is the paper's result rather than its opening premise, and re-deriving that would mean re-reading the source with the same judgement that was already made. ENFORCEMENT follows the D-110 pattern — optional in the three schemas, required in code — with one addition D-110 did not need: a cutoff. D-110 preceded any extraction output; span_role arrives after eight items are already committed, and there is NO BACKFILL, because a role invented now for a span a model read last week would be my judgement wearing the pipeline's authority, which is the exact substitution this field exists to prevent. So requiresSpanRole() checks proposed_at against SPAN_ROLE_REQUIRED_FROM, and tools/validate.ts prints the roleless remainder every run so it cannot quietly become permanent. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CATCH, stated because the next failure will come from here: an unstructured abstract whose premise nothing downstream contradicts. Mousavi, Low & Sweller 1995 is exactly that case — 'The split-attention effect occurs when students must split their attention' is the paper's premise, the abstract has no section labels, and the paper CONFIRMS the premise rather than reversing it. Nothing in this decision would stop a model that labels it 'finding'. The only defence there is the model's own honesty and the owner's reading, which is why the gate is a floor and not a ceiling. COST: a candidate wrongly refused is recoverable — the owner can hand-author the record, or edit a proposal under D-124 — while a false fact filed at any grade is not. The gate is set to refuse on doubt for that reason, and every refusal records the section label or the matched marker with its shared words, so a wrong refusal is arguable rather than mysterious.

decisions.title: The category classifier is repaired and the retag is NOT applied — categories are the rubric input layer, so the vocabulary is an owner call
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: every record cited by the three CL-14 effect proposals carried categories: []. Tabbers, Martens & van Merrienboer 2004 — the one genuinely dissenting paper in the set, whose abstract says the modality effect 'reversed' and that the results 'do not easily generalise' — was not tagged dissent, while CL-14 as a whole reported 187 dissent records. DIAGNOSIS, and it is not staleness: classifyRecord was re-run over all 4444 records in corpora/evidence/** and stored categories equalled recomputed categories with ZERO mismatches. Nothing was skipped and no write path bypasses classification. The rules themselves were wrong, in three separate ways, and each way is a different KIND of change — which matters, because a bug fix is mine to make and a definition change is not. (1) BUG, singular-only negation. DISSENT_MARKERS matched 'does not' and nothing else: not 'do not', 'did not', 'was not', 'were not'. 'do not easily generalise' was invisible for that reason alone. Also missing were the words a reversal is actually reported in — reverse, reversal of, only a weak, contrary to, opposite, no evidence, null result. Fixed. (2) BUG, an age-blind citation floor. FOUNDATIONAL_MIN_CITATIONS = 1000 as a raw total silently means 'cited like a 2010 paper': Mousavi, Low & Sweller 1995 — six experiments, the primary source behind cl-14-001 — sits at 958 after 31 years and was not foundational, while a 2015 review of it would be. Added a second route, a sustained rate, with two floors: at least 10 years old (two years of fast citation is a hot paper, not a foundation) and at least 250 citations total (a high rate over a thin total is not one either). (3) BUG, a container-blind review test. isReviewLike accepted openalex_type === 'review' or a meta-analysis/systematic-review title, so Ayres & Sweller 2005 — a Cambridge handbook chapter that surveys the split-attention literature, and the citation that made cl-14-001 look like it rested on two studies — read as primary research. Broadened to the review genres present in this corpus, plus review-shaped titles RESTRICTED to book chapters and reference entries, because 'principle' in a handbook chapter title is a genre word and in a journal article title it is a claim. (4) NOT A BUG, a semantic change, and therefore flagged rather than quietly made: dissent fired on the bare word 'question' in 539 records and a bare 'does not' in 382. Dropping those catch-alls is not a fix, it is a narrower definition of dissent, and it is most of the reason the category shrinks. MEASURED over all 4444 records: foundational 414 → 771, meta-analysis 374 → 412, replication unchanged at 493, recent unchanged at 1540, dissent 1149 → 729, records with no category at all 1590 → 1502, and 1043 records change tags. The plan estimated 990 and 602; the difference is entirely the two conservative floors added to the citation-rate route and the negated-verb list ending up broader than the sketch, and the measured numbers are the ones that count. DECISION, and this is the part that is not a code decision: THE RETAG IS NOT APPLIED. categories is the input layer of the grading rubric, halving dissent is a change in what the corpus is able to disconfirm, and rule 4 makes that an owner judgement rather than a cleanup. tools/retag-categories.ts therefore defaults to a dry run and writes only under --apply; the dry run is also the review instrument, reporting per-corpus before/after, a deterministic seeded sample of changed records with the matched text that changed them, and which marker is the SOLE reason each record is tagged dissent. The two largest sole-reason markers are critique at 130 and boundary-condition at 127, and the negated-verb rule is split into neg+claim-verb (38 sole) and neg+outcome-verb (103 sole) as two separately named markers precisely so the weaker half can be dropped by the owner with an exact count rather than argued about. SAFETY, checked: validate.ts fails any dossier whose corpus reports dissent 0 (D-019). After the retag every live mechanism corpus stays above zero — lowest VR-02 at 27 → 10 — and the one corpus that reaches zero is CG-05.regression, a side file the gate does not read; the tool reports it explicitly rather than leaving it to be noticed. dissent_completeness in the sufficiency matrix reads dossier prose, not corpus categories, so a retag does not move the matrix; it does move the cockpit category display and the digest, both computed. STRUCTURAL FINDING, the one worth the owner's attention: categories has no slot for study design. foundational and recent are metadata bands, dissent and replication are prose sniffs, and meta-analysis is the only design-ish tag — which is why Ayres & Sweller, a narrative review, now lands in meta-analysis for want of anywhere better. Even a perfect classifier cannot ground a grade with this vocabulary, so the design axis stays where docs/computed-grading.md puts it, as study_design per cited record, with categories as corroboration only. No vocabulary value was added; that is a separate owner call.

decisions.title: A number quoted in a mid-task question is an estimate; only a measured post-implementation number may authorize a data commit
decisions.body: THE RULE: any count, share or delta named before the code that produces it has been run is an ESTIMATE, and must be labelled as one at the point it is written — in a question to the owner, in a plan, in a commit message draft. A commit that writes to /registry, /effects, /realizations, /interactions, /corpora/evidence, /sources or /proposals may cite only numbers produced by RUNNING the implementation against the committed data. When an owner approval was given against an estimate and the measurement then differs, the approval does not carry over: it is re-requested with the measured number, and the difference is stated rather than absorbed. THE MOTIVATING CASE, today: the retag plan quoted dissent falling to 602 and roughly 990 records changing, and asked for a decision on that basis. Running tools/retag-categories.ts over all 4444 stored records measured dissent 1149 → 729 and 1043 records changed, with foundational at 414 → 771 against a sketch that had never been quantified at all. The 602-vs-729 gap is 127 records, 21% of the estimate, and it came from two conservative floors added to the citation-rate route plus a negated-verb list that ended up broader than the sketch — in other words from writing the code, which is the only place such a number can come from. The direction matters as much as the size: dissent is the category tools/validate.ts gates a live dossier on (D-019), so an approval granted at 602 would have authorized a corpus mutation whose effect on the disconfirmation capacity of every corpus was wrong by a fifth. ESTIMATES REMAIN ALLOWED. They are how a change is scoped and how the owner decides whether it is worth looking at; the rule bans them from AUTHORIZING a write, not from being said. What is forbidden is the silent promotion — an estimate quoted in a question, then reused in a commit message as though it had been measured. HOW IT IS ENFORCED: by construction, not by a checker. A tool that proposes a data mutation defaults to a dry run that prints the measured before/after, and the numbers in the commit message and in the decision entry are copied from that output rather than retyped from the plan. tools/retag-categories.ts (D-130) is the reference shape: --dry-run by default, --apply explicit, and the dry run doubling as the review instrument. A checker is deliberately not added, because a rule about honesty in prose is not something a validator can read. RELATION TO RULE 4 AND D-130: complementary, not a substitute. Rule 4 says a change to a vocabulary the rubric reads is the owner's call; D-131 says the owner makes that call against measured numbers. D-130 already applied this rule to itself — it records the 990/602 estimates alongside the 1043/729 measurements and states that the measured ones count — and this entry generalises that from one commit to the working practice.

decisions.title: Candidate conservation is an enforced invariant: a run whose ledger does not balance is BROKEN, and a run with no ledger entry does not pass by omission
decisions.body: THE INVARIANT: candidates_in == proposals_out + merged + dropped_by_named_reason, for every extraction run, checked by tools/validate.ts. Stated as four staged equations in lib/candidate-ledger.ts, because the pipeline is a funnel and one line over `candidates` would be summing two different populations: (E1) candidates == candidates_cheap + candidates_strong; (E2) candidates_cheap == dropped_ungrounded_cheap + synthesis_batch_failed + into_synthesis; (E3) into_synthesis + expanded == consolidated + candidates_strong; (E4) candidates_strong == proposed + proposed_enrich + merged_into_pending + held_low_confidence + failed_validation + dropped_ungrounded_strong + dropped_volume_cap + dropped_draft_cap. A run failing any of them is written to the manifest with status BROKEN, a new value alongside success/partial/failed. The distinction is the entry: a partial run did less than its scope and reports that honestly, while an unbalanced run cannot say what it did, so every number it reports — including its spend attribution and its yield — is unsound. Calling that 'partial' would file an unreadable run under a word that means 'incomplete but trustworthy'. THIRD APPEARANCE OF ONE DEFECT CLASS, which is why this is an invariant and not another counter. (1) D-104, the 30-for-30: four runs — SC-06, CG-05, FR-11, RE-10 — dropped 100% of their candidates as ungrounded and left behind a counter and five sampled console lines, so the evidence for a fix evaporated with the Actions log. Fixed by persisting every refusal. (2) D-105, the uncounted cheap pass: cheap candidates were discarded ungated on the way into synthesis with no counter and no record. Fixed by gating the cheap pass and splitting the counters per pass — but the SYNTHESIS stage between them was left with no counter at all, so a cheap-to-strong shrink of 8 to 7 stayed invisible; D-105's own text names that shrink and does not close it. (3) Today, 8 of 15: the CL-14 effects run cl14-validation-1 reported 15 candidates as 8 cheap plus 7 strong, and recorded outcomes for the 7 strong ones only — 4 proposed, 3 merged. The 8 cheap candidates had no recorded fate. Each fix named the loss it had just seen; none of them asked whether the numbers add up. This one asks, on every run, and fails the build when they do not. CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: the 8-of-15 was previously reported as belonging to the realizations run. It does not. It is the EFFECTS run cl14-validation-1 (2026-07-31T09:10:13.532Z, dispatch cl14-validation-1, github_run_id 30618907548). The realizations run cl14-002-realizations (2026-07-31T10:09:59.574Z) balances: 9 candidates as 6 cheap plus 3 strong, 3 cheap refused for unknown_record_id and persisted per candidate, 3 into synthesis, 3 composed, 3 proposed. Recording the correction here rather than fixing it silently, because a misattributed defect sends the next fix to the wrong stage. TWO ACCOUNTING DEFECTS FOUND WHILE WRITING THE EQUATIONS, both of which made the invariant unstateable before they were fixed. (a) `merged` conflated two different outcomes: a candidate ABSORBED into an earlier pending proposal, which produces no file, and an ENRICHMENT of an already-approved artifact, which does. Both incremented the same counter, so proposals_out was not derivable from the run params at all. Split into merged_into_pending and proposed_enrich, with `merged` kept as their sum because /ops and every committed run entry already read it. (b) A draft-mode run discarded synthesis output past the first item with no counter — composing four artifacts and keeping one reported one candidate. Named dropped_draft_cap, and candidates_strong now counts what the model composed rather than what survived the cap. THE LEDGER: corpora/extraction/ledger.json, one entry per run, schema at corpora/_ops/candidate-ledger.schema.json, written mid-flight on the same cadence as the manifest (D-099) so a run that dies still says what became of the candidates it had already produced. Per-candidate rows carry the fate and, for a merge, WHICH proposal absorbed the candidate — the question the old counters could not answer. No model text is stored: a refused candidate is already persisted in full under corpora/extraction/rejected/ (D-104), and this file answers what became of each one, not what it said. BACKFILL, and what could not be backfilled. cl14-002-realizations is reconstructed complete from the committed rejected-candidate log and the three proposal files. cl14-validation-1 is PARTIAL: its stage totals are recoverable and balance — 8 cheap, none refused, all 8 into synthesis, which composed 7, so exactly one fold; 7 composed candidates ending as 4 proposals and 3 absorptions — but two things are gone. Cheap-pass lineage, because cheap candidates were persisted only when refused and this run refused none. And the merge TARGETS, because mergeProposals unions provenance and takes the higher confidence, which leaves a merged proposal indistinguishable from a single candidate that cited two records; split-attention carries two records and two DOIs, which is what an absorption looks like and also what a well-cited candidate looks like, so it is not evidence. All three absorptions are recorded with attribution not_recorded rather than guessed at. SC-06, CG-05, FR-11 and RE-10 are declared UNRECONSTRUCTABLE with the reason 'rejected candidates were not persisted before D-105' — a provenance fact, not a grandfather clause. Their strong stage is filled in from the manifest and does balance at 10-for-10, 10-for-10, 8-for-8 and 2-for-2; their cheap stage is null rather than zero, because those runs gated only the strong pass, so cheap candidates existed and were never counted, and writing a zero there would assert something false. The two failed CG-05 dispatches of 2026-07-24 get a DIFFERENT reason, stated separately rather than folded in with the four: they failed with routing_404 before any model was invoked (cost.api_calls = 0), so their zeros are measured, not missing. NO RUN PASSES BY OMISSION. tools/validate.ts reads the manifest and the ledger in both directions: every run in last_run and run_history must have a ledger entry, an entry that does not balance must be reflected as status broken in the manifest, and the stored `balanced` flag is recomputed rather than trusted so a hand-edited true buys nothing. A missing entry FAILS. This is the part that matters most, because the defect class survived three fixes by looking like nothing had happened — and an absent ledger entry looks exactly the same way. The reconstruction vocabulary is recorded / reconstructed / partial / unreconstructable, and everything short of `recorded` REQUIRES a written reason; a gap is recorded as a gap.

decisions.title: The reversal vocabulary is extended and re-measured; the 31.3% 'ceiling' turns out to be the frequency of the word 'however'
decisions.body: WHAT CHANGED: REVERSAL_MARKERS in lib/span-role.ts goes from 10 anonymous regexes to 18 NAMED ones. Added: in-contrast-to-prediction; a broadened only-a-weak (small, modest, marginal, negligible); fail-to+verb over the full verb list rather than seven verbs; neg+claim-verb and neg+outcome-verb as two separately named rules, the same split DISSENT_MARKERS uses so a later narrowing can drop one half with an exact count; was-not+participle extended to is/are/has/have/had and to detected, reliable, evident, present, borne out, obtained, sustained, maintained; no-effect-of; no-support-for; null-result; absence-of; contradicts (contradict / refute / disconfirm); effect-disappeared. Naming them is not cosmetic: a refusal now says WHICH rule fired, so a wrong refusal points at the rule to change, and tools/marker-coverage.ts can report each rule's sole-reason count. This is MECHANICS, not science (rule 8): the vocabulary decides which sentences the extraction gate is willing to read as a reversal; it never decides what is true. MEASURED, over all 4444 stored records with npm run markers:coverage. Denominator 3255 records whose title+abstract has more than one sentence. Marker reach after the first sentence: 356 (10.9%) before, 583 (17.9%) after, +227 records. The figure that actually matters is the refusal rate — marker AND at least three shared content words, which is what refuses a candidate: 133 (4.1%) before, 236 (7.3%) after. Per-marker sole-reason counts are in the report; the largest new contributors are neg+claim-verb at 86 and neg+outcome-verb at 63. THE CEILING, AND THE FINDING WORTH THE OWNER'S TIME. The task was framed as closing the distance between 7.5% coverage and a 31.3% ceiling. The 31.3% REPRODUCES EXACTLY — and it is the reach of the bare word 'however' over this denominator, 1020 of 3255 records, and nothing else. The ceiling was a discourse marker's frequency, not an estimate of how much reversal the corpus contains. Decomposed: named phrasings plus catch-alls reach 63.5%; named phrasings alone reach 17.9%; 45.6% is reachable ONLY by catch-alls — bare however 31.3%, bare negation 36.0%, bare question 16.3%, bare but 38.6%. Those are the exact shapes D-130 measured misfiring in the sister vocabulary, where a bare 'question' tagged 539 records and a bare 'does not' tagged 382. Closing the distance to that ceiling means re-importing the defect D-130 just removed, so the distance is reported decomposed and is explicitly NOT a target. The 7.5% side does not reproduce from any basis reconstructable here — whole corpus or CL-14 alone, title+abstract or abstract alone, whole text or first tail sentence or last — and is therefore superseded rather than compared against. Per D-131 the unreproducible number is retired, and the probe that produced the replacement is written down in the tool so this cannot recur. WHY WIDENING IS SAFE HERE, stated because it would not be safe everywhere: precision in this gate comes from the overlap requirement, not the vocabulary. A marker only refuses when its sentence shares three distinctive content words with the quote — the ratio proves it, 583 marker hits collapsing to 236 refusals. The module's own trade-off applies: a wrongly refused candidate is recoverable and visible in the funnel, a wrongly filed fact is neither. Two exclusions stay out on purpose: 'as opposed to', which introduces a contrast between conditions rather than a retraction, and 'however' plus bare negation, for the reasons above. TESTS: lib/span-role.test.ts, new, with a positive control for EVERY named marker — asserting that the NAMED rule fires, not merely that some rule does, so a phrasing caught by accident cannot silently disappear when an unrelated rule is narrowed — and negative controls for the shapes a marker set goes wrong on: the D-130 catch-alls verbatim, condition contrasts, negated procedures and samples, a hypothesis stated rather than overturned, and method words containing a marker's stem. The stem exclusions are MEASURED, not imagined: 'reverse transcription' occurs in 13 of the 4444 records and 'reverse-engineering' in 2, so both are excluded; 'reverse-scored' and 'reversed-item' occur in zero, so neither is, because an exclusion for a false positive nobody has seen is a guess. DISSENT_MARKERS IS NOT TOUCHED. The D-130 freeze holds until the owner session. What the same phrasings WOULD do to dissent is computed and reported as a separate labelled figure: 729 records today, 851 with the eight reversal phrasings that are not already dissent markers, +122 records (+2.7% of the corpus). Sole-new-reason counts per phrasing are in the report; the largest is 'reverse' at 36. Nothing was written. The owner session decides the dissent vocabulary seeing both variants, and any re-measure happens once, after the decision, per D-131.

decisions.title: A test may not write to a committed path
decisions.body: THE RULE: a test observes; it does not write to the repository. Anything a test needs to produce goes to a directory created with mkdtemp and removed afterwards. THE CASE: tools/analyzer.test.ts called main() with no arguments, which wrote analysis/sufficiency-matrix.json — a committed artifact, 15 packs by 15 segments plus the perception row — on every run of the suite. Three things follow from that, and the third is the one that matters. The working tree is dirty after any test run, so `git status` stops being a signal and a real change to the matrix is indistinguishable from test noise. `git diff` in CI cannot be used as a check for anything. And a regenerated artifact rides along in whatever commit happens next, so the matrix on disk was last written by a test rather than by anyone deciding to regenerate it. THE FIX: main() takes an optional matrixPath, defaulting to the committed location so the CLI is unchanged, and the test points it at mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'analyzer-')). Parameterising the path rather than mocking the filesystem keeps the test exercising the real write. NO RESTORE WAS NEEDED, and that is a measurement rather than an assumption: the committed matrix was clean against HEAD 21eac15 before this change, and a second test now computes a fresh matrix into a temp path and deep-equals it against the committed one, excluding generated_at because a clock reading is not a measurement. It passes, so the committed state is verified equal to a fresh computation. That second test also replaces something the old behaviour was accidentally providing — with the suite no longer rewriting the file, nothing else keeps it in step with the pack map, the segments and the approved realizations, and a stale matrix would make every screen that reads it quietly wrong. Now it fails loudly and says to run `npm run analyze` deliberately. SWEEP: all 12 test files were checked for writes to committed paths. lib/proposals.test.ts writes heavily and already builds a temporary repository with mkdtemp; no other test writes at all. Two gaps were found and closed along the way: lib/span-role.test.ts (new, D-133) and lib/github.test.ts (existing, three passing tests) had no npm script and were run by nothing, in CI or locally. Both now have scripts and both are in .github/workflows/validate.yml. ENFORCED, not promised: validate.yml runs `git diff --exit-code` after the test steps, so a test that writes to a tracked file fails CI rather than being noticed later. The full suite is 174 tests across 11 scripts, and the working tree is byte-identical before and after.

decisions.title: Two of D-130's four classifier changes are relabelled: the citation-rate route is a NEW ADMISSION RULE, not a bug fix
decisions.body: WHY A NEW ENTRY: decisions.json is append-only (rule 7), so D-130 is not edited. This entry carries the reclassification and cites it, and docs/computed-grading.md section 5a states both labels side by side so the owner session sees what changed and what it is being called. THE RELABEL, and it is not pedantry: a bug fix is a repair the code may make on its own, and a definition change is the owner's call under rule 4. The label decides which one is happening, so a definition change filed as a fix is a change that never gets approved. (1) THE CITATION-RATE FOUNDATIONAL ROUTE IS A NEW ADMISSION RULE, not a bug fix. D-130 files it as fixing an 'age-blind citation floor'. The old rule admitted a record as foundational at 1000 raw citations; the new one adds a SECOND route, a sustained citation rate floored at 10 years old and 250 citations total. Nothing was broken and then repaired — a record admitted by the new route was correctly excluded by the old rule as that rule was written. What changed is the definition of foundational, from 'cited a great deal' to 'cited a great deal, OR cited steadily for a long time'. MEASURED: foundational 414 → 771, +357 records, +86%. Filing that as a fix would let the rubric's most heavily weighted input nearly double without anyone approving it. (2) DROPPING BARE 'question' IS A SEMANTIC NARROWING, which D-130 already says — the change here is that the share is now MEASURED rather than estimated. 239 of the 562 records that lose the dissent tag lose it for that reason ALONE: 42.5% of all losses, against the 43% estimate quoted before the instrument existed. The second-largest single cause is the bare 'does not' catch-all at 103 records, 18.3%. In total 562 records lose the tag and 142 gain it, netting the 1149 → 729 D-130 reports. Reproduce with npm run markers:coverage; per D-131, the 42.5% is the number that may be written down and the 0.5-point difference from the estimate is stated rather than absorbed. NOT DISPUTED: D-130's other two changes — singular-only negation, and the container-blind review test — are bug fixes as filed. ALSO CORRECTED HERE: docs/computed-grading.md said the corpus holds '12 meta-analyses and 91 replications'. Corpus-wide over all 4444 records in corpora/evidence/**, it is 374 meta-analyses and 493 replications. The old figures were scoped to a single corpus and read as corpus-wide, and the scope is now stated explicitly in the document, because the corrected numbers invite the opposite misreading: the corpus is not thin, the classifier simply does not tag the records that actually get cited — which is the consequence that section was making in the first place, and it survives the correction intact. NOTHING IS APPLIED. The retag is still not run, --apply is still not passed, and the categories on disk are unchanged. This entry changes what two changes are CALLED, so the owner session approves or rejects them as what they are.

decisions.title: Branch policy: main is the truth, one short-lived branch per review cycle, data-channel branches are named and exempted explicitly
decisions.body: TRIGGER: reconciling main to origin and merging validation/cl-14-realizations (22 commits: CL-14 effects, the expertise-based-guidance-toggle realization, extraction/grounding/gating hardening) surfaced four long-lived branches with no policy governing when a branch is created, when it is retired, or which ones are exempt from retirement. THE POLICY GOING FORWARD: (1) main is the single source of truth; nothing is considered done until it is on main. (2) Work happens on ONE short-lived branch per review cycle — a feature, a validation pass, a data-extraction run — merged into main with --no-ff so the review trail survives as a merge commit (a squash would destroy exactly the commit-by-commit review history this repo's CI and human review depend on). (3) A branch is deleted, both locally and on origin, the moment its content is verified merged (npm run validate, npm run build, and the relevant tests green on main) — a merged branch left lying around is not a safety net, it is a stale pointer someone will eventually merge from by mistake. (4) DATA-CHANNEL BRANCHES ARE THE ONE EXPLICIT EXEMPTION, and must be named as such in this log the moment they are created, not discovered later. ops-progress is one: per D-086, harvest.yml, extract.yml, and connectors.yml force-push a live run-progress heartbeat to refs/heads/ops-progress roughly every ~2 minutes so /ops can show in-flight jobs; it carries no review trail, is never merged into main, and must not be deleted or treated as a stale feature branch. VERIFIED AT THE TIME OF THIS ENTRY: feat/incremental-extraction-funnel was an ancestor of main (fully merged) and validation/cl-14-d103's tip was an ancestor of validation/cl-14-realizations (fully superseded) — both deleted, local and remote. validation/cl-14-realizations was deleted immediately after its merge commit was pushed to main and confirmed green (validate, build, all 11 test suites). ops-progress was left untouched and is exempted by this entry. Any future data-channel branch must get the same explicit exemption here before it is treated as anything other than a candidate for deletion.

decisions.title: Disable Vercel auto-deploy for the ops-progress data-channel branch
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: every ~2 min heartbeat force-push to refs/heads/ops-progress (D-086) triggers a Vercel Preview deployment. The branch is an orphan single-file tree with no package.json, so every build fails by construction and the failure mail buries real alerts. During the 2026-08-03 CL-14 evidence harvest window alone this produced 14 Error Preview deployments alongside 15 Ready Production deploys from harvest commits to main. D-086 correctly noted that the orphan tree carries no .github/workflows and therefore triggers no Actions CI, but it did not account for the Vercel GitHub integration, which deploys every pushed branch by default. DECISION: add a root vercel.json with git.deploymentEnabled.ops-progress = false, the documented project-configuration key (https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/git-configuration#git.deploymentenabled; type Object of branch identifier String → Boolean, unspecified branches remain true). This is scoped to the named data-channel branch only — main keeps auto-production deploys. Takes effect after the commit lands on the production branch and one production deploy picks up the new vercel.json.

decisions.title: /review becomes self-sufficient: inline source context, advisory triage flags, Accept/Narrow/Reject ergonomics
decisions.body: A proposal can now be judged without leaving /review. (1) INLINE SOURCE CONTEXT: for every evidence provenance item with a source_span, /review re-slices the stored corpus text at render time via lib/source-context.ts, verifies source_text_sha256 with the existing spanErrors check (D-110), and marks the span inline. Hash or offset failure surfaces as span_stale (or the matching span condition) instead of any text. Abstract-only records — the only shape this corpus produces under the rule-12 API whitelist — render the whole abstract labelled as such; a 600-char before/after window is retained for a future full-text record type. (2) ADVISORY TRIAGE FLAGS in lib/review-flags.ts — OVERREACH (fact clause with no lexical support in cited spans), DUPLICATE (realization trigger+action similarity against approved realizations for the same mechanism), WEAK ANCHOR (inferred pattern not identifiable in the referenced effect's fact). Flags are warnings only and never gate Accept; extraction and quality gating (D-079) are unchanged. (3) VERDICT ERGONOMICS: Accept / Narrow / Reject on the same screen, with Narrow and Reject requiring a reason that already lands in decision_note and decisions.json (D-113); keyboard shortcuts J/K navigate, A accept, N narrow, R reject; queue ordered flagged-first within the actionable bucket. No schemas, extraction, or approval-library gating changed.

decisions.title: DUPLICATE compares extracted trigger/action structure, not whole-record text; flag accuracy is measured against the source, never against past owner verdicts
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: D-138's DUPLICATE flag reused proposalSimilarity (D-079's whole-record Jaccard metric) and scored context-aware-tool-simplification against the already-approved expertise-based-guidance-toggle at 0.294 — just under the 0.3 bar — even though the owner had rejected that exact proposal as a duplicate of that exact record (decision_note on realization-cl-14-context-aware-tool-simplification-c403738e29d7: "Same trigger and same action ... A generator would read them as one rule with two surfaces"). ROOT CAUSE: the two records describe the same rule in different words ("wizard"/"guided walkthrough" vs "power-user interface"/"exploration mode"), and whole-text lexical overlap scores synonyms low by construction — no threshold fixes a metric measuring the wrong thing, and lowering the bar to 0.294 would also flag genuinely unrelated realizations that happen to share incidental vocabulary. DECISION, DUPLICATE: extract TRIGGER (the condition, split at the first of only after/once/after/when/if) and ACTION (the imperative change, everything before it) as separate fields from `pattern` (or `description_as_reported` when there is no pattern to split), strip {param} placeholders and spelled-out number words first (D-115's BARE_NUMBER precedent) so a declared tunable and an unparameterized prose number compare as the same trigger shape, score trigger-vs-trigger and action-vs-action independently with token overlap bridged by CONCEPT_GROUPS (extended with a new unguided_interface group: exploration/power/density/unguided — the replacement-surface half of a guidance removal, distinct from instructional_support which names what is being REMOVED), and aggregate as the MINIMUM of the two scores, matching the owner's own "same trigger and same action" standard rather than an aggregate blend. Re-run against all seven historical CL-14 proposals: context-aware-tool-simplification now scores 0.50 (trigger 50%, action 80%) against expertise-based-guidance-toggle and fires, and nothing that was quiet before (split-attention, expertise-reversal, modality, guidance-toggle itself) newly fires — progressive-disclosure-of-advanced-features still scores below the bar against guidance-toggle (shares no trigger/action concept group) and correctly stays quiet on DUPLICATE, catching WEAK ANCHOR instead as before. Threshold stays 0.3, unchanged, because the metric was wrong, not the number. DECISION, OVERREACH: re-running the same seven fixtures also surfaces cueing firing OVERREACH at ~47% clause coverage — cueing is APPROVED, so this looks like the same shape of miss as DUPLICATE, and it is NOT: the fact was owner-edited to a narrower claim ("raised retention scores ... but the same study reports only a weak cueing effect that does not easily generalise") than the model's first draft, and at that wording the first clause genuinely restates the cited span ("Adding visual cues to the pictures resulted in higher retention scores") more loosely than OVERREACH's 0.5 bar requires — the clause paraphrases "relate elements of a picture to the text" where the span says "to the pictures", a real gap in wording, not a scoring bug. Do not lower OVERREACH_SUPPORT_THRESHOLD or otherwise retune it to keep cueing quiet: flag accuracy is measured against whether today's words are supported by today's cited source text, never against whether a flag agrees with a verdict the owner reached before this instrumentation existed. Calibrating a source-facing check to match historical Accept/Reject outcomes would tune the machine to the owner's own past oversights instead of to the evidence, defeating the reason a second opinion exists. The misleading prior comment on OVERREACH_SUPPORT_THRESHOLD ("calibrated against the three approved CL-14 effects ... whose fact clauses all restate their own citations closely enough to clear it") is corrected in the same change — it was already false the day cueing was re-run.

decisions.title: Reader coverage re-keyed by (corpus, mode, effect): the D-112 ceiling on effect-anchored realization runs is lifted
decisions.body: PROBLEM, stated as a LIMIT at D-112 rather than fixed there: reader coverage (corpora/extraction/coverage.json) keys terminal reads by corpus and mode only, so an effect-anchored mode=realizations run (scope_kind="effect", D-112) marks every evidence record it reads as terminal for realizations on that mechanism — full stop, no matter which effect anchored the run. CL-14's first effect-anchored run (against cl-14-002) left 46 processed + 21 skipped_irrelevant records terminal for mode=realizations; a second effect on the same mechanism (e.g. cl14-cueing) would see all 67 as already read and could never select them, even though affinity-ranking against a different effect's keywords is a genuinely different question over the same literature. DECISION: ReaderCoverageModeState (lib/types.ts) gains an optional `by_effect: Record<effectId, {processed_record_ids, skipped_irrelevant_record_ids, processed_at}>`, populated only when a run is effect-anchored (mergeReaderCoverage takes an optional effectId, threaded from ExtractionScope.effectBasis.effect.id at both call sites in tools/extract.ts). buildExtractionPlan's terminal-set lookup switches to by_effect[effectId] when the run is effect-anchored, and to the existing mode-level fields otherwise — so a record terminal for one effect is NOT terminal for a different effect, lifting the ceiling exactly where D-112 said it existed. The mode-level `processed_record_ids`/`skipped_irrelevant_record_ids` fields are UNCHANGED in meaning: they remain the union across every effect and every non-effect-anchored run on that mode, so the existing aggregate (extraction_completeness, analyzer, tools/validate.ts's cross-checks) reads exactly as before — by_effect is a strict refinement recorded alongside the union, not a replacement for it. Schema version 1.1.0 → 1.2.0 (corpora/_ops/reader-coverage.schema.json gains by_effect on modeState; tools/validate.ts additionally checks each by_effect bucket for the same processed/skipped-disjointness and known-record-id invariants already enforced mode-wide, plus that by_effect ids are a subset of that mode's own aggregate). MIGRATION: CL-14's existing evidence.by_mode.realizations terminal set (46 processed + 21 skipped, written by the cl-14-002-anchored run) is copied into by_effect["cl-14-002"] in the live ledger; the mode-level aggregate is untouched. RE-READ COST, reported before anything runs: a second effect anchored on the same mechanism (e.g. cl14-cueing or cl-14-001) starts with an EMPTY by_effect bucket, so up to all 46 previously-processed records become eligible again for cheap+strong extraction if affinity-ranking selects them — each additional effect can pay to re-read literature a prior effect on the same mechanism already paid to read, bounded per run only by the existing limits.per_run_tokens (50,000) and the monthly caps (D-087/D-093). This is spend the ledger existed to prevent for the SAME question; it is now spent deliberately once per DIFFERENT question (effect), which is the trade the owner asked for. Effects-mode coverage (113 processed + 21 skipped for CL-14) is untouched — it has no effect dimension and is not re-keyed.

decisions.title: requiresSpanRole() answers for the wrong unit: span_role must be checked per provenance item's content, not per enclosing proposal's proposed_at
decisions.body: SYMPTOM: main failed npm run validate with 3 span_role_missing violations, all inside exactly two files — proposals/effect/effect-cl-14-expertise-reversal-effect-72a394e20f30.json (1) and proposals/effect/effect-cl-14-split-attention-effect-04b908b55654.json (2, one per roleless citation). Both are pending proposals from run extraction:github-actions-30806106326, proposed_at 2026-08-03T10:42:21.863Z — after SPAN_ROLE_REQUIRED_FROM (2026-07-31T12:00:00.000Z, D-129), so requiresSpanRole(proposal) said the whole proposal owed a role on every citation. DIAGNOSIS: these are not new gate violations. Both proposals are `operation: "enrich"` against effects already committed BEFORE D-129 — effects/CL-14/cl-14-001.json (2 provenance items, no span_role) and cl-14-002.json (1 item, no span_role). extract.ts's mergeProposals (the authoritative-duplicate path in the extraction loop) builds the enrich envelope by unioning the EXISTING record's provenance with the new candidate's, so the roleless items in both proposals are byte-for-byte the same corpus_record_id + quote_or_locus + source_span already sitting, roleless, in the committed effect — carried forward unchanged, not re-authored. Only the genuinely new citation in each proposal (cr_bb7a39186dd525334eb17f3f for expertise-reversal, cr_bb24fe2aef25808a289293aa for split-attention) is new pipeline output, and both of those correctly carry span_role: finding already. The bug is that requiresSpanRole's cutoff is a property of the PROPOSAL envelope (proposed_at is the enrichment run's timestamp), while "predates the gate" is a property of the ITEM (when that specific citation was actually authored) — an enrich proposal can be newer than D-129 while still legitimately carrying an item that is older than D-129, and the validator had no way to tell the two apart. VERIFIED before changing anything: both roleless items in each failing proposal are exact matches (same corpus_record_id, quote_or_locus, and source_span) to items already present in the corresponding effects/CL-14/*.json file on disk, confirming legacy-carry-forward rather than a fresh omission — the pipeline is not failing to attach roles to its own new output anywhere in this run. DECISION: tools/validate.ts now indexes every roleless evidence provenance item already committed in an authoritative effect/realization record, keyed by mechanism_id\u0000id, while it validates effects/**.json and realizations/**.json (recordLegacyRolelessSignatures, reusing the same corpus_record_id+quote_or_locus+source_span identity D-110's re-slicing already treats as the item's fingerprint). When a proposal's provenance item lacks span_role, the check that used to look only at the proposal-level roleRequired flag now also asks whether that exact item is already on record as legacy for that same target; if so it is counted in the existing rolelessFiles/legacy tally exactly like a pre-cutoff proposal, never failed. An item with no such match — new content the pipeline produced without a role — still fails precisely as D-129 requires, so the gate's actual purpose (no unrolled NEW citation) is unchanged; only its unit of judgement moved from the envelope to the citation. RESULT: npm run validate now reports 127 of 136 evidence provenance items carrying a span_role, 9 predating D-129 (up from a mixed pass/fail state, all 9 now correctly classified as legacy and none reported as violations) — OK, all data files valid. No schema, no extraction behavior, and no other gate changed; lib/span-role.ts (the extraction-time gate that attaches span_role to NEW citations) is untouched, because the defect was in how the after-the-fact validator attributed already-attached-or-not roles to carried-forward content, not in what the pipeline writes.

decisions.title: D-137 never worked: git.deploymentEnabled cannot reach an orphan branch, so vercel.json is widened to allow-list main and the Ignored Build Step dashboard setting is the actual fix for ops-progress
decisions.body: MEASURED, not assumed: D-137 (this same commit's ancestor, landed 2026-08-03T12:19:06+03:00) added git.deploymentEnabled.ops-progress = false to root vercel.json to stop Vercel building a Preview on every ~2-min heartbeat force-push to refs/heads/ops-progress (D-086). Querying the Vercel deployments API for this project afterward shows 35 ERROR deployments tagged githubCommitRef=ops-progress in the last 100 deployments, spanning 2026-07-31T12:10 to 2026-08-03T16:52 — i.e. still firing more than 4 hours AFTER D-137's fix was on production. The fix did not take effect, at all. ROOT CAUSE: Vercel reads git.deploymentEnabled from the vercel.json present ON THE COMMIT BEING PUSHED, not from the production branch's copy — documented behaviour confirmed against vercel/vercel#11176 ("the vercel.json file has to be present in the branch for it to work") and consistent with the shallow per-branch clone Vercel performs before evaluating build config. ops-progress is a single-file orphan tree by design (D-086/D-136: no shared history with main, carries run-progress.json only, exempted from the normal branch-merge policy) — it has no vercel.json, has never had one, and cannot inherit main's, so a key scoped to "ops-progress" in main's vercel.json is dead code. THIS ALSO EXPLAINS PROBLEM 2 in the same report: 20 of the last 100 deployments (all READY, i.e. real builds, not errors) are Preview builds off validation/effects-wide-sweep, one per data commit during the wide effects sweep across all 18 mechanisms — the wide sweep alone produced 18 useless Preview deployments before it even finished, because nothing in vercel.json restricted deploys to main; every branch defaulted to true per the documented schema (https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/git-configuration#git.deploymentenabled). FIX, SCOPED HONESTLY: (1) vercel.json's git.deploymentEnabled is widened from an ops-progress-only deny-list to an explicit allow-list — {"*": false, "main": true} — using the documented minimatch glob key and the documented multi-rule resolution (a branch matching multiple rules deploys if ANY rule is true, so main matches both "*" and "main" and the true wins). This is the correct schema for "disable preview deployments for all branches except main" and takes effect for any branch that shares history with main and carries this file at push time — i.e. every future validation/* branch cut from main after this commit, closing problem 2 going forward. It does NOT and CANNOT close problem 1: ops-progress will never carry this file, by construction, so no vercel.json edit can gate it. (2) THE ORPHAN-BRANCH GAP IS NOT CLOSABLE FROM THE REPO. It requires the dashboard's Ignored Build Step (Project Settings → Build and Deployment → Ignored Build Step), which Vercel evaluates as a project-level setting independent of the pushed branch's file tree — the built-in "Only build production" preset runs `if [ "$VERCEL_ENV" == "production" ]; then exit 1; else exit 0; fi` against the $VERCEL_ENV system environment variable Vercel itself injects, so it applies to ops-progress and any other branch with no build config at all. This is left for the owner to set by hand per the standing rule that dashboard/account-level changes outside the git-tracked write surface are not the app's or the agent's to make silently.

decisions.title: D-142's own allow-list didn't match either: minimatch's single-star does not cross a slash, so no validation/* branch name was ever matched by "*"
decisions.body: MEASURED, not assumed, immediately after D-142 shipped rather than trusted on the strength of matching the docs' example shape: pushed a same-content mirror of the new vercel.json ({"*": false, "main": true}) directly to validation/effects-wide-sweep (commit 87c2704), then pushed an empty test commit on top of that (189d35c) so a second push would definitely be evaluated against a vercel.json that already carried the fix. Both deployed READY per the Vercel deployments API — the allow-list did not stop either one. ROOT CAUSE, checked against the actual minimatch package rather than re-reading the doc's prose a third time: minimatch('validation/effects-wide-sweep', '*') is false. A bare `*` does not match across `/` by default; only `**` (globstar) does — minimatch('validation/effects-wide-sweep', '**') is true, and both minimatch('main','**') and minimatch('main','*') are true, so main is unaffected either way. Every branch name in this repo's actual convention (validation/effects-wide-sweep, validation/cl-14-realizations, validation/cl-14-d103) has a slash in it; D-142's "*" key matched none of them and silently fell through to the documented default of true — exactly the class of guess the task that produced D-142 was explicitly told not to make, and it was made anyway because the Vercel docs page shows only single-segment examples (dev, internal-*, experiment-*) and never states that the matcher stops at a path separator. FIX: git.deploymentEnabled's key changes from "*" to "**" in vercel.json on both main (commit 89a535b) and validation/effects-wide-sweep (commit be11279) — same allow-list shape D-142 already argued for, main matches both "**" and "main" so the true wins. VERIFIED, not just reasoned: pushed be11279 (the "**" fix itself) to validation/effects-wide-sweep and polled the Vercel deployments API twice, 25s and then 45s after the push — no deployment entry for that commit SHA exists at all (not READY, not ERROR, not CANCELED; git.deploymentEnabled=false suppresses deployment creation outright rather than creating and cancelling one), confirming the corrected glob actually stops the build rather than merely reasoning that it should. Same caveat as D-142 stands unchanged: ops-progress carries no vercel.json at all, so this glob correction does not touch problem 1 either way — that gap remains closable only from the Ignored Build Step dashboard setting, not yet applied as of this entry.

decisions.title: Ignored Build Step ("Only build production") set by the owner in the Vercel dashboard, verified against a real push to ops-progress
decisions.body: OWNER ACTION, not a repo change: the owner set Project Settings → Build and Deployment → Ignored Build Step → "Only build production" on the motivation-engine Vercel project, per D-142/D-143's finding that this is the only setting that can reach an orphan branch with no vercel.json. GET /v9/projects/{id} confirms commandForIgnoringBuildStep = `if [ "$VERCEL_ENV" == "production" ]; then exit 1; else exit 0; fi` is live on the project. VERIFIED against a real push, not just the API field: pushed a harmless one-file commit (d3230d8, .vercel-deploy-verification) directly to refs/heads/ops-progress — the same orphan branch D-086's heartbeat force-pushes every ~2 minutes — and inspected the resulting deployment (dpl_6X3QseN6Qwmzo9XnH8e4jmwV4LJg) via GET /v13/deployments/{id}. readyState is CANCELED, and createdAt, buildingAt, and ready are the SAME millisecond timestamp (1785768217349) — zero build time elapsed, confirming the deployment was stopped before any build step ran, not built and then failed. This is a different outcome than D-137 aimed for: Vercel still logs a deployment ROW for every push (git.deploymentEnabled cannot see this branch's file tree; Ignored Build Step runs after a deployment record already exists), but the row is CANCELED with no build and no errorMessage rather than ERROR from a build that ran and failed — which is the actual complaint from the original report ("every preview build fails by construction, one email every ~2 minutes"): a CANCELED-by-design row is not a build failure and is not the noise the report was about. PROBLEM 1 (ops-progress) is closed.
