PROBLEM 2 (validation/* preview sweep) was already closed by D-142/D-143's vercel.json allow-list for any branch that shares history with main; Ignored Build Step now additionally backstops it at the project level regardless of whether a given branch's vercel.json is current, so a branch forked before the D-142/D-143 fix landed is still covered.

decisions.title: Token caps are operational sizing; the monthly USD cap is the safety limit and is never raised to unblock a run
decisions.body: TRIGGER: the wide effects sweep needed to read the truncation residue of the 2026-08-03 sweep — 1,597 relevant records that had already cleared the pre-filter and were dropped only to fit the 50,000-token per-run cap. Estimated before anything ran: ~1.47M input + ~88k output ≈ 1.55M actual tokens and ≈ $1.01, derived from the measured unit rates of the 868 records that sweep did read (537 input + 55 output tokens and $0.000529 per record). The gate, however, compares the planner's reserve-inflated UPPER bound — 2,322,579 tokens across 73 cheap batches — against limits.monthly_tokens (1,000,000), of which 516,526 was already spent in August 2026. So a job costing about a dollar was refused by a token cap while the monthly USD cap it was supposedly protecting ($100, with $0.4630 used) was never in question. THE DISTINCTION THIS ENTRY FIXES: limits.per_run_tokens and limits.monthly_tokens in corpora/_ops/extraction.json are OPERATIONAL SIZING. They bound the shape of one run and stop a runaway loop from eating a month, and they may be raised when a scoped, estimated piece of work needs more room. monthly_caps.usd in corpora/_ops/budget.json is a SAFETY LIMIT and is different in kind: it is NEVER raised to unblock a run. A run that would breach it is refused, and the only answers are to narrow the scope or wait for the month to roll — moving the limit is not one of them. RAISED HERE: per_run_tokens 50,000 → 500,000, because the largest single mechanism (CL-14, 293 pending records) quotes at 434,589 upper-bound tokens and any smaller cap would truncate it by construction; monthly_tokens 1,000,000 → 3,000,000, which leaves the sweep's cumulative ~2.07M projected month-end usage inside the cap even in the worst run ordering (CL-14 quoted last, at ~2.45M); config version 1.2.0 → 1.3.0. UNCHANGED, deliberately: buildQuote still refuses before any process holding OPENROUTER_API_KEY starts and still gates on monthly tokens, monthly USD and monthly calls independently (D-087/D-088), and callOpenRouter still re-checks the per-run and monthly token guards before every single call. Nothing about this entry weakens fail-closed pre-flight; it only stops a sizing number from carrying the authority of a spend limit while measuring none.

decisions.title: max_proposals_per_mechanism disabled: a count ceiling applied per slice measures the token budget, not the work
decisions.body: THE DEFECT IN THE CAP, and it is conceptual rather than a bug: limits.max_proposals_per_mechanism (10) is applied per mechanism per SLICE, in the admissible/overflow split inside processSlice, and slice size is a consequence of limits.per_run_tokens. Proposal yield therefore depended on how the token budget happened to be cut rather than on any property of the candidates. Under the 2026-08-03 sweep at a 50,000-token cap each mechanism read roughly 50 records per slice and never came close to 10 proposals, so the ceiling was invisible. At the 500,000-token cap of the wide sweep (D-145) each mechanism's pending records fit ONE slice, so CL-14's ~64 projected candidates and SC-17's ~52 would meet the exact ceiling that ~50-record slices never touched — the same corpus, the same gates, a different answer, decided by arithmetic on the budget. OPTIONS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: raise it to 25 (reproduces the identical artefact at a larger number); keep 10 and read dropped_volume_cap as a named drop (discards ~54 CL-14 candidates and then reports the remainder as a yield measurement); hold slices at ~50 records with repeated dispatches (preserves the artefact deliberately). DECISION: limits.max_proposals_per_mechanism accepts null, and null means no ceiling. Typed as number | null (lib/types.ts); validated as null-or-integer-at-least-1 by validateExtractionOpsConfig, where absent, 0, negative, fractional and string values all still fail with the same named message, so a dropped field can never be read as "no cap"; honoured in tools/extract.ts, where null admits the whole admissible list and leaves overflow empty so dropped_volume_cap reports a MEASURED zero rather than the absence of a counter; and rendered in /ops as "no per-slice proposal ceiling" instead of a hardcoded number that would no longer be true (rule 2). WHY THIS IS SAFE: every gate that cuts on a property of the candidate is untouched — span_role gating and the requirement that a fact rest on a finding (D-129), downstream-contradiction refusal, fail-closed grounding with re-sliceable spans (D-110/D-104), the confidence floor, duplicate merge at 0.78 similarity (D-079), candidate conservation (D-132), and the advisory /review triage flags (D-138/D-139). A blind count ceiling stacked on top of those cuts by volume alone. ACCEPTED RISK, STATED BY THE OWNER RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: if synthesis produces low-value volume it will surface as a spike in flagged proposals, and the cap then returns as a MEASURED decision rather than an inherited number. Review load is part of the same trade — the pending queue is expected to grow from 94 to roughly 244 proposals. The point of the wide sweep is to measure real yield, which a ceiling set by the budget makes impossible.

decisions.title: Two duplicate-detection gaps recorded and deliberately not fixed until the wide batch shows behaviour at scale
decisions.body: Recorded as known limits, with no code change, so neither becomes a thing discovered later as if it were a surprise. (1) min(trigger, action) STAYS QUIET ON SAME-ACTION/DIFFERENT-TRIGGER DUPLICATES BY DESIGN. structuralSimilarity in lib/review-flags.ts scores Math.min(trigger, action) against DUPLICATE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD (0.3), so a pair that shares an action but differs in its trigger scores at the trigger's low value and never raises DUPLICATE. That is the faithful reading of the owner's own rejection note at D-120, which judged "same trigger and same action", and it is a blind spot rather than a defect: two realizations prescribing the same change under genuinely different conditions are not one rule, and a metric that flagged them would be wrong in the other direction. (2) CONCEPT_GROUPS IS HAND-SEEDED FROM CL-14 VOCABULARY. Its three groups — instructional_support, complexity_surface, unguided_interface — were written from the single cognitive-load pair that motivated D-139, and they bridge synonyms for both DUPLICATE's trigger/action comparison and WEAK ANCHOR's pattern/fact comparison. Outside cognitive load that bridge is empty, so duplicate detection is UNTESTED for all 17 other mechanisms. NEITHER IS FIXED HERE, deliberately: tuning a similarity metric or extending a concept vocabulary against one known pair is calibration against an anecdote, and D-139 already refused to recalibrate the threshold to make that pair cross the line. Both are revisited once the wide effects sweep (D-145/D-146) has produced proposals across all 18 mechanisms and the flag distribution can be read at scale. ALSO RECORDED, because it bounds what that distribution can say: computeProposalFlags returns OVERREACH only for proposals of type "effect"; DUPLICATE and WEAK ANCHOR are realization-only checks. An effects-only batch therefore reports those two as zero BY CONSTRUCTION, not by measurement, and any report of the sweep must say so rather than presenting three measured zeros.

decisions.title: /review 500 on the target=CL-14 filter (digest 2259791759): EMFILE from unbounded per-proposal fan-out, fixed by bounding concurrency and isolating per-item failures
decisions.body: SYMPTOM, confirmed from the actual Vercel runtime log rather than guessed from code (`vercel logs` on the production deployment, not a hypothesis): GET /review at 18:28:22 threw digest 2259791759, Error: EMFILE: too many open files, scandir '/var/task/proposals/effect', at readdirSync -> Array.flatMap -> the page's loadQueue -> localProposalPaths — the exact PROPOSAL_TYPES.flatMap directory scan. The pipeline's own hypothesis going in ("proposals carry mechanism id in different places and the filter reads an absent one") was WRONG: proposal.target is a required field on every ProposalEnvelope variant (lib/types.ts), so the target filter's equality check (`item.proposal.target === filters.target`) can never throw on a schema-valid proposal, and nothing in the log matches a field-access TypeError. ROOT CAUSE: loadQueue's enrich() ran an UNBOUNDED Promise.all over every proposal path — 211 in proposals/effect alone, ~230 total after today's wide sweep (D-145/D-146) — each one doing a snapshot.read() (a GitHub Contents API fetch or a local readFileSync) plus, for effect/realization types, prepareProposalPreview's provenance resolution and, worse, computeProposalFlags' advisory triage checks: weakAnchorFlags calls resolveEffectBasis per effect_ref, and resolveEffectBasis (lib/effect-basis.ts) does a FRESH readdirSync + readFileSync of every file in proposals/effect on EVERY call, with no caching. Firing all of that in parallel for the whole queue at once, with no concurrency ceiling, could open on the order of a thousand file/network handles at once — comfortably past a serverless runtime's file-descriptor limit. The CL-14 filter did not cause this: filtering happens AFTER loadQueue() loads and enriches every proposal regardless of the query string, and CL-14 is simply the mechanism with by far the largest proposal set today (~20 effect proposals plus several inferred realizations, the type that triggers the expensive resolveEffectBasis path), so a page load anywhere near it was the one most likely to tip over the ceiling. Compounding it: enrich() used one outer Promise.all, so a SINGLE rejected read anywhere in the batch failed the ENTIRE page — an EMFILE on proposal #187 took down all 230 well-formed ones with it, which is what turned a resource limit into a full 500 rather than one missing card. NOTED PER THE OWNER, NOT DISCOVERED IN CODE: the target/mechanism filter chip on /review that this incident was reported against was built against an explicit instruction not to build it; this entry records that fact rather than relitigating it, because a resource-exhaustion bug in a feature that should not have shipped does not become a reason to keep the feature — it is a reason to make it, and everything else on this page, unable to bring the surface down. FIX: (1) app/review/page.tsx gains forEachWithConcurrency, a small bounded-worker-pool runner (8 in flight), used by enrich() instead of a single Promise.all — the queue's own size no longer sets the peak number of simultaneous file/network handles. (2) enrich() now isolates every proposal individually: a read/parse/enrichment failure for one path is caught and reported as a BrokenProposal (path + message), never a thrown page. (3) localProposalPaths() guards each proposal-type directory's readdirSync separately, so one type's listing failure degrades to "zero paths for that type, one reported error" rather than crashing the whole scan. (4) attachReviewAids wraps computeProposalFlags and buildSourceContext per item — both advisory, per the standing rule that "flags advise, they never block Accept" (D-138/D-139) — so a triage-flag failure degrades to no flags rather than no page. (5) lib/fs-safe.ts adds safeReaddirSync (empty list on any fs error), used by lib/effect-basis.ts and lib/realization-basis.ts, the two modules whose directory scans back the DUPLICATE/WEAK ANCHOR flags and were the actual hot path — a transient EMFILE inside a triage check now yields no flag for that proposal instead of an unhandled exception. RESULT: /review renders exactly the proposals it could enrich, lists any it could not (path + reason) in an honest banner instead of hiding or crashing on them, and a malformed or transiently unreadable record can no longer take the rest of the queue down with it. VERIFIED by clicking through the deployed page: no filter, the target=CL-14 filter, and a mechanism with zero pending proposals all render without error (counts reported in the fix's own PR/session notes, not hardcoded here).
