decisions.title: MM-15 redundancy effects disconfirm each other — preserved, not reconciled (dissent record)
decisions.body:
The corpus's first self-disconfirmation, preserved rather than resolved, per rule 4 ("a corpus that cannot disconfirm is broken"). This entry is the dissent RECORD the owner asked for — no schema-sanctioned dissent artifact exists yet (dissent is a required field on the Dossier schema, dossiers/dossier.schema.json, and no MM-15 dossier has been built); this decision is the linking record until one does.

effects/MM-15/content-redundancy.json (D-302, approved from effect-mm-15-content-redundancy-7686ab66e7bd) states: content redundancy INCREASES learning outcomes and DECREASES cognitive load. Single source (10.1111/bjep.12592).

effects/MM-15/mm15-redundancy-effect.json (D-306, approved from effect-mm-15-redundancy-effect-c1c7ed537b36) states: modality-based redundancy (the classic simultaneous text+narration case) tends to DECREASE learning outcomes and INCREASE cognitive load. Seven sources, and the proposal's own citations do not agree with each other either: one reports no significant effect at all, one reports a REVERSED (beneficial) effect for foreign-language learners — the same direction as content-redundancy's finding — and one reports the effect is moderated by ADHD symptoms.

THE CONFLICT, stated plainly. Both proposals' own boundary text already distinguished "content" from "modal" redundancy as a way to keep them from contradicting each other. That distinction does not fully hold: one of redundancy-effect's own seven sources reports the SAME positive direction content-redundancy reports, for a different population (foreign-language learners) under what the source itself calls a "reverse redundancy effect." The corpus does not resolve whether redundant information, as a class, helps or hurts learning — direction depends on redundancy type and population in ways this evidence base does not cleanly separate.

WHY BOTH ARE KEPT, not merged, not one dropped. Rule 4 does not permit smoothing a disconfirmation into a synthesis the corpus itself does not support. Each proposal's boundary field now states the tension and cross-references the other's proposal id, so a reader who opens either effect sees the disagreement rather than a false consensus.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not decide which direction is correct — that would be resolving the dissent, which rule 4 forbids as a first move. It does not create a new artifact type; "dissent record" is represented here as a decision entry plus cross-referencing boundary text, the only structural facilities that exist pre-dossier. If MM-15 gets a dossier, its `dissent` field is where this belongs formally, and this decision is the source material for writing it.

decisions.title: Transferability never checks a lever against the mechanism's own forbidden-lever list
decisions.body:
Open defect, logged not fixed. effect-sc-17-native-ad-blindness-ae9ef1eb3142 (rejected NOT_TRANSFERABLE this batch, D-263) carried a v3-identified lever of 'reword or hide native-ad disclosure cues.' That lever directly instructs the thing SC-17's own hard rule forbids: registry/mechanisms/SC-17.json's constraints.hard_rules includes no_disguised_advertising (severity block) — 'Promotional or paid content must not be disguised as native content to bypass ad avoidance.'

The transferability filter (lib/transferability.ts) has no code path that reads a mechanism's constraints.hard_rules and checks a VARIABLE-identified lever against it. It judges only whether a lever is ACTIONABLE (does a product surface exist that could act on it), never whether acting on it is something the mechanism's own pack forbids. Confirmed by grep: constraints.hard_rules is read by lib/status.ts (registry-completeness check), tools/render-cards.ts and tools/render-packs.ts (rendering the pack's forbidden list from it), and tools/validate.ts (non-empty schema check) — never from lib/transferability.ts or the extraction pipeline that calls it.

This one was caught by the owner reading the review packet, not by the pipeline. A lever that violates a DIFFERENT mechanism's hard rule (not the one it was extracted under) would not be caught even by manual review unless the reader happened to check every pack's forbidden list against every lever by hand.

NOT FIXED HERE. A real fix needs a decision about scope: check a lever only against its OWN mechanism's hard_rules, or against every mechanism's (a lever proposed under one mechanism could still describe a dark pattern forbidden elsewhere) — and where the check should run (transferability, a separate triage flag alongside OVERREACH, or a pack-build-time check). That is a separate piece of work, deliberately not started by this entry.

decisions.title: Monthly token cap raised for the bounded realizations wave; USD cap untouched (D-145 precedent)
decisions.body: TRIGGER: the bounded first realizations wave (twelve owner-picked effects, LA-01/EN-03/SC-06/SP-08/ID-12/CL-14/MM-15, plus a second CL-14/MM-15 redundancy-effect pair per D-328, thirteen slices total) quoted at a measured wave upper bound of 2,100,987 tokens against 678,043 remaining under limits.monthly_tokens (3,000,000 cap, 2,321,957 already used in August 2026) — 3.10x the headroom, overflowing by 1,422,944 tokens. Every one of the thirteen quotes individually reports allowed:true and capped:false, because buildQuote gates one run at a time; only the SUM exceeds the cap, which no single quote can see. RAISED HERE, following the D-145 distinction: limits.monthly_tokens in corpora/_ops/extraction.json is OPERATIONAL SIZING and may be raised for a scoped, estimated piece of work, so it moves 3,000,000 -> 4,500,000 (config version 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0), leaving headroom for the full thirteen-slice wave (2,100,987 upper bound) plus existing August usage (2,321,957) inside the new cap with margin (4,423,944 of 4,500,000, 76,056 remaining) even in the worst case where every slice spends its full upper bound rather than the measured actuals four prior realizations runs showed (historically 40-70% of the quoted upper bound). monthly_caps.usd in corpora/_ops/budget.json is UNCHANGED and stays the safety limit: $100 cap, $2.1018705 used, $97.8981295 remaining measured before this entry; the wave's summed estimated_usd is $2.2202, leaving the USD cap nowhere near threatened either before or after this raise, and it is not touched by this entry regardless. NOT A FULL DISPATCH: this entry authorizes the sizing headroom for the wave; it is not itself an approval to run all thirteen slices. The owner scoped an initial probe of three slices only (mm15-modality-effect, sc-06-02, la-01-04) rather than all thirteen, reasoning that D-170 (a zero-yield run permanently burns its effect anchor coverage) makes each slice a one-shot draw, and three of the four realizations runs ever dispatched (all anchored on CL-14 effects) produced zero proposals — so the fixes behind those zeros (D-167 anchor-citation, D-171 parameter-schema) are unverified on any anchor outside CL-14, and staking all thirteen coverages on the assumption they generalise was judged premature.

decisions.title: Extraction accounting survives a lost commit race: a conflict-free per-run receipt, a retry, and a reconciler that folds it back into the cap
decisions.body:
THE LOSS, MEASURED. On 2026-08-11 three realizations runs were dispatched within seconds of each other onto extraction-anchor-and-accounting. Run 31480702995 (effect=la-01-04) called models, printed 'SPEND, MEASURED from the responses (completed): 6 call(s), 56,432 tokens in / 6,878 out, $0.070004', and then lost every one of its four artifacts: no manifest entry, no ledger entry, no coverage delta, and not even the rejected-candidates file it had already written (corpora/extraction/rejected/2026-08-11T10-08-13.201Z.json is absent from the tree). Confirmed by arithmetic rather than inference: the budget snapshot before this entry read $2.1018705 and after the other two runs landed read $2.3119525, a delta of exactly $0.2101 — the sum of the three SUCCESSFUL runs only. The $0.070004 was real money the monthly cap could never see.

THE CAUSE, AND WHY IT IS THE THIRD POSITION THIS BLOCKER HAS OCCUPIED. The always() accounting step ended in `git add corpora/extraction; git commit; git pull --rebase --autostash; git push` under `set -euo pipefail`. `git add corpora/extraction` stages coverage.json, ledger.json and manifest.json — three whole-file JSON documents that EVERY run rewrites end to end, so two concurrent runs are structurally guaranteed to conflict on all three. The rebase hit content conflicts in exactly those three files, exited 1, `set -e` killed the step, and every following success() step (validate, commit proposals) was skipped. The comment sitting directly above that rebase claimed it was the protection against precisely this race: 'rebase rather than fail, because losing the race must not lose the spend record.' It was not. A rebase resolves a fast-forward race; it cannot resolve a content conflict.

D-099 established that spend is recorded even when a run fails. D-168 moved that record AHEAD of validation, because validation was the thing blocking it, and stated the principle as 'is the money recorded is answered before was the run sound'. D-173 then found a fail-closed guard inside that step had inherited its always() condition, and fixed the predicate — but touched nothing in the git tail. So the blocker moved a third time: off validate (D-168), past the discard guard (D-173), and into the push itself, where no entry had ever looked. D-168's own logic holds only if the commit can actually land, which nothing checked.

THE FIX, IN THREE PARTS, because any one alone moves the loss instead of closing it.

(1) A CONFLICT-FREE RECEIPT. tools/spend-record.ts writes corpora/extraction/spend/<run-id>.json before the aggregates, named for the run's own start timestamp — the same key already used by manifest.run_history[].timestamp, ledger.runs[].run_id and rejected/<run-id>.json. The shape is borrowed wholesale from tools/rejected-candidates.ts (D-104/D-169): one file per run, no retention, so two runs can never touch the same path and this commit always rebases cleanly however many runs race. The workflow's accounting step is split accordingly — the receipt commits and pushes FIRST and alone; the conflict-prone aggregates follow best-effort, and a failure there is now survivable rather than fatal.

(2) BOUNDED RETRY on both git tails, three attempts with backoff, each aborting any in-progress rebase so the next attempt and the next step start clean. This is an optimization, not the correctness mechanism — it converts a transient fast-forward race into a success and does nothing for a content conflict, which is why (1) exists. Applied to the 'Commit reviewed proposals' step too: it carries the same three aggregates and had the identical defect at a second site, unremarked until now. Deliberately NOT added: a `git reset --hard` cleanup after a failed aggregate push, because if the receipt push had also failed its commit would still be local-only and the reset would destroy the one artifact the step exists to protect.

(3) THE RECONCILER, which is the load-bearing half. A receipt is conflict-free but CAP-INVISIBLE: lib/status.ts computeMonthlyRollup sums manifest run_history and nothing else, so a receipt that is never folded back moves the loss rather than closing it — the same 'spend the cap can never see' failure D-099, D-164 and D-166 each named in turn. tools/reconcile-spend.ts reads spend/*.json, finds any run_id absent from run_history, and writes a MATCHED PAIR: a manifest run entry and a ledger run entry keyed by the same run_id. Both or neither, because tools/validate.ts checks the two files in both directions (D-132) — a manifest run with no ledger entry fails as 'a run with no accounting is not a run that balanced', and an unbalanced ledger entry recorded as anything but broken fails too. It runs at the top of every extract job, BEFORE the budget gate reads the manifest, so the cap is computed against every measured dollar rather than only the ones whose commit happened to land. Default is report-only; --apply writes.

THE RECOVERED ENTRY. The lost run predates the receipt mechanism, so its receipt was rebuilt by hand from its Actions log and carries reconstructed_from naming that log — a field that exists so a reader can tell a rebuilt receipt from one a run wrote for itself, the same instinct as span_absent_reason (D-112) and CandidateLedgerRun.reconstruction (D-132). Precedent is D-166, which appended a probe's lost measured spend straight into run_history on the reasoning that D-131 governs ESTIMATES and this already happened; re-running to re-measure a number already known would not be a fix. Written: manifest status 'broken' (mandatory — validate fails an unbalanced run recorded as anything else), cost as measured, and a ledger entry with every stage NULL rather than zero, reconstruction {status: partial, reason}. Null because the run's own counters contradicted themselves — it reported candidates_strong 5 in its stats while its ledger equation read 'into_synthesis + expanded = 8 but consolidated + candidates_strong = 0' — and D-132 is explicit that writing a zero where a number was never established asserts something false.

NOT RECONSTRUCTED, DELIBERATELY: cost.models, the per-tier split, because the log printed totals only and a plausible apportionment is still an invented one; the stage counters, above; and the run's rejected-candidates file, which is simply gone. Each omission is a declared gap, not a silent one.

ONE THING THE FAILURE DID NOT BREAK, stated so it is not re-investigated: the lost run's coverage delta was never committed either, so la-01-04's by_effect bucket was NOT burned by it, and the successful retry burned it correctly. D-170's 'a zero-yield run still consumes an effect's entire reader coverage' did not compound here.

VERIFIED BY ARITHMETIC. After reconciliation the budget snapshot reads $2.3819565 — exactly $2.3119525 + $0.070004. That number is the proof the cap can finally see the money, and it is the only acceptable evidence that this entry did what it claims.

decisions.title: A dispatch evicted from the concurrency queue cannot report itself; the next run reports it
decisions.body:
OBSERVED. Three realizations dispatches were fired within seconds of each other on 2026-08-11. The first started; the second (effect=sc-06-02, dispatch realizations-probe-sc-06-02, GitHub run 31480696849) was CANCELLED seven seconds later without ever starting a job; the third ran. Nothing in the repository recorded that the second existed. It was noticed only because someone happened to be reading `gh run list` at that moment, and it cost nothing only because it was evicted before any model call — an eviction a few seconds later would have been invisible AND expensive.

THE MECHANISM. extract.yml serialises on `concurrency: {group: extraction, cancel-in-progress: false}`. That setting is usually read as 'never cancel anything', and that reading is wrong: it protects the RUNNING job, but GitHub holds only ONE pending entry per concurrency group. Dispatch a third run while a second is queued and the second is cancelled outright, with conclusion `cancelled` and an empty job list.

WHY THE RUN CANNOT REPORT ITSELF, which is the constraint that shapes the fix. A run cancelled while QUEUED never starts a job, so no step inside it ever executes — not `if: always()`, not `if: cancelled()`. There is no hook. Any design that proposes to have the superseded run announce its own death is wrong about how GitHub schedules, and would produce a fix that silently never fires. The report has to come from an observer, and the only observer guaranteed to run afterwards is the NEXT extraction.

THE FIX. tools/report-superseded.ts runs at the top of every extract job. It asks the API for cancelled extract.yml runs, and for each one counts jobs that ever started. A run is SUPERSEDED when conclusion is `cancelled` AND zero jobs started; a run a human cancelled mid-flight has started jobs and is deliberately excluded, because that was a decision rather than a silent eviction. That distinction is the whole point and is pinned by a test: both cases read `cancelled` in the UI, and reporting deliberate cancellations as losses would train the reader to ignore the warning.

For each superseded run it emits a ::warning:: annotation (visible on an otherwise green run), appends a row to the job summary, and writes corpora/extraction/superseded/<run-id>.json. The marker exists because the Actions UI ages out: a warning nobody reads within the retention window is the same as no warning. It uses the one-file-per-run shape D-342 established for spend receipts — unique path, so it can never lose a rebase — and rides the same conflict-free commit. Detection is idempotent: a run already carrying a marker is skipped, so the annotation fires once rather than on every subsequent extraction.

APPLIED TO THE RUN THAT PROMPTED IT. corpora/extraction/superseded/31480696849.json is committed with this entry, recovering the one dispatch this session lost.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. The group key was not made unique per dispatch. That would end the cancellation entirely — every dispatch would run — but it would also let concurrent runs write coverage.json, ledger.json and manifest.json simultaneously, which is exactly the race that lost $0.070004 in D-342. Trading a visible failure for a silent one is not a fix. Serialisation stays; only its invisibility is removed. Related and unchanged: transferability-probe.yml shares this group on purpose (D-164), and any future change to the key must account for that file too.

OPERATIONAL NOTE, earned the hard way: dispatches into this group must be issued one at a time, waiting for each to leave the queue. Firing a batch is not merely slower, it silently discards all but the first and last.

The check never fails a run. It is a reporting aid, and a reporting aid that can break an extraction would be a worse defect than the one it reports.

decisions.title: The hard-rule check gap recurs at measured scale: 4 of 11 realization proposals (36%) collided with their own mechanism's blocking rules, caught only by manual review
decisions.body:
THE ARITHMETIC. Of the 11 realization proposals produced by the 2026-08-11 bounded probe (D-330-D-341), 4 (36%) carried a pattern conflicting with their own anchoring mechanism's hard_rules — every one severity block — while the pipeline's own triage flags read clean across all 11: OVERREACH 0, DUPLICATE 0, WEAK ANCHOR 0. None of the four was caught by any automated check. All four were caught by owner review of the rendered proposal text, the same route that caught D-329's SC-17 case.

THE FOUR, NAMED, WITH THE RULE EACH TOUCHED:

1. view-count-triggered-text-suppression (MM-15). Original pattern hid 'redundant text captions' after repeated viewing. Captions are accessibility infrastructure, not redundancy — this collided with MM-15's accessibility_preserved ('comprehension gains for some users may not remove access for others'). Narrowed before approval to exclude any text serving an accessibility function (D-333).

2. narration-text-redundancy-toggle (MM-15). Original pattern hid on-screen text by DEFAULT whenever audio narration played. Removes the text channel for deaf and hard-of-hearing users by default — the same accessibility_preserved hazard, reached by a different route (default state rather than explicit user action). Narrowed for consistency with #1 (D-334).

3. repeated-view-scarcity-nudge (SC-06). Pattern instructed 'showing a limited-availability message where none was previously visible' — manufacturing a scarcity signal rather than reporting one, near-verbatim against no_manufactured_limits ('Do not artificially restrict availability solely to manufacture urgency where no real constraint exists') and genuine_scarcity_only. Its sole evidence item was a scam-warning persuasion study, so the transfer was wholly grounded in fraud-persuasion research rather than commerce research. Rejected outright, not narrowed — the pattern's mechanism was the violation, not an omission around its edges (D-332).

4. low-stock-indicator-badge (SC-06). The weakest of the four, worth stating precisely rather than folding into the other three: the ORIGINAL pattern did not instruct fabricating a count, but it also never stated the count had to be genuine — silent on exactly the dimension genuine_scarcity_only and no_fake_timers govern, in an artifact the generator reads with no other mechanism-level check available to it (D-112: the generator never reads the effect or the mechanism pack directly). One of its five evidence citations was to fraud-tactics research, dropped as non-load-bearing. A truthfulness clause was added explicitly, making the hard rule legible in the pattern text itself rather than assuming a downstream reader would supply it (D-335).

THE MECHANISM OF THE MISS, STATED PLAINLY. lib/transferability.ts, which judges every proposal admitted to this pipeline, reads a mechanism's applicability, evidence_terms and boundary lexicon — never constraints.hard_rules. Confirmed by grep across lib/ and tools/: hard_rules is read by lib/status.ts (a registry-completeness check, i.e. does the field exist and is it non-empty — not what it says), tools/render-cards.ts and tools/render-packs.ts (rendering the pack's forbidden list FROM it, downstream of extraction), tools/validate.ts (schema shape only), and tools/extract.ts (only when a run is DRAFTING a mechanism record, i.e. authoring hard_rules, never when checking a candidate against them). No code path anywhere in lib/transferability.ts, lib/proposals.ts, or lib/review-flags.ts reads a mechanism's own hard_rules and checks a proposed pattern against them. This is the identical gap D-329 named for SC-17's native-ad-blindness effect proposal — 'the transferability filter judges only whether a lever is ACTIONABLE, never whether acting on it is something the mechanism's own pack forbids' — now measured a second time, on a different record type (realization, not effect) and two different mechanisms (MM-15, SC-06), with a real rate attached: 4 of 11, 36%.

NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately, for the same reason D-329 stated: the scope question is unresolved. Check a lever/pattern only against its OWN anchoring mechanism's hard_rules, or against every mechanism's (a pattern proposed under one mechanism could still describe a pattern forbidden under another — MM-15's accessibility_preserved plausibly constrains ANY mechanism's realizations that touch text/imagery, not only MM-15's own)? And where should the check run: inside lib/transferability.ts's judgement, as a new triage flag alongside OVERREACH (D-138/D-139), or as a pack-build-time gate in tools/render-packs.ts, downstream of both effects and realizations? Each answer has a different blast radius and this entry does not choose one.

ONE RULE ADDED IN RESPONSE, NOT AS A FIX TO THIS GAP BUT BECAUSE IT SURFACED A SEPARATE ONE: LA-01 had no hard rule at all covering withholding a user's own data/results/artifacts as conversion pressure — the pattern behind proposal #3's rejection reasoning and, on inspection, an uncomfortably close description of LA-01's OWN existing implementation LA-01-trial-ownership ('shows what the user has CREATED (previews of their projects/results)'). no_data_hostage covers deletion; nothing covered withholding short of deletion. Recorded separately, not folded into this entry, because it is a missing RULE, not a missing CHECK — the pipeline gap this entry documents would exist even with every mechanism's rule set complete.

decisions.title: LA-01 gains no_withholding_pressure; the same gap checked and not (yet) fixed on the other 17 mechanisms
decisions.body:
TRIGGER. The 2026-08-11 rejection of session-threshold-performance-reveal (LA-01) cited LA-01's no_data_hostage as the nearest hard rule 'in spirit' rather than as a literal breach, because no_data_hostage governs DELETION under pressure and the proposal withheld the user's own performance summary behind a usage-session threshold — a different act with the same coercive shape. LA-01 had no rule naming that act at all.

ADDED. registry/mechanisms/LA-01.json constraints.hard_rules gains no_withholding_pressure, severity block: 'The user's own data, results, or created artifacts are never hidden, delayed, degraded or placed behind a threshold in order to create pressure to pay or act. Access to what the user made or earned is not a lever. This is distinct from no_data_hostage, which governs deletion.' constraints.boundary_test is updated to 'Is the user being shown less of their own work than they would be if we were not trying to convert them?', replacing the previous general boundary_test ('If the user learned exactly how this works, would they shrug — or feel deceived?'). The schema (registry/mechanism.schema.json) permits exactly one boundary_test string per mechanism, so this is a REPLACEMENT, not an addition — recorded plainly because the two questions test different things and only one now ships.

A CONFLICT SURFACED BY THIS ADDITION, NOT RESOLVED HERE. LA-01's own implementation LA-01-trial-ownership reads: 'The paywall shows what the user has CREATED (previews of their projects/results) and frames payment as keeping access to what is theirs.' 'Previews' of the user's own created results, gated behind payment, is a plausible instance of exactly what no_withholding_pressure now forbids. This is flagged, not fixed — mechanism.implementations is the product-authored directive layer (constitution: 'you never author science', and implementations are the one layer that is owner-authored by design, not extraction output), so editing it is an owner call, not a pipeline correction.

CHECKED ACROSS THE OTHER 17 MECHANISMS FOR THE SAME GAP, per instruction, none added. No other mechanism's hard_rules names withholding the user's OWN data/results/artifacts as pressure; the closest adjacent coverage, none of it equivalent: EN-03 honest_trial_scope ('If trial access is partial, do not imply full possession') requires honesty about a partial state but does not forbid creating it under pressure; ZE-07 real_headstart_only/no_manufactured_incompleteness govern fabricated progress, not withholding real accumulated progress; RE-10 no_unwanted_gifts_as_leverage governs forced trials that auto-bill, a different mechanism of coercion; IF-18 no_scent_suppression_for_exit_paths governs mislabelling an exit path, not withholding content. EN-03 and ZE-07 are the two where the mechanism's own subject matter (ownership; accumulated progress) makes this gap most plausible to matter in practice, ahead of the other 15.

decisions.title: copy_formulas no longer projects into packs — the single largest measured source of cross-product output homogeneity
decisions.body:
MEASURED FIRST. 55 copy_formulas strings exist across the registry, all inside mechanism.implementations, concentrated in 12 of 18 core mechanisms (six — CL-14, IF-18, MM-15, PF-16, PS-13, SC-17 — carry none). LA-01 carries the most (7, across 5 implementations), then EN-03 and ZE-07 (6 each, across 3 implementations apiece). The eight S8 _seed mechanisms (AE-26, AU-20, CO-19, DE-23, ER-22, FB-21, FL-24, RR-25) carry zero — they have no implementations at all, per the standing note in CLAUDE.md that they are owner-authored placeholders, never extraction output.

WHY THIS WAS A DEFECT, NOT A STYLE CHOICE. Constitution rule 1: 'Packs are evidence, not instructions... No directives, no copyable examples. The generator decides for itself.' A copy_formula is exactly a copyable example — a pre-written string ('Don't lose your {n}-day streak', 'Stop losing ${x} every month') that every generator reading the same pack receives verbatim and, absent a reason not to, reproduces verbatim. Projecting it was the single largest source of output homogeneity in the system: every product built from LA-01's paywall implementation was one edit away from shipping the identical sentence.

THE FIX IS ONE SEAM, NOT A CASCADE. tools/render-packs.ts buildImplementation() is the only place a registry Implementation record becomes a PackImplementation — the boundary between the owner-authored layer (rule 5: 'Packs are generated, never hand-written') and what a generator reads. copy_formulas is no longer spread through that function, and PackImplementation (lib/types.ts) drops the field entirely, so a future call site cannot silently reintroduce it by forgetting to omit it — there is nothing to omit. registry/mechanisms/*.json is UNCHANGED: copy_formulas remains on every Implementation record as owner reference, required by mechanism.schema.json exactly as before. Nothing about mechanism proposals, mechanism.schema.json, or the extraction prompt that asks a mechanism-drafting run to populate copy_formulas was touched — those govern the registry, not the projection.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM TO FIX. Removing the formulas removes one demonstrated source of homogeneity; generation_directive, which every implementation still carries into the pack, is imperative prose and could itself converge toward similar phrasing across generators reading the same directive. That is a different, unmeasured question and is not addressed here.

VERIFIED. All packs regenerated after the change; no pack's implementations block carries a copy_formulas key. npm run validate and the full test suite pass unchanged, since no schema or test asserted on the field in pack output (grep of tools/render-packs.test.ts returns no match).

decisions.title: Realization approval writes only realization -> effect; the reverse link (and the validator that should have caught it) never existed
decisions.body:
OBSERVED. la-01-04 showed realization_ids: [] while three approved realizations carried effect_id: la-01-04 pointing at it. The same held for mm15-modality-effect (3 missing) and sc-06-02 (4 missing) — 9 broken links across 3 effects from the same approval batch (D-336..D-341, D-333..D-335). Only cl-14-002 was correctly linked, and it was set by owner hand-edit (D-118/D-119), not by anything the approval pipeline did.

ROOT CAUSE. projectRealization (lib/proposals.ts) writes exactly one file: realizations/{mech}/{id}.json. Contrast projectEffect, which writes the effect AND updates registry/mechanisms/{id}.json.effect_refs, then re-validates. Nothing in projectRealization ever touched effects/{mech}/{effectId}.json.realization_ids. effect_refs on the realization always pointed the right direction; nothing ever wrote the other one.

WHY npm run validate NEVER CAUGHT THIS, which is the more important finding. tools/validate.ts's cross-check at the effect/realization boundary walks `effect.realization_ids` and, for each id found there, confirms the named realization links back via effect_refs — a real check, but structurally incapable of catching an EMPTY realization_ids array, because an empty array has nothing to iterate. The validator checked 'is everything listed consistent', never 'is everything that should be listed, listed'. It ran clean across this entire session, on every commit, while the defect sat present the whole time.

THE FIX, both halves. (1) projectRealization now writes the reverse link: for every effect_refs entry, it reads the effect, adds this realization's id to realization_ids (deduped, sorted), writes it back, and re-validates via validateMechanismReferences — the same pattern projectEffect already used for the mechanism side, applied here for the first time. (2) tools/validate.ts gains the missing direction: for every realization, for every effect_refs entry, the corresponding effect's realization_ids must list it back. Verified against the live defect before fixing it: the new check failed on exactly the 9 broken links, and only those. The 9 were then backfilled directly (effects/LA-01/la-01-04.json, effects/MM-15/mm15-modality-effect.json, effects/SC-06/sc-06-02.json), and validate now passes clean.

A regression test was added to lib/proposals.test.ts, extending the existing effect-then-realization approval fixture with an assertion that the effect record's realization_ids contains the newly approved realization's id after approval — so a future regression fails a unit test, not a silent gap noticed months later.

decisions.title: Realizations gain boundary_refs: effects to read a pattern against, distinct from effect_refs (which claims embodiment)
decisions.body:
TRIGGER. Low-Stock Indicator Badge (SC-06) states its pattern's purpose as triggering competitive anxiety and increasing perceived value, while the same pack also carries sc-06-03 (scarcity-induced aggression toward other shoppers) and scarcity-wellbeing-deterioration (scarcity communications harming psychological wellbeing) — two adjacent, harm-direction effects on the same mechanism. A generator reading only the realization would never see them; the caution lives in the mechanism pack's hard_rules, which the generator never reads (D-112).

WHY NOT effect_refs. That field is defined as 'first-class L2 effects this realization embodies' — a claim that the pattern IS an instance of the named effect, load-bearing enough that derivation=inferred requires an inference-provenance item resolving against each one. Putting sc-06-03 there would assert the pattern demonstrates aggression-inducing scarcity, which is false and would additionally fail approval (no inference item could resolve against it, since it isn't what the pattern transfers from).

THE FIX. realization.schema.json gains boundary_refs: an array of effect ids, same id pattern as effect_refs, but carrying no evidentiary claim and no inference-provenance requirement — a caution list, not a citation list. Threaded through lib/types.ts (Realization, PackImplementation's sibling PackRealization), lib/proposals.ts (projectRealization requires each entry resolve to an approved effect record, mirroring effect_refs' existence check exactly, without the inference check), tools/render-packs.ts (projected and rendered as a flow sequence next to pattern/parameters, not buried after artifact_context), and tools/validate.ts (the same existence check independently enforced against every committed record, matching the belt-and-suspenders pattern already used for effect_refs).

APPLIED. low-stock-indicator-badge now carries boundary_refs: [sc-06-03, scarcity-wellbeing-deterioration]. Its pattern also dropped the intent clause ('to trigger competitive anxiety and increase perceived value') per D-349 — the two changes are related but recorded separately, since one is a new field and the other is a text edit.

Test coverage added to tools/render-packs.test.ts: boundary_refs projects in full (unlike effect_refs, which projects only its first entry as effect_id — a boundary reference is a list a generator should see all of, not a claim needing one citation), is absent rather than emitted as undefined on a record that declares none, and round-trips through the pack's own re-parse self-check.

decisions.title: Low-Stock Indicator Badge states what to display, not what emotion to induce
decisions.body:
The pattern approved under D-335 read '...to trigger competitive anxiety and increase perceived value.' That is a statement of INTENT, not of behavior — it tells a generator what feeling to produce in the user rather than what interface state to render. No other realization approved this session carries an intent clause of this kind; every other pattern states a trigger and a display change only.

Stripped. The pattern now reads: 'Display a remaining-stock counter or badge on the product card or page when inventory falls below {stock_threshold} units, where the displayed count must reflect true remaining inventory at the moment it is shown.' Paired with D-348's boundary_refs addition (sc-06-03, scarcity-wellbeing-deterioration), so a generator reading this record sees the display instruction and the two effects it should be read against, and does not additionally receive a stated emotional target that description_as_reported's evidence never measured as a design goal — only as a described consequence.

decisions.title: Removing copy_formulas from pack projection (D-346) was cosmetic: the same sample sentences survived inside generation_directive
decisions.body:
MEASURED. Across 45 implementations in the registry, 15 generation_directive fields carried a quoted example sentence a generator would read and reproduce verbatim ('Don't lose your 12 days', 'Your {n} projects will be deleted in {d} days', 'Stop losing ${x}/month', 'Your gallery' / 'Your workspace', '90% success' not '10% failure', 'What do you want to build?', 'You're a founder', '2 slots left this week', 'X businesses use this' / 'trusted by 12,400 founders', 'most popular' / 'chosen by {segment}', 'your best week', 'account created check-mark', and others). Two more quoted a single UI word rather than a sentence ('theirs', 'was') -- same defect, smaller instance, fixed for consistency. One further directive (RE-10-value-first) named a specific real feature -- Ventora's free Idea Check report -- as the template to follow, which is the identical problem in a different shape: a concrete example standing in for the general condition. 18 of 45 directives (40%) touched in total.

WHY D-346 DID NOT CLOSE THIS. copy_formulas and generation_directive are separate fields carrying overlapping content -- the copy string removed from projection had, in nearly every affected case, ALSO been paraphrased or quoted directly inside the directive prose that WAS still projected. The generator reads the whole directive; stripping one field while the same sentence sat one field over changed nothing about what reached the generator.

THE FIX. Each affected generation_directive was rewritten to state the CONDITION (the trigger, the interface element, the constraint on truthfulness) with no sample sentence, no invented number, and no single named product standing in for the pattern. Every rewrite was verified against its exact prior text before being written (a script refused to proceed on any mismatch), so no directive was edited blind.

NOT CLAIMED FIXED: this closes the specific defect (a copyable sentence embedded in prose read by every generator). It does not evaluate whether the remaining directive language itself could still converge toward similar output across different generators reading the same prose -- a different, unmeasured question.

decisions.title: The instruction-voice collapse fired on a quoted word inside third-person policy prose, blanking a real hard rule to bare "forbidden"
decisions.body:
OBSERVED. EN-03's real_ownership_only rendered in pack-paywall-conversion.yaml's hard_boundaries block as `- real-ownership-only: forbidden` — no rule text at all, the only entry in that block with an empty body. Every sibling entry carried its full rule.

CAUSE. tools/render-packs.ts boundaryReason() collapses a hard rule to bare 'forbidden' whenever its text matches VOICE_TOKENS (/\b(?:you|your|should|prefer)\b/i) — correct behavior for a rule actually written in second person. real_ownership_only's stored text is third-person policy prose throughout: "Ownership language must reflect something the user actually created, customized, or possesses; do not fabricate 'your' where nothing was invested" — but it MENTIONS the word 'your', in quotes, as the example of the fabricated copy it forbids. The regex has no concept of a quoted span; it matched the word regardless of the quote marks around it.

SCOPE, MEASURED. Grepped every hard_rules[].rule across all 18 core mechanisms for the same token pattern: this is the ONLY occurrence in the entire registry. Not a systemic defect, a single false positive — but one that silently deleted real content from a document the owner explicitly said they were reading closely for the first time.

THE FIX. boundaryReason() now strips quoted spans (single- or double-quoted) before testing for voice tokens, so a rule can legitimately reference the pattern it forbids in quotation without being misread as using that pattern itself. Scoped narrowly: this only affects the collapse decision inside boundaryReason, not the separate whole-file voiceViolations scanner (a different, advisory-only function) — regenerating packs after this fix still emits one instruction-voice WARNING on this same line, because the word 'your' is still literally present in the rendered text and that scanner has no equivalent quote-awareness. That warning is non-blocking and was left as-is: fixing it was not requested, and the rule text itself is correct — the warning is a false positive in a diagnostic, not a defect in the data.

decisions.title: The realizations prompt said where the domain lives but never that it must not survive into the pattern; fixed with an abstraction rule plus a warning-only check
decisions.body:
OBSERVED. Every inferred realization LA-01 produced while anchored on la-01-04 (Myopic Loss Aversion) came back worded in the anchor's own industry. bias-awareness-tooltip: "whenever the displayed portfolio volatility metric exceeds {volatility_threshold} percent". periodic-performance-digest: "Replace frequent, granular portfolio performance notifications with a single periodic digest". The rejected session-threshold-performance-reveal: "Withhold the aggregated portfolio performance summary behind a placeholder". A ceramics shop cannot apply any of the three. That is a failed transfer, not a specific pattern.

CAUSE. inferredRealizationInstruction in tools/extract.ts stated the split correctly but in one direction only: description_as_reported stays in the source's domain, pattern is the product-UI directive. It never said the domain must NOT survive into pattern. Meanwhile anchorBlock hands the model the effect's fact and boundary verbatim, as the most quotable text in the context. Told where the domain belongs and shown the domain in full, the model kept it in both fields. The domain is already recorded structurally in source_domain and domain_transfer, so carrying it into pattern is duplication that costs the pattern its generality.

THE PROMPT FIX. Two additions. The pattern bullet now carries the requirement: state it in domain-neutral product terms; the anchored claim's vocabulary -- its industry, its measured setting, its subject matter -- must not appear in that text. A new THE ABSTRACTION RULE block gives the model the operation that satisfies it: replace every object the anchored claim names with its functional role in an interface ("portfolio performance notifications" becomes "outcome or performance updates the user did not request"; "volatility metric" becomes "a displayed metric with high variance"), and test the result by asking whether a ceramics shop's checkout could apply it as written. synthesisInstruction re-uses taskInstruction and so inherits both, which matters because synthesis composes the final patterns.

THE CHECK, AND WHY IT IS A WARNING. lib/review-flags.ts gains pattern_carries_anchor_domain: an inferred realization's pattern is tokenized, {placeholders} stripped, folded to singular, and intersected with the tokens of its anchor effect's fact and boundary, minus stopwords, minus generic interface vocabulary. A non-empty intersection raises a flag naming the exact shared terms. Warning severity by owner instruction -- the rate is to be measured before deciding whether it should block. It is the exact complement of WEAK ANCHOR: that check asks whether the pattern kept ENOUGH of the anchor, this one asks whether it kept the WRONG part.

SINGULARISATION IS LOAD-BEARING. la-01-04's fact says "portfolios"; every pattern it produced says "portfolio". A raw token intersection misses the exact leak the check exists to catch. Both sides are folded to singular before comparison, and the new lib/review-flags.test.ts pins that case against the three real committed patterns rather than a paraphrase of them, plus a domain-neutral rewrite that must stay clean -- a check that flagged everything would report a rate and teach nothing.

CONSTRUCT VOCABULARY IS DELIBERATELY NOT EXEMPT. A pattern that says "loss aversion" is flagged like one that says "portfolio". The owner chose the literal reading of the rule: a term drawn from the anchor that is not generic, and a construct name is not generic. Exempting it would need a second hand-curated list beside the generic-UI one, and would also hide a pattern that merely restates the effect, which the prompt separately forbids. The flag names every term it counted, so construct-versus-industry stays visible to the reader rather than being decided by the code.

BASELINE, MEASURED BEFORE ANY RUN. Run over the committed corpus: 7 of 10 approved inferred realizations carry anchor domain (70%), and 15 of 22 realization proposals across all statuses (68%). Spread across four mechanisms, not one: LA-01 (portfolio, loss, aversion, risk, taking), SC-06 (scarcity, quantity, limited, anxiety, perceived, competitive), MM-15 (audio, modality, instructional), CL-14 (attention, split, procedure, integrated, advanced). The leak was never an LA-01 problem; la-01-04 is only where it was noticed.

ONE FALSE POSITIVE FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY GUESS. The first pass flagged four CL-14/MM-15 proposals on the shared discourse word "rather" ("X rather than Y" occurs in both anchor and pattern). A FUNCTION_WORDS set was added, kept separate from GENERIC_UI_TERMS because these are not interface vocabulary, and separate from span-role's OVERLAP_STOPWORDS because that list belongs to downstream-contradiction scoring and must not be retuned to suit a different check. That removed two proposals from the flagged set: 17 of 22 became 15 of 22. Both word lists are hand-maintained and documented as such, on the same terms as CONCEPT_GROUPS.

la-01-04 COULD NOT CARRY THE MEASUREMENT RUN. Its by_effect bucket holds 119 processed + 23 skipped = 142 of LA-01's 142 evidence records; the anchor is fully burned, and a quote returns selected 0 at $0. Per D-170 that is the one-shot draw, not an exhausted corpus, and re-opening it would mean mutating a committed coverage record. Coverage is keyed per-effect (D-140), so the owner selected la-01-02 (Loss aversion in airline revenue; boundary "Airline revenue management") -- same mechanism, same 142-record pool, unburned, and the domain-heaviest anchor available. Anchor and prompt both change between the two runs, so this is NOT a controlled A/B: it measures whether the abstraction rule holds against a domain-heavy anchor of the same mechanism, and any report of its result must say so.
